entry.title: OperAItor: An Agentic Framework for Fault-Tolerant Operation of Chemical Processes

author.name: Javal Vyas, Mehmet Mercang{\"o}z

entry.summary: OperAItor is an open-source framework for building and evaluating LLM agents that handle supervisory fault management in chemical processes, demonstrated on a dynamic reactor-distillation plant with 113 variables, 8 PI control loops, 22 alarms, and 11 safety instrumented functions. The agent integrates multivariate statistical process monitoring with LLM reasoning. It provides a realistic, reproducible testbed for agentic control in safety-critical industrial settings.

entry.title: Four Extensions of the Universal Law of Robustness: Log-Concave Covariates, Heterogeneous Mixtures, Vector-Valued Predictors, and Markovian Data

author.name: Tobias J. Peter (ZHAW Zurich University of Applied Sciences)

entry.summary: This theory paper extends Bubeck and Sellke's universal law of robustness—relating overparameterization and Lipschitz constants for fitting noisy data—by relaxing its Gaussian, homogeneous, scalar-output, and independence assumptions. It covers log-concave covariates, mixtures, vector-valued predictors, and Markovian samples.

entry.title: When Latent Dynamics Meet Data Assimilation: A Benchmark of Koopman-Type Representations

author.name: Zhiwei Zhang, Wenxuan Yuan, Xiaoyuan Cheng, Pouria Behnoudfar, Chuanqi Chen, Charlotte Moser, Yuta Tarumi, Jin-Long Wu, Rossella Arcucci, Takemasa Miyoshi, Nan Chen, Marc Bocquet, Sibo Cheng

entry.summary: This benchmark systematically compares seven Koopman-type latent representations and structural baselines for deep latent data assimilation across five dynamical systems ranging from periodic to strongly chaotic, evaluating forecast and assimilation accuracy, physical recovery, and dynamical consistency. It reveals trade-offs between latent simplicity and downstream assimilation performance and examines Gaussian error assumptions and analysis uniqueness.

entry.title: Finite-Sample Convergence in Networked Average Reward MARL: Decentralization Pitfalls and Entropy Remedies

author.name: Yizhou Zhang, Yashaswini Murthy, Laixi Shi, Adam Vierman

entry.summary: The paper studies average-reward multi-agent RL on networks where agents update using only k-hop neighborhood information, proving impossibility results for converging to globally optimal joint policies due to multiagency and partial observability. It then proposes entropy-based remedies that enable finite-sample convergence guarantees for decentralized networked MARL.

entry.title: LoopKV: Loop-Aware KV Cache Compression for Serving Looped Transformers

author.name: Tianle Zhou, Yang Zhang, Tianyu Wu, Zhuohan Wang, William Nixon, Juncheng Yang

entry.summary: LoopKV introduces sensitivity-aware KV cache compression for looped transformers like Ouro, which keep a separate cache per loop iteration and thus face memory bottlenecks that limit batch size. Measurements show quantization and sharing sensitivity vary across loop-layer cells, and the method allocates precision accordingly rather than using uniform-bit or fixed per-loop rules. This improves serving throughput for parameter-efficient recurring architectures.

entry.title: Policy Network Diffusion

author.name: Jiate Liu, Deheng Ye

entry.summary: The authors propose DPPG, a task-conditioned diffusion model with a Transformer-based parameter autoencoder that generates reinforcement learning policy network parameters conditioned on different environments. Experiments show a single unified generator producing policies that generalize across tasks.

entry.title: ZEMA: confidence-calibrated signed descent with only one state

author.name: Ali Dadsetan, Domenic Rosati, Frank Rudzicz

entry.summary: Building on the view of Adam as uncertainty-modulated sign descent, ZEMA computes a per-coordinate z-score from per-example gradients, converts it to a sign probability, and smooths with a single exponential moving average, halving optimizer state versus Adam. The probability is formed before smoothing, and per-example variance can be estimated from a small gradient sample. This has clear appeal for memory-constrained LLM training where optimizer state is a major cost.

entry.title: DRAP: Dynamics-Risk Adaptive Plasticity for Continual Learning in Physical AI

author.name: Oswaldo Ludwig

entry.summary: DRAP is a replay-free continual learning method for physical AI that weights sample-level action gradients by a Lyapunov-inspired, policy-independent estimate of trajectory amplification risk, derived from the largest singular value of a local linear model fit to expert transitions. This targets the compounding-error structure of closed-loop control that distinguishes continual learning in embodied agents from standard settings. The risk-aware plasticity could prevent small per-step policy errors from cascading into task failure.

entry.title: Provably Learning Mixtures of Linear Experts

author.name: Adrian Candocia, Aamod Varma, Mark Davenport

entry.summary: This work gives the first global convergence guarantee, to the authors' knowledge, for jointly training the gate and experts of a gated mixture-of-experts model with linear experts and Gaussian-cluster gates using gradient EM. With logarithmic overparameterization, it converges from random initialization to arbitrary accuracy despite the nonconvex objective.

entry.title: Do We Still Need Rotation-Invariant Architectures? A Statistical Robustness Benchmark for Point Cloud Classification

author.name: Abdulla Nasir Chowdhury, Gulpi Qorik Oktagalu Pratamasunu, Kazuhiro Fukui

entry.summary: This benchmark evaluates 10 point cloud architectures across 5 domains under pose, noise, and occlusion perturbations, using confirmatory hypothesis tests rather than point estimates. It finds rotation-invariant architectures trade noise robustness for pose robustness, and shows a simple invariance loss with training-set rotations can recover robustness, questioning the need for built-in invariance.

entry.title: Spin Spherical Fourier Neural Operators: Efficient Equivariant Learning for Vector and Spin Fields on the Sphere

author.name: Kevin Mulder, Matthew A. Price, Eirini Leftaki, Jason D. McEwen

entry.summary: The authors extend spherical Fourier neural operators to spin fields (e.g., wind, CMB polarization, weak lensing shear) via lifted spherical convolutions that are exactly rotationally equivariant. Computation is made exact and efficient through harmonic representations and sampling theorems on the sphere and rotation group.

entry.title: SWAP-INR: Implicit Neural Representation with Switchable Attention Paths for Time-varying Multivariate Scientific Data Compression

author.name: Hyunsoo Son, Jeonghyun Noh, Chaoli Wang, Won-Ki Jeong

entry.summary: SWAP-INR is an implicit neural representation architecture for high-fidelity lossy compression of massive multivariate, time-varying scientific simulation data. It adds a switchable attention path module to explicitly model cross-variable interactions and adapt to the diverse spectral characteristics of different physical variables, addressing key weaknesses of prior INR compressors in HPC settings.

entry.title: When Self-Verification Hurts: Calibrated Answer Repair for Financial Question Answering

author.name: Celine Guo, Weida Liang, Yujian Fu, Anqi Dang, Yanzheng Jin, Kenji Kawaguchi, Wenya Wang

entry.summary: The paper shows that open-ended self-verification can damage correct content or reinforce errors in financial question answering, and proposes Calibrated Answer Repair (CAR), which first estimates whether a draft will benefit from repair, then performs a targeted check with localized evidence and constrained edits. It formulates repair as an explicit trade-off between recovered and damaged information.

entry.title: Do Pretrained Backbones Transfer to Physical Sensors? A Systematic Study of Multimodal Initialization Across the Sensor Stack

author.name: Fabio Montello, Ronja G\"uldenring, Lucas Mogensen Sandby, Christoffer Koo {\O}hrstr{\o}m, Lazaros Nalpantidis

entry.summary: A systematic study of whether pretrained backbones transfer to multi-sensor setups with real physical sensors, curating a 2.82M-image multi-sensor autonomous driving collection. It examines which pretrained weights transfer best and whether in-domain masked-autoencoding pretraining can beat off-the-shelf solutions under modality sparsity.

entry.title: Learning from Unlabeled Photographs for General Oral Image Analysis

author.name: Zhong-Shi Zhang, Zi-Li Yu, Xiao Xiao, Huan Liu, Gui-Song Xia, Cui Huang, Meng-Xun Li

entry.summary: Develops DOVE, a domain-adaptive self-supervised visual encoder pretrained on roughly 530,000 unlabeled oral photographs, and shows transferable representations across 5 classification and 4 segmentation dental tasks versus established baselines. Reduces dependence on costly expert annotation in oral healthcare AI.

entry.title: Manifold Embedding of Deep Image Features for Image Matching via Neural Adjoint Maps

author.name: Nafie El Amrani, Moritz Heep, Florian Bernard

entry.summary: The paper improves semantic correspondence between object instances by combining foundation-model features with the functional maps framework from 3D shape matching, using neural adjoint maps to impose spectral regularization. This regularizes otherwise noisy nearest-neighbour matching on foundation features, particularly for dense correspondences.

entry.title: Anchored Rank-Adversarial Fine-Tuning Pretrained Visual Place Recognition Models

author.name: Mostafa Kira, Bader Rasheed, Manuel Mazzara

entry.summary: Shows that foundation-model visual place recognition systems like SuperVLAD and BoQ collapse under imperceptible white-box ranking attacks (near-zero top-1 recall at a 1/255 budget), and proposes ARAFT, a fine-tuning method using a listwise rank loss with an anchor to the frozen pretrained model's clean descriptors. Checkpoint selection is governed by a pre-set clean-accuracy budget, with full robustness-accuracy trade-offs reported.

entry.title: ActOR: Ambient AI-Based Agentic Orchestration for Humanoid Autonomy in Operating Rooms

author.name: Han Zhang, Sicheng Lu, Aleks Santari, Jeffrey K. Jopling, Masaru Ishii, Mathias Unberath

entry.summary: ActOR couples wall-mounted ambient cameras with a humanoid robot's head-mounted camera into a shared object-level digital twin, with an LLM agent planning over this fused representation to enable humanoid autonomy in operating rooms. Ambient perception addresses the limitation of partial onboard observations that makes de novo robot orientation and planning in ORs cumbersome.

entry.title: te-comp: A Complete MLIR Compiler Generating Self-Contained C Inference Engines for MCUs

author.name: Van Chan Ngo

entry.summary: te-comp is an MLIR-based compiler that takes standard model formats (.tflite, .safetensors) and emits fully self-contained, dependency-free C source code for microcontroller deployment, including kernels, weight arrays, memory layout, and RTOS integration. This eliminates interpreter dispatch overhead and framework dependencies that plague existing tinyML deployment paths.

entry.title: Functional-Group Knowledge Is Structured in Language Models Before It Is Spoken

author.name: Tran Nhat Khang Nguyen, Anh Nguyen, Obed Issakah, Janghoon Ock

entry.summary: This mechanistic interpretability study reads internal representations of five open-source models on prompts covering 92 molecules and 20 functional groups to determine whether chemistry failures reflect recognition failures or output failures. Even without chemistry training, models internally organize functional-group structure before they express it in output.

entry.title: A Guideline-Grounded Multi-Agent Framework for Personalized Exercise Prescription from Clinical and Wearable Data

author.name: Xintong Li (Center for Data Science, Nell Hodgson Woodruff School of Nursing, Emory University, Department of Computer Science, Emory University), Yufen Lin (Nell Hodgson Woodruff School of Nursing, Emory University, Cancer Prevention and Control Research Program, Winship Cancer Institute, Emory University), Yuhua Wu (Center for Data Science, Nell Hodgson Woodruff School of Nursing, Emory University), Fengran Wang (Center for Data Science, Nell Hodgson Woodruff School of Nursing, Emory University), Minxiao Wang (Center for Data Science, Nell Hodgson Woodruff School of Nursing, Emory University), Rebecca A. Gary (Nell Hodgson Woodruff School of Nursing, Emory University), Jacob Kariuki (Lillian Carter Center for Global Health and Social Responsibility, Nell Hodgson Woodruff School of Nursing, Emory University), James Smith (Lancaster Medical School, Lancaster University), Sandra A. Billinger (Department of Neurology, University of Kansas Medical Center), Canhua Xiao (Nell Hodgson Woodruff School of Nursing, Emory University), Xiao Hu (Center for Data Science, Nell Hodgson Woodruff School of Nursing, Emory University, Department of Computer Science, Emory University, Wallace H. Coulter Department of Biomedical Engineering, Georgia Institute of Technology and Emory University), Runze Yan (Center for Data Science, Nell Hodgson Woodruff School of Nursing, Emory University)

entry.summary: FITTER is a multi-agent framework that integrates clinical and wearable data with condition-specific guidance to generate personalized FITT-VP exercise prescriptions, including deterministic safety audit and repair for rule-checkable violations. Evaluated on 400 All of Us participants (300 cancer, 100 stroke) against five LLM comparators with clinician review.

entry.title: Query-based Submodular Data Selection for Efficient Instruction Tuning

author.name: Zhenghao Zhao, Yasutomo Kawanishi, Huihuo Zheng, Michael E. Papka, Yan Yan

entry.summary: QSGS formulates targeted instruction-tuning data selection with query-based submodular functions and gradient-guided synthesis, capturing inter-example interactions that point-wise top-k ranking ignores, particularly near-redundant examples at tight budgets. This improves data efficiency for specialized fine-tuning, where subset quality dominates quantity.

entry.title: Clocks all the way down: does sequence-processing AI need endogenous temporal structure?

author.name: Meysam Hashemi, Alireza Valizadeh, Viktor Jirsa

entry.summary: This position/theory paper asks whether sequence-processing AI like transformers lacks a computationally important ingredient present in brains: endogenous, internally generated temporal structure such as rhythmic oscillations. Drawing on four lines of evidence including phase-dependent routing, delay-structured representation, and cross-frequency multiplexing, the authors argue this difference may be genuinely computational rather than merely implementational. It motivates architectures with internally evolving temporal references as a possible path beyond input-driven computation.

entry.title: Patching the Protocol: A Taxonomy of Pre-Registration Repairs in LLM-Proposer Experiments

author.name: Peter Chen, Ni Zhang, Siyuan Zhang

entry.summary: Studies how pre-registered protocols in LLM-proposer experiments must be repaired when software implementations contain defects, proposing a taxonomy of protocol patches from three case studies across scheduling, incentive design, and task assignment. Crucially, the reported repairs did not alter judgment criteria, thresholds, scoring rules, or collected data. It contributes to methodology for trustworthy automated research involving LLM-generated content.

entry.title: Spatial Memory for AR Glasses: Hierarchical Visual Acquisition and Source-Linked Recall

author.name: Tianxing Zhu, Dan Huang

entry.summary: Presents a dual-camera spatial-memory prototype for optical see-through AR glasses that selectively captures detailed RGB observations based on quality screening, appearance novelty, and temporal support, while retaining links between semantic observations and source images for grounded retrieval of past encounters. The architecture separates capture acceptance, interpretation, and question support, with bounded reassessment control mechanisms. Relevant to always-on wearable AI where memory bandwidth and battery are tight.

entry.title: JHiMA-WebRL: A Joint Hierarchical Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Framework for Long-Horizon Web Tasks

author.name: Shanka Subhra Mondal, Jiayun Wang

entry.summary: JHiMA-WebRL explicitly separates planning and execution in multimodal web agents and jointly trains the planner with the actor using hierarchical multi-agent reinforcement learning. The paper argues this provides a stronger inductive bias for long-horizon web navigation than monolithic policies or modular systems with a frozen planner.

entry.title: Physics-Informed Functional Tucker Method with RKHS Factors for Sparse Spatiotemporal Reconstruction

author.name: Zhengyang Liu, Jianguo Huang, Junxi Hu, Yucheng Mi, Haojie Cai, Wenxuan Shen, Zhikun Zhang, Renfeng Peng, Guangtao Zhang, Zhiqiang Liu

entry.summary: PhysFTM reconstructs physical dynamics from sparse sensors and missing frames by parameterizing Tucker mode factors in reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces and enforcing PDE constraints via finite-difference residuals at off-sensor collocation points. This adds physical supervision in unobserved regions, addressing the ill-posedness of sparse spatiotemporal inverse problems.

entry.title: Rethinking Next-Visit Diagnosis Prediction Beyond Aggregate Metrics: Retrieval--Memory Multi-Agent Adjudication

author.name: Heejoon Koo

entry.summary: This paper critiques standard aggregate evaluation of next-visit diagnosis prediction from electronic health records, proposing a multidimensional evaluation framework that separates distributional challenges (variable-size diagnosis sets, long-tailed labels) from temporal ones (persistent, new, and recurrent diagnoses). Applying this framework to rule-based heuristics, LLM prompting, retrieval, memory, and multi-agent methods reveals that a simple last-visit repeat baseline outperforms most LLM-based approaches. The authors then introduce a retrieval-memory multi-agent adjudication approach informed by these findings.

entry.title: Whose startup does the AI back? An algorithm audit of reputation and demographic signals in LLM-assisted crowdfunding

author.name: Mirza Samad Ahmed Baig, Syeda Anshrah Gillani

entry.summary: A large pre-specified conjoint experiment (seven LLMs, 40,248 responses) audits how LLM assistants use founder gender and ethnicity signals when advising on crowdfunding campaigns. Results show founder names barely matter under task-focused backer personas, with demographic effects largely emerging only under specific persona conditions.

entry.title: DiMuRe: Diagnosis-Guided Multilevel Recovery for Robotic Task Execution

author.name: Renkai Yi, Yuwei Wu, Haoyu Zhang, Penghao Dai, Zhi Gao, Jin Chen, Che Sun

entry.summary: DiMuRe is a recovery framework for robot agents that uses phase-specific evidence and method preconditions to choose between program reuse, predefined recovery skills, or MLLM-generated corrective code, with local verification of each attempt. The authors also contribute LIBERO-Disturb, a benchmark for robustness and recovery under disturbances.

entry.title: Reciprocity Can Erase Direction:tructural Boundaries and Controlled Utility of Magnetic Graph Networks

author.name: Dawei Han, Zicheng Wang, Yaoxing Ren, Yi Lv, Rongqian Wu, Fumin Wang

entry.summary: The paper characterizes when magnetic graph networks, which encode direction through phase, can lose their directional mechanism during learning. It provides exact identities linking imaginary energy to amplitude-weighted reciprocity, proves failure conditions under top-k selection, and constructs paired examples with a provable chance-level limit for direction-erasing representations.

entry.title: Density-Aware Reward Scaling: A Reinforcement Learning Framework for Reward-Proportional Sampling

author.name: Ria Shekhawat, Abhijeet Sinha, Yingtao Zhu, Dianbo Liu

entry.summary: DARS is a reward-processing mechanism that promotes reward-proportional sampling in continuous outcome spaces by inversely scaling rewards according to local outcome density within each on-policy rollout group. It requires no learned density model, critic, or change to the policy-gradient objective, and avoids mode collapse in a multimodal navigation task.

entry.title: VisSearch-Bench: Evaluating Long Horizon Visual Search in Multimodal Agents

author.name: ZhengXian Wu, Qianhao Nie, Zhuohong Chen, Junjie Gao, Yuyao Zhang, Yunyao Yu, Hangrui Xu, Cheng Cheng, Guiyu Ma, Jin Zhang, Xingzhong Xu, Kai Yang, Haoqian Wang

entry.summary: VisSearch-Bench provides 204 human-written tasks across 7 domains evaluating multimodal agents on visual context management: linking object appearance, details, and spatial relations to external information over multi-step web and image search. It covers set-wise, sequential, and hybrid visual search beyond image-as-entity-identification tasks.

entry.title: Molecular Prior Networks

author.name: Pawel Gomoluch, Anthony Bradley

entry.summary: This paper applies tabular in-context foundation models, specifically Prior-data Fitted Networks, to drug-target affinity prediction, a setting where labeled data is scarce (tens to hundreds of molecules per project). Molecular Prior Networks aim to make existing protein-ligand affinity datasets usable for new chemical series and targets via single-forward-pass inference. It targets a central, expensive bottleneck in drug discovery.

entry.title: LoopVQ: Sub 1-bit KV Cache Quantization for Looped Transformers

author.name: Minsoo Cheong, Sungjoo Yoo

entry.summary: LoopVQ targets the KV cache bottleneck in looped transformers, where each loop step stores its own keys and values, causing cache growth linear in loop steps. Exploiting high redundancy of the cache along the loop axis and differing quantization sensitivity across steps, the authors propose a vector quantization scheme achieving sub 1-bit compression. This makes parameter-efficient looped language models practical for memory-constrained deployment.

entry.title: Honest Small Decision Models for Finance: Scale, Specialization Collapse, and Mixed-Corpus Remediation

author.name: Ajitabh Kumar

entry.summary: The author trains small System-1 decision models (0.8B to 32B parameters across two families) fine-tuned to output calibrated typed decisions in a single forward pass on finance and policy corpora, including a sealed 2026 outcome-based test set. Narrow fine-tuning costs 9-45 percentage points of general decision competence, with mixed-corpus training proposed as remediation for this specialization collapse.

entry.title: Denoising Is Stein: Moment Access and a Resource Hierarchy for Learning Hidden Structure in Diffusion Models

author.name: Rui Wang

entry.summary: This theory paper studies what can be learned about hidden non-Gaussian structure in data from diffusion model denoising pairs. It shows that correlations in the denoising loss act as Stein discrepancies that yield exact moment queries on the clean distribution, and derives a resource hierarchy: recovering a latent component requires order d^(k*-1) features in the covariance-matched regime, where k* is the order of the first distinguishing moment.

entry.title: RAPID: Increasing Efficiency of Internal Distillation via Randomized Methods

author.name: Ryan Swift, Konstantinos Psounis

entry.summary: RAPID addresses the inefficiency of learnable projection matrices in internal knowledge distillation, where dimensional mismatches between teacher and student representations force costly projectors that are discarded after training. The proposed randomized method replaces learned projections with randomized ones, reducing training cost. This is a practical efficiency improvement for compressing large models into small students.

entry.title: Deep Learning Compilers: Architecture, Optimization, and Empirical Characterization

author.name: Jinghao Wen, Ruixuan Wang, Xun Jiao

entry.summary: A systematic survey of deep learning compilers covering frontend, middle-end, and backend architecture, compilation workflows, and optimization techniques for heterogeneous hardware. The paper also includes empirical characterization and outlines emerging research directions.

entry.title: Leakage-free evaluation of residual graph convolutional networks for network intrusion detection

author.name: Zahid Iqbal

entry.summary: This study re-evaluates residual graph convolutional networks for intrusion detection after removing sources of optimism such as test flows shaping training graphs, duplicate flows across splits, and single-split reporting. After rigorous cleaning, the residual GCN's advantage over eight simpler baselines largely disappears.

entry.title: Non-Interfering Asymmetric AdamW Updates for Constrained Exploration of Equifinality in Hybrid Models

author.name: Ekaterina Gikalo, Zavud Baghirov, Christian Reimers, Markus Reichstein, Martin Jung, Marco K\"orner

entry.summary: This paper addresses equifinality in hybrid physics-ML models, where fits to aggregate observations leave internal partitions (like the split of evapotranspiration into transpiration and evaporation) underdetermined. The authors deliberately induce diverse partitionings across ensemble members using auxiliary repulsion terms and a modified asymmetric AdamW update scheme. This matters for scientific ML applications where mechanism attribution, not just prediction accuracy, is the goal.

entry.title: Towards an Optimal Control Foundation of Early Exits - Turnpikes and ResNets

author.name: Jens P\"uttschneider, Simon Heilig, Asja Fischer, Timm Faulwasser

entry.summary: Using optimal control theory, the authors prove that ResNets trained with joint losses on output and intermediate layers exhibit the turnpike phenomenon, bounding the number of layers needed to reach a prescribed loss level independently of total depth. This yields a similarity property across internal representations and gives a theoretical foundation for early-exit inference and data-dependent regularization. Relevant to making deep inference more efficient in a principled way.

entry.title: Beyond Foundation Models: PFN Priors Improve Tabular Hyperparameter Optimization

author.name: Artem Chistyakov, Renat Sergazinov, Artem Babenko

entry.summary: PriorTune reuses tabular foundation model synthetic priors to meta-tune hyperparameter configurations for conventional models trained from scratch, selecting a configuration pool offline on PFN-sampled tasks. Online, new datasets only fit the selected configurations, yielding performance gains at no extra inference cost, with scaling behavior observed in both configurations and synthetic datasets.

entry.title: Mapping urban heat from citizen-collected data: a scalable Gaussian process approach to correcting for preferential sampling

author.name: Ellie K. Kim, Zachary D. Calhoun, Michael H. Bergin, David E. Carlson

entry.summary: This paper introduces two scalable Gaussian process frameworks that correct for preferential sampling bias in crowdsourced urban temperature data, enabling statewide high-resolution mapping of urban heat island effects. It matters because dense citizen-collected sensor data is noisy and spatially biased, yet is critical for neighborhood-scale public health assessment of heat stress.

entry.title: Integrating Machine Learning and Uncertainty Quantification for Real-Time Decision-Making in Digital Twins: A System-Centric Review and Perspective

author.name: Yi-Ping Chen, Ying-Kuan Tsai, Seul Lee, Vispi Karkaria, Dex Doksoo Lee, Wei Chen

entry.summary: A narrative review of Digital Twins that examines how predictive modeling, machine learning, uncertainty quantification, and decision-making must be integrated to sustain closed-loop, real-time operation. It is scoped by functional requirements of real-time decision-making rather than Digital Twin terminology, covering architectures and engineering applications.

entry.title: COMPREHEND: Ultra-Fine-Grained Benchmark Understanding by Entailment Hierarchy

author.name: Sivaraaman Balakrishnan, Prakriti Shetty, Jeremiah Hong, Hamed Zamani, Haw-Shiuan Chang

entry.summary: This paper introduces COMPREHEND, a method that automatically builds an ultra-fine-grained entailment hierarchy over user prompts to characterize LLM strengths and weaknesses. Instead of general cluster names, it uses entailment-based sentences for precise cluster descriptions, helping practitioners understand prompt distributions and model performance in detail.

entry.title: What Does the Model See? Representation Validity in Multimodal LLM-Based Video Analysis

author.name: Christian Pipal, Eva-Maria Vogel, Morgan Wack

entry.summary: This paper examines representation validity for social-science video analysis with multimodal LLMs, comparing text, audio, video, and combined inputs across six open-weight models and three annotated datasets on seven news-related constructs. No representation consistently wins: three models do better with text and three with video, and combining inputs rarely helps, so measurement validity does not follow accuracy alone.

entry.title: Weight-Space Programming for Improving Image-Restoration Diffusion Models: Technical Conjectures and a Recursive Improvement Loop

author.name: Zhuoran Zheng, Doubao

entry.summary: Explores whether LLMs can directly edit diffusion model weights to improve image restoration quality (deblurring, super-resolution, denoising, inpainting) without gradients or paired data, extending weight-space programming from bug-fixing to capability improvement. The paper argues restoration UNets are a good testbed because low-level signal-processing layers are localized enough for targeted weight edits.

entry.title: 3DGS-VBench+ and 3DGSV-Assessor: A Multi-Dimensional Subjective Benchmark and a Reference-Flexible Objective Model for 3D Gaussian Splatting Video Quality Assessment

author.name: Yuke Xing, William Gordon, Jiarui Wang, Yujie Zhang, Guangtao Zhai, Yiling Xu

entry.summary: Introduces a large-scale subjective benchmark and an objective quality model for compressed 3D Gaussian Splatting videos, addressing dimension-specific distortions from generative compression and the lack of aligned ground-truth references in real captures. This supports quality-controlled deployment of splatting-based novel view synthesis.

entry.title: VISAGE: Vertex-based Intrinsic Surface Appearance GEneration via Dual-Stream Diffusion for Arbitrary 3D Heads

author.name: Jeremias Krau{\ss}, Pragati Jaiswal, Ren\'e Schuster, Didier Stricker

entry.summary: This paper introduces VISAGE, a conditional diffusion framework that generates per-vertex albedo and roughness directly on arbitrary 3D head meshes, avoiding the seam artifacts and surface inconsistencies of UV-based or image-space pipelines. It combines global spectral processing with local geodesic K-nearest-neighbour refinement to recover detailed, physically based appearance from sparse multi-view images. The work matters for graphics, avatar creation, and 3D reconstruction where UV-free, topology-agnostic appearance generation is a practical bottleneck.

entry.title: Beyond Local Refinement: Wide-Area Precise Cross-View Localization

author.name: Qingguo Hu, Xinyu Ma, Yujie Lin, Yaoxiang Wang, Qi Shi, Zonghao Guo, Chi Chen, Jinsong Su

entry.summary: Studies cross-view localization over large aerial regions rather than narrow geographic priors, proposing RingMatch, a search-and-verify approach to handle spatial-extent disparity between ground and aerial views and visual ambiguity from look-alike locations. Extends fine-grained localization applicability when upstream localization is coarse.

entry.title: ScoreDial: Precise Control of Visual Attributes in Image Generation via Regressor Guidance from Limited Human Ratings

author.name: Jianbo Tang, Keita Ishii, Hiroki Sakamoto, Manabu Kikuchi, Katsuma Kitamura, Chiho Semba, Kenta Nishiyama, Teppei Mori, Yukihiro Kiwaki, Takeo Kato

entry.summary: ScoreDial enables requested-value control of image attributes by fitting a differentiable regressor to as few as 100-479 human-rated images and applying error-adaptive guidance during sampling to hit a requested rating value. It demonstrates precise control across four diverse attributes with a single shared sampler configuration and very low error.

entry.title: COSMIO: A Benchmark for Cross-Survey Modality Imputation

author.name: Dichang Zhang, Yixuan Shao, Jiaqi Deng, Jiali Cui, Haotian Yin, Yuanpeng Liu, Xiang Gao, Zhiqiang Lao, Heather Yu, Simon Birrer, Dimitris Samaras

entry.summary: Formalizes cross-survey modality imputation, inferring how an astronomical object appears in surveys it was not observed by, and introduces COSMIO, a benchmark of forward-rendered shared scenes across LSST, Euclid, and Roman with survey-specific instrument characteristics. It enables systematic evaluation of imputation methods under heterogeneous observation conditions.

entry.title: Self-Consistent Neural Control: Learning Trajectories for Implicit Equilibrium

author.name: Hengyi Zhou, Haobo Fang, Xiaonan Huang, Dezhong Tong, M. Khalid Jawed

entry.summary: Introduces Self-Consistent Neural Control, which improves adjoint-based trajectory optimization for systems governed by implicit equilibria by explicitly controlling sensitivity variations, deriving a bound on gradient error from the frozen-tangent approximation. This targets multistable, path-dependent physical systems where unrolling equilibrium solvers is expensive.

entry.title: VARP: A Visual Adaptive Rearrangement Planner for Non-Monotone Object Rearrangement Planning

author.name: Hanwen Ren, Meng Zheng, Zhongpai Gao, Anwesa Choudhuri, Benjamin Planche, Terrence Chen, Ziyan Wu

entry.summary: VARP learns non-monotone object rearrangement directly from visual state representations generated from expert demonstrations, predicting pick-and-place actions from current and goal states. An Action Refinement Strategy improves action feasibility while a Progress Enforcement Strategy mitigates stagnation. This avoids the high computational cost and expensive replanning of search-based planners in cluttered environments.

entry.title: Caging Vision-Language Navigation for Legged Robots via Barrier-Certified Safety Architecture

author.name: Abhijeet M. Kulkarni, Saimouli Katragadda, Yuze Du, Zijun Sha, Guoquan Huang

entry.summary: The paper augments end-to-end VLA navigation planners for legged robots with a low-level physical-grounding and safety layer, providing barrier-certified guarantees rather than replacing the learned planner. The caging architecture adds the physical grounding and explicit safety assurance that pretrained LLM/VLM-based planners lack for real-world legged operation.

entry.title: Computing Invariant Reachable Sets through Sum-of-Squares Programming

author.name: Mohamed Khalid M Jaffar

entry.summary: This paper presents a self-contained, practical treatment of computing funnels — time-varying invariant sets that certify a closed-loop robotic system tracks its planned trajectory — using sum-of-squares (SOS) programming. It proposes a minimum-volume formulation with inlet and outlet constraints so that funnels compose by construction, and releases an open-source implementation (computeSOSFunnels). The work addresses the gap between well-established SOS funnel theory and its sensitive, under-documented practice.

entry.title: Can alignment realistically be solved under Plan C?

author.name: Simon Lermen

entry.summary: Simon Lermen argues against the view that alignment could be solved during a short pause, responding to Scott Alexander's Plan C argument that delegating alignment to AI systems might work within months. The post contends we get one critical shot with limited ability to learn from experience, and that trained models will diverge from trained-for objectives, making brief-pause alignment solutions implausible.

entry.title: Toward User-Centered Agentic Recommendation: When Does Platform Competition Benefit Users?

author.name: Kehan Zheng, Deyao Hong, Qian Li, Jun Zhang, Jie Jiang, Hongning Wang

entry.summary: The paper formalizes user-centered agentic recommendation as a repeated game where user agents compare recommendations from competing platform agents that strategically modify item descriptions, with users assessing credibility from consumption feedback alone. Analysis shows expanded cross-platform access need not improve welfare because strategic misrepresentation can offset competition benefits.

entry.title: TactiNavi: Serving and Revising an LLM Game Coach with Explicit Strategy Conditions

author.name: Qi Liu, Xiaoyang Yuan, Zhuomeng Zhang, Yubin Ruan, Xinyi Mou, Wenjin Wang, Hanying Jiao, Di Wu, Jinke Li, Jingxuan Hong, Ke Feng, Zixun Sun

entry.summary: TactiNavi is the serving system behind a commercial open-world game LLM coach that makes strategy applicability an explicit artifact spanning offline compilation, online execution, failure diagnosis, and release. An offline compiler produces strategy packages with explicit prerequisites, which the serving plane evaluates as three-valued conditions over structured player state, enabling validated revisions via condition-rule dependency tracking.

entry.title: Learning Directional Randers Geometry for Latent-Space Exploration

author.name: Th\'eau Blanchard (HeKA | U1346, GE Healthcare), St\'ephanie Allassonni\`ere (CMAP)

entry.summary: This paper argues that asymmetry, not curvature, is the key missing geometric structure in deep latent spaces, learning directional Randers geometry to model asymmetric transition costs. This captures directional processes like disease progression where certain transitions are impossible, improving interpolation and extrapolation fidelity over symmetric Riemannian metrics.

entry.title: P$^2$-MOPD: Accelerating Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation via Parameter Priors

author.name: Sinuo Wang, Jiacheng Lu, Zeyu Zhang, Maojia Song, Rui Sun, Beidi Luan, Yutong Xie, Jing Li, Daxin Jiang, Qi Wu, Zuo Bai

entry.summary: P2-MOPD unifies multi-teacher on-policy distillation with task arithmetic by treating the linear combination of student and expert parameters as a differentiable model, jointly optimizing mixing coefficients and student weights under the same distillation objective. Unlike task arithmetic, the student remains trainable so experts act as parameter priors rather than constraining the student to the frozen parameter span, with gains across four domains at 1.7B and 4B scales.

entry.title: ScienceVision: Can AI Observe and Reason Like a Scientist?

author.name: Tianyi Ma, Jing Gu, Haozhe Zhao, Liang Chen, Yunfan Zhang, Haijun Su, Jialong Wu, Le Xue, Arnav Das, Dustin Tran, Yinfei Yang, Andrew Dai, Kuan Li

entry.summary: ScienceVision is a cross-domain benchmark for scientific 3D understanding and reasoning, with 250 expert-level VQA questions spanning Biology, Chemistry, Medical Imaging, Mechanical CAD, and Architecture. It addresses the gap left by benchmarks focused on text and 2D images and inconsistent 3D evaluation protocols across disciplines.

entry.title: GeoFaham: Domain-Specialized Multi-Agent Geospatial Analytics for Disaster Response

author.name: Muhammad Sohail Danish, Gilles Q. Hacheme, Akram Zaytar, Satej S. Soman, Inbal Becker-Reshef, Juan Lavista Ferres, Salman Khan, Girmaw Abebe Tadesse

entry.summary: GeoFaham is a domain-specialized multi-agent system for disaster-response geospatial questions that require multi-source workflows combining spatial databases, satellite imagery, and raster products while preserving spatial scope, temporal context, and execution state. It targets geospatial-specific agent failure modes such as wrong evidence-source selection and invalid geometric operations.

entry.title: MedPhysBench: A Benchmark for Evaluating Language Models on Medical Physics Calculations and Error Detection

author.name: Omar Nusrat

entry.summary: MedPhysBench evaluates language models on medical physics calculations in radiation therapy, diagnostic imaging, nuclear medicine, and radiation protection, using ten seeded generators up to clinical tasks like TG-51 calibration worksheets. Reference answers come from code implementing governing protocols, with a unit-aware grader and separate error-detection items where half of colleague worksheets contain a planted error. It probes whether LLMs can perform and check safety-critical clinical calculations.

entry.title: Graph-Localized Coverage for Conformal Prediction on Inductive Graphs

author.name: Jinwen Xu, Qin Lu, Georgios B. Giannakis

entry.summary: GLocalCP is an online conformal prediction framework for inductive node classification and edge prediction that combines marginal coverage with graph-local calibration using kernel-based local corrections. It introduces an uncertainty-adaptive nonconformity score based on mutual information from MC-dropout predictions, providing finer-grained coverage guarantees that reflect neighborhood-level uncertainty.

entry.title: Exploiting Biases in Attention for Transformers

author.name: Charles Herr, Gabriele Spadaro, Enzo Tartaglione

entry.summary: The authors analyze column-wise sparsity and unequal relevance of attention matrices in vision transformers, showing token importance grows more pronounced with depth. They propose an attention reformulation adding an input-dependent bias term that scores each token's anticipated influence, usable as a proxy for pruning attention maps.

entry.title: Auditing Multi-Proxy Explanations of Web User Preferences: Identification Boundaries and Abstention

author.name: Yu Zhang, Zhihan Wang, Yuhang Lu, Shuai Li

entry.summary: The authors develop an audit framework for explanation methods applied to preference proxies (behavior, ratings, text, LLM-generated profiles), distinguishing point identification, partial identification, and principled abstention relative to a reference distribution. They prove a sharp majority threshold under which the coordinatewise median recovers latent attribution support and direction despite arbitrarily signed proxy bias, plus minimax error characterization. This is rigorous work on the trustworthiness of explanation pipelines in recommendation and web systems.

entry.title: Complete Donor-Set Guidance for Frozen Diffusion Docking Models

author.name: Hyunwoo Kim, Insoo Park, Ziseok Lee, Wooyeol Lee, Yoorim Gang, Kyungsu Kim

entry.summary: The paper proposes Complete-Identity Contract Guidance (CICG) and Historical Contract Transfer (HCT), inference-time techniques that steer pre-trained general-purpose diffusion docking models to respect specified metal-coordinating ligand donor atoms without retraining. This corrects incorrect metal-donor geometry in predicted poses, which matters for metalloprotein drug docking.

entry.title: Hybrid acoustic and pretrained embedding feature fusion for unmanned aerial vehicle detection using stacking ensemble learning under a leakage-aware evaluation protocol

author.name: Zahid Iqbal

entry.summary: The paper revisits acoustic drone detection on a public dataset, exposing severe data leakage from random clip-level splits when sources span train and test sets. It introduces a grouped, source-disjoint evaluation protocol and fuses acoustic features with pretrained embeddings in a stacking ensemble, showing how reported accuracies deflate under honest evaluation.

entry.title: EvoGroup: A Self-Evolving Harness for Group Agents in Shared Contexts

author.name: Xinyi Xu, Xiaoyang Li, Yucheng Feng, Wenqing Chen, Youliang Yuan, Wei Shi, Rongxiang Weng, Zibin Zheng

entry.summary: Proposes EvoGroup, a self-evolving harness for group agents collaborating in shared, continuously accumulating contexts, starting from a minimal six-tool cold start and adapting via confidence signals during interaction. It targets group-level knowledge (relationships, collaboratively formed knowledge) that individual-agent memory systems miss.

entry.title: CardioVascBench:Prioritized Diagnosis Generation from Real-World Chinese Cardiovascular Records

author.name: Minghao Kong, Muyao Chen, Jianhao Wu, Yuqiang Zhang, Xiangbin Meng, Zirong Liu, Ting Cao, Kaida Ning, Zhen Song, Rongjie Wang

entry.summary: CardioVascBench is a retrospective benchmark of 3,262 de-identified Chinese cardiovascular inpatient cases linking clinical narratives and ECG reports to expert-verified, ICD-10-standardized ordered discharge diagnoses. Its rank-aware protocol separately evaluates primary-diagnosis identification, coverage, and list precision, with an English translation enabling cross-lingual comparison.

entry.title: Auditing Targetless Camera-LiDAR Extrinsic Correction before Recursive Use

author.name: Bo Ma, Weiqi Yan

entry.summary: Proposes a log-disjoint audit protocol for targetless camera-LiDAR extrinsic correction, evaluating correction quality, confidence ranking, and recursive risk under synthetic drift on Argoverse 2. Findings are sobering: single-frame Canny alignment is harmful in mild drift, and multi-frame alignment's claimed joint improvement is statistically negative.

entry.title: Bounded AUKS: A Novel Evaluation Metric for Anomaly Detection via Bounded Area Under the Kolmogorov--Smirnov Curve

author.name: Yanshuo Zhang, Juan Du

entry.summary: Proposes Bounded AUKS, a new anomaly detection metric measuring separation between normal and anomalous score distributions, addressing thresholds-blindness in AUROC and FPR/FNR trade-offs in AUPRO as benchmark scores approach saturation. Reevaluates practical readiness of anomaly detection on MVTec AD and VisA.

entry.title: Sparse Anchors for Visual Multi-Session Registration in Changing Environments

author.name: Yunus Talha Erzurumlu, Niklas Trekel, Saurabh Gupta, Nico Koltermann, Olga Vysotska, Jens Behley, Louis Wiesmann, Cyrill Stachniss

entry.summary: The paper tackles visual multi-session localization for repeated robotic monitoring, where environmental change leaves only sparse reliable cross-session correspondences. It registers a full query trajectory to a reference map by combining a sparse set of absolute pose anchors with within-session relative-pose constraints.

entry.title: Sparse-View 3D Coronary Reconstruction from Vessel Segmentations Using a Diffusion Prior

author.name: Tianyuan Wang, Kenan Niu, Stefano Stramigioli

entry.summary: Proposes a vessel-specific 3D coronary reconstruction framework combining an unconditional diffusion prior trained on coronary masks (without paired 2D-3D data), visual-hull initialization, and projection-based data consistency, reusable across different view counts without retraining. It targets supporting percutaneous coronary intervention under sparse angiographic views.

entry.title: Low-Rank Hierarchical Merging for Efficient Long-to-Short Reasoning

author.name: Zeqiu Yu, Xuesheng Zhang, Wenxiao Zhao, Shixiao Wang

entry.summary: LHM is a training-free model-merging framework that combines long chain-of-thought reasoning with the concise style of base models by replacing first-order activation statistics with lightweight second-order curvature information, using Hutchinson-estimated low-rank Hessian approximations. This addresses degraded hard-task accuracy in linear-interpolation merging methods.

entry.title: Measuring Model-Specific Alignment Drift in LLM-Based Opinion Dynamics

author.name: Nata\v{s}a Djurdjevac Conrad, Sebastian Pokutta, Christof Sch\"utte

entry.summary: Using a psychometric instrument to quantify stances of LLM agents discussing a contested policy issue over repeated rounds, this study finds committed personas are intrinsically stable but lose alignment under peer interaction - a model-specific phenomenon termed alignment drift. Across six LLMs, gpt-4.1 keeps opinion clusters apart while other models behave differently.

entry.title: The Agent Board: Kanban for Machines; Durable Coordination for Agents That Outlive the Conversation

author.name: Tyler Hunt, Donald Nguyen, Gurbinder Gill

entry.summary: The Agent Board is a durable, shared table of semi-semantic tasks enabling multi-agent coordination that outlives any single model call, where agents post, watch, and block on tasks with a Board Keeper system agent handling events from non-agent systems. It challenges the single-threaded one-agent-one-history assumption underlying most LLM harnesses.

entry.title: CORA: Teacher-Guided Causal O-RAN Adaptation for Jamming Detection

author.name: Sneihil Gopal, Richard A. Rouil

entry.summary: Introduces a teacher-guided reinforcement learning framework that transfers the hindsight of a retrospective KPI detector to a causal, streaming-capable jamming detector for mission-critical networks, without labeled attack data. A retrospective teacher defines a recall-weighted reward for tuning a causal detector's sensitivity, persistence, and grace. This matters for 5G security where missed jamming events are costlier than false alarms and labels are scarce.

entry.title: CaliSplat: Sparse Gaussian Fitting and Calibrated Rate Allocation for Image Compression

author.name: Zhenbang Zhang, Zhengquan Luo, Kai Zhao, Zhiqiang Xu

entry.summary: Proposes CaliSplat, a Gaussian image codec that uses the closed-form reconstruction error of the single-Gaussian case as an inexpensive local difficulty measure, fitting higher-capacity candidates only where needed and globally allocating a constrained Gaussian budget. This removes costly per-image optimization while keeping deterministic fast decoding. Relevant to efficient learned image compression using explicit 2D Gaussian representations.

entry.title: Amortized Nonlinear Variable Selection with Prior-Data Fitted Networks

author.name: Jin Zhu, Junxian Zhu

entry.summary: The paper proposes MambaPFN, a model-agnostic method for nonlinear variable selection built on Transformers trained as prior-data fitted networks, treating variable selection as a functional-mapping learning problem. It amortizes selection across datasets so that it identifies variables with general nonlinear dependence on the response without refitting per-dataset pipelines.

entry.title: ReVi: Recursive Recap Video Generation

author.name: Kyrie You Wu, Chaozhuo Li, Songyang Liu, Xueyang Feng, Ziluowen Luo, Chenxu Wang, Ji Qi, Jinfu Zhu, Litian Zhang

entry.summary: ReVi addresses novel-to-recap video generation, producing self-contained, source-grounded audiovisual retellings of novels within a fixed viewing-time budget. Its dual-loop multi-agent approach handles story compression while preserving causal connections, time allocation for retained events, and narration-visual alignment.

entry.title: Characterizing Adversarial GEO via Implicit Brand Injection

author.name: Shobhnik Kriplani, Haohan Wang

entry.summary: This paper studies adversarial generative engine optimization (GEO), introducing Implicit Brand Injection (IBI), a method for inserting a target brand into retrieved articles so it fits naturally yet still influences generated search answers. It characterizes the trade-off between naturalness and retrieval relevance in manipulating generative search outputs.

entry.title: Navigating Runtime Dynamism in Semantic Query Serving

author.name: Hengrui Zhang, Xupeng Miao

entry.summary: This paper addresses efficient serving of LLM-powered semantic queries that combine relational processing with multiple LLM operators, tackling coupled inter-query scheduling and intra-query plan dynamism whose circular dependency makes statically optimized plans unreliable. It proposes handling runtime variation in operator costs and selectivities during execution.

entry.title: CosmosAlpha: Multi-Relational Graph Search with Pareto-Guided Exploration for LLM-Driven Alpha Mining

author.name: Zhan-He Wang, Zi-Yang Lang, Yi-Yang Li, Qing-Yu Lan, Yun-Song Piao

entry.summary: CosmosAlpha reframes LLM-driven formulaic alpha factor mining as multi-relational graph search, using structural and statistical relationships across search branches rather than generation lineage alone. Pareto-guided exploration handles the multiple non-commensurable objectives of factor discovery and reduces redundant exploration.

entry.title: Therapy-FIS: A Dataset for Assessing Facilitative Interpersonal Skills in Psychotherapeutic Setting

author.name: Qijian Zheng, Wanqing Lin, Yuanfang Wang, Yijun Ge, Jordan Bate, Katie Aafjes-van Doorn, Feng Liu

entry.summary: The paper introduces Therapy-FIS, claimed to be the first publicly available dataset for automated assessment of Facilitative Interpersonal Skills in psychotherapy, containing facial, acoustic, and textual data from standardized therapy tasks. It aims to automate a labor-intensive, human-rater-based evaluation process used for mental health professionals.

entry.title: Basin2Vec: Learning Basin-Centric Embeddings for Scalable Hydrological Modeling

author.name: Muhammad Talha, Xiaofeng Liu, Yuan Yang, Pang-Ning Tan, A. Pouyan Nejadhashemi

entry.summary: Basin2Vec is a self-supervised framework that learns compact representations of hydrological basins from hydroclimatic and physiographic data without requiring observed streamflow. Organized around basin scale and spatiotemporal relationships, the embeddings outperform handcrafted attributes and general-purpose geospatial embeddings on temporal generalization and zero-shot prediction in ungauged basins. It addresses a persistent challenge in hydrology: reliable prediction where measurements do not exist.

entry.title: Aligning Language Models with General Preferences: An Empirical Study of Direct Nash Optimization

author.name: Austin Tsai, Saurav Nanda, Ganapathy Parthasarathy, Bhuvnesh Kumar, Parivesh Choudhary

entry.summary: This paper independently re-implements Direct Nash Optimization (DNO-Prct) and evaluates it on Llama 3.1 8B Instruct and Mistral 7B Instruct v0.1 with GPT-4o or family-matched open models as annotators. Three iterations raise length-controlled win rates against GPT-4o on AlpacaEval 2.0 from 31.7% to 45.3% for Llama and from 6.8% substantially higher for Mistral. It provides empirical validation of a Nash-equilibrium-based alignment alternative to RLHF/DPO.

entry.title: Does the Trust Boundary Hold over Time? A Long-Horizon Benchmark for Receiver-Directed Federated Learning

author.name: Ting Xu, Henry Leung

entry.summary: The paper introduces a long-horizon benchmark for receiver-directed federated learning where each site admits, rejects, or abstains on incoming model transfers, testing whether trust decisions hold over hundreds of rounds. With thirteen semi-synthetic sites, exact oracles, and attack protocols, it finds fixed-reference gates admit 29% of transfers harmful to the site's current model.

entry.title: Quantifying out-of-distribution data severity with Wasserstein distances: benchmarking large language models for alloy property prediction

author.name: YuJie Liu, Dezhen Xue, Jun Sun, Xiangdong Ding, Zhibin Gao, Turab Lookman

entry.summary: This paper benchmarks general-purpose LLMs against domain-specific materials models (SteelBERT, MatSciBERT, SciBERT) for alloy property prediction across Ti, steels, high-entropy alloys, and Al, finding LLMs surprisingly outperform the specialized models. It also uses Wasserstein distances to quantify OOD severity and proposes a hybrid approach where priors from CatBoost or SteelBERT prompt LLMs like DeepSeek V3.1 and Gemini-2.5-Flash as reasoners.

entry.title: Rapid Mean-Field Formation Transport with a Shared-Representation Neural Fokker-Planck Controller

author.name: Zejian Zhou, Hao Xu

entry.summary: The authors develop a mean-field formation transport controller for large-scale multi-agent systems that avoids repeated solution of coupled forward-backward PDEs at planning time. Density and control are approximated by a shared parameterized nonlinear map trained offline on Fokker-Planck residuals, formation-matching costs, and control effort, enabling low-cost online replanning.

entry.title: StreamLTT: Risk Certification for Policy Selection under Stream Dependence

author.name: Jinwen Xu, Qin Lu

entry.summary: StreamLTT extends the Learn-then-Test framework for certifying deployment policies to sequential settings where losses are dependent and nonstationary, by introducing an average predictable risk that conditions each loss on previously observed information. Using conditional centering, empirical deviations form a martingale, enabling variance-adaptive tests and finite-sample Hoeffding-style guarantees.

entry.title: Variational Learning with Lie Group Exponential Families

author.name: Eren Mehmet K{\i}ral, Thomas M\"ollenhoff, Koichi Tojo, Mohammad Emtiyaz Khan, Kenichi Bannai

entry.summary: The paper extends a Lie group framework for variational Bayesian learning in deep networks to general Lie groups, giving explicit connections to natural-gradient variational methods such as Bayesian learning rule. Lie group parameterizations naturally handle constraints and yield low-variance gradient estimators.

entry.title: Sheaf-MPNN: A Library for Sheaf Neural Networks as Message Passing

author.name: Alessio Borgi, Mario Severino, Luke Braithwaite, Steve Azzolin, R\'emi Bourgerie, Olga Zaghen, Emanuele Mule, Riccardo Ali, Leo Minh Kustermann, Edoardo Coppola, Antonio Purificato, Stefano Fiorini, Christopher Irwin, Filippo Spiga, Fabrizio Silvestri, Michael Bronstein, Pietro Li\`o

entry.summary: Sheaf-MPNN is a PyTorch Geometric library reformulating sheaf neural network diffusion as local incidence-wise transport instead of assembling a global sheaf Laplacian matrix, reducing memory and compute overhead. Sheaf networks give nodes and edges their own vector spaces to address oversmoothing and heterophilic graphs.

entry.title: On the Complexity of Finite-Sum Nonconvex-Strongly-Concave Minimax Optimization with Exact Proximal Oracles

author.name: Yuxing Peng, Zhiqing Tang, Weijia Jia

entry.summary: This paper establishes lower bounds for finite-sum nonconvex-strongly-concave minimax problems, showing that neither unrestricted adaptivity nor exact component proximal access improves polynomial complexity. The proximal oracles considered expose global saddle points of regularized component problems, directions invisible to plain gradients. The result tightens our understanding of what is achievable in adversarial training and distributionally robust optimization.

entry.title: Cool Graphs: Active Property Search Towards Quantum Nano-Refrigerators

author.name: Sofia Blyufer, Amir Kleiner, Uri Peskin

entry.summary: The authors combine a Graph Variational Autoencoder with an uncertainty-driven active learning loop to search the exponentially large configuration space of quantum nano-refrigerators, identifying energy-absorbing configurations in electronic junctions. The GVAE maps physical parameters into a smooth latent space separating cooling from dissipative regimes, drastically reducing the number of expensive quantum-chemical computations needed. A nice example of ML accelerating materials and quantum device discovery.

entry.title: Federated Transfer Learning for Medical Image Classification under Mixed Skew

author.name: Alexandre G. Leclercq, S\'ebastien Bougleux, Aur\'elien Corroyer-Dulmont, Romain H\'erault

entry.summary: The paper proposes a personalized federated learning method for medical imaging that handles mixed skew (feature, label, concept, and quantity shifts across institutions) and starts from a pretrained foundation model rather than training from scratch, which is essential given limited per-site data. This addresses privacy-constrained multicenter medical AI realistically. Deployable personalized FL for healthcare is a significant practical need.

entry.title: NovoCRF: Globally Normalized De Novo Peptide Sequencing on a Prefix-Mass Lattice

author.name: Rui Qiao, Lei Xin, Baozhen Shan

entry.summary: NovoCRF is a conditional random field whose states are prefix masses, restricting candidate paths to peptides within a tight mass tolerance, with edge scores from physics-derived ion-match features and globally normalized training over all mass-feasible peptides. It claims to be the first de novo peptide sequencing method trained with exact normalization over all mass-feasible candidates.

entry.title: A local orchestration harness for molecular design with foundation models

author.name: Sakib Mostafa, Md Atik Ahamed, James Zou, Lei Xing, Md Tauhidul Islam

entry.summary: MolCrew is a locally deployable system that coordinates specialized molecular models for generation, description, endpoint prediction, and editing through a language-model orchestrator and RDKit validation, keeping molecular data under local control. It addresses data privacy, cross-task model integration, and chemical constraint verification in molecular design workflows.

entry.title: Co-Occurrence Priors Override Visual Spatial Evidence: Understanding False Alarms in Vision-Language Models for Construction Struck-By Hazard Detection

author.name: Xiaoshan Zhou

entry.summary: Using 355 counterfactual worker-excavator scene pairs, this study probes Qwen2.5-VL-7B and InternVL3.5-8B to show that false hazard alarms in construction safety VLMs stem from learned co-occurrence priors overriding spatial evidence, despite correct entity recognition and spatial relation encoding. The work combines behavioral analysis, representation probing, causal interventions, and decision correction.

entry.title: Conditional independence and graphical models for rankings

author.name: Aritz P\'erez

entry.summary: The paper introduces relative rank models, a probabilistic framework based on structured coarsenings of the ranking space that relax mutual-exclusivity constraints while preserving relative order information. This yields a well-defined notion of conditional independence for rankings and enables graphical model structure over ranking distributions.

entry.title: PROSE: Preservation-Constrained Selective Editing for Guilty Bias in Legal Judgment Prediction

author.name: Yimeng Wang, Zeyuan Tian, Xinyu Wang, Danyang Gao, Chenglei Shen, Zhongxiang Sun, Lei La, Weijie Yu

entry.summary: The paper studies guilty bias in legal judgment prediction models, which retain guilty verdicts even when a decisive legal condition is removed, and introduces CAIL-MC, a dataset of 11,478 matched case pairs across 261 Chinese criminal charges. PROSE performs preservation-constrained selective editing so unsupported verdicts change while supported ones remain stable.

entry.title: Computational Phenomenology of Borderline Personality Disorder: A Comparative Evaluation of LLM-Simulated Expert Personas and Human Clinical Experts

author.name: Marcin Moskalewicz, Anna Sterna, Karolina Dro\.zd\.z, Kacper Dudzic, Marek Pokropski, Paula Flores

entry.summary: This cross-listed study evaluates whether GPT, Gemini, and Claude models can support qualitative phenomenological analysis of clinical life-story interviews with BPD inpatients, using blinded expert judges, semantic congruence measures, and neural methods across two studies. It finds generally strong expert-rated validity for AI-generated thematic analysis relative to human clinical experts.

entry.title: SettleSplat: Monocular Gaussian Mapping under In-View Scene Changes

author.name: Anh Thuan Tran, Xiyun Song, Yubin Zhou, Heather Yu, Jana Kosecka, Liang Peng

entry.summary: SettleSplat tackles in-view scene changes in online 3D Gaussian mapping, where objects are manipulated in front of the camera and transition from transient distractors to persistent parts of the scene. This setting is distinct from prior work on out-of-view or cross-capture dynamics and requires disentangling transient from persistent change.

entry.title: Mitigating Spatial Blindness in Multiple Instance Learning for Whole-Slide Image Analysis

author.name: Xiangyu Li, Jincheng Li, Xing Xie, Bin Guan, Shaohua Kevin Zhou, Rui Yan, Ran Su

entry.summary: Identifies spatial blindness in whole-slide MIL, where models predict from tissue composition while ignoring spatial organization, and proposes ResTopoMIL: freeze a composition predictor, then train a graph residual pathway with a coordinate-reassignment separation loss. Includes permutation and information analyses plus a controlled spatial task to validate the mechanism.

entry.title: ReXMo: End-to-End Video Character Replacement with Expression and Motion Preservation

author.name: Hualiang Wei, Wenhui Li

entry.summary: An end-to-end framework for video character replacement supporting single-, multi-, and selective-character scenarios, using paired triplet supervision with synthetic driving data and an in-context diffusion transformer conditioned on driving videos, reference identities, and text. Aims to preserve expressions, motion, and scene dynamics better than masked pose-guided methods.

entry.title: Lightweight graph transformers for clutter and target classification in automotive radar

author.name: Adrian Gheorghiu, Tunc Alkanat, Ashish Pandharipande

entry.summary: The paper proposes TGTNet, tiny graph transformer models that classify radar detections as clutter versus stationary or moving targets on the public RadarScenes dataset. The models match state-of-the-art precision and recall while being one to two orders of magnitude smaller with significantly faster inference.

entry.title: CoReMatch: Recurrent Continuous Coordinate Refinement for Real-Time Robotic Feature Matching

author.name: Robert J. Wang, Charles Ling, Boyu Wang

entry.summary: Presents CoReMatch, a recurrent feature-matching framework that refines correspondences directly in continuous coordinate space instead of predicting confidence on fixed grids, using a Deep Aggregated Transformer for global context at the coarse stage. The approach targets robotic perception tasks like SLAM, localization, and navigation with real-time requirements.

entry.title: Mass Scaling Laws for Energy-Optimal Horizontal Multirotor Flight

author.name: Ayush Patnaik, Nicolas Michel, Leonard Baursfeld, Davide Scaramuzza, Xinfan Lin

entry.summary: The paper derives closed-form scaling relationships between energy-optimal steady horizontal flight behavior of a multicopter and its vehicle mass, validated experimentally on two multirotor platforms. These relations enable energy-aware flight planning under frequent payload-induced mass variation, addressing range and endurance bottlenecks in real drone applications.

entry.title: PACT: Pose-Robust Actuation Co-Design for Tendon-Driven Robotic Hands

author.name: Prashant Kumar, Rachael Granberry, Taylor Niehues, Andrew A. Stanley, Gabe Pirie

entry.summary: PACT is a co-design framework that jointly optimizes tendon routing, moment arms, and capstan dimensions for tendon-driven robotic hands under pose-dependent force requirements and bandwidth constraints, using a feasible-force formulation with equilibrium enforcement at all joints. It avoids the sequential design trap where force capability and joint speed trade off against each other.

entry.title: AI Safety at the Frontier: Paper Highlights of October 2026

author.name: gasteigerjo

entry.summary: A monthly digest summarizing frontier AI safety research highlights, including claims that superposition may be practically irrelevant for interpretability, OpenAI's expanded misalignment monitoring flagging 80% of past incidents, rogue self-deployment risk from cheap 26B-capable devices, LLM-simulated control evaluations, gradient routing to remove reward hacks, and Claude agents finding finetuning datasets that evade monitors.

entry.title: Exact Optimality Certification of QPLIB 2096 through Complete Set Partitioning

author.name: Jingyang Du, Zixiong Yi, Yang Shen

entry.summary: The authors provide an exact computational proof that the QPLIB_2096 nonconvex quadratic instance has global minimum 7,025,720, via a coefficient-level reconstruction into a set-partitioning formulation over 25 items, with the solution approach explored using ZiYor, a self-evolving AI system. This is a rare exact optimality certificate for a hard benchmark instance.

entry.title: RAHC: Rule-Augmented Hyper-Relational Knowledge Graph Completion for Materials Synthesis

author.name: Jiawei Sun, Sijia Xu, Zihan Chen, Zhengyi Yang

entry.summary: RAHC addresses recovering missing synthesis conditions in materials science via rule-augmented hyper-relational knowledge graph completion. It builds a traceable rule catalog from training records and retrieved literature, retrieves rules per query-candidate pair, and combines graph structure with explicit domain regularities to complete single-slot and joint multi-slot synthesis conditions.

entry.title: When the Consumer Is an Agent: Execution-Grounded Service-Level Agreements

author.name: Michal Orzechowski, Renata G. Slota, Jacek Kitowski

entry.summary: The paper introduces execution-grounded completion contracts, where an independent control plane verifies deadline-bound service-state predicates to determine whether an LLM agent's task is truly complete in asynchronous distributed services. Evaluation on a live multi-provider data service shows accepted completions can miss deadlines and the contracts improve accountability and recovery.

entry.title: Shuffled OPSD: When Semantic Consistency Hurts On-Policy Self-Distillation?

author.name: Qingyuan Zheng, Zhihao Dou

entry.summary: The paper asks whether preserving the semantic structure of the shared problem statement helps on-policy self-distillation, and shows that shuffling the question words while keeping the teacher-only worked example intact can surprisingly improve distillation of reasoning ability. This challenges an intuitive design assumption in OPSD.

entry.title: Physical Experience Builds Continual Spatial World Models

author.name: Yuhang Sun

entry.summary: Studies how continual physical experience can improve spatial world models over time using a physics-grounded dynamic maze that separates recurring spatial changes from action consequences, with a cross-episode Spatial Change Memory learning relations among environmental transformations. The work addresses how agents can update prior expectations without letting them override current physical evidence.

entry.title: Counterexample-driven autonomous research with application to excess radiated energy in a Z-pinch

author.name: Bowen Zhu, Jian Wu

entry.summary: Simjecture is an open-source framework where LLM agents pursue human-defined physical conjectures through counterexample-driven falsification and prospective hypothesis repair, using computational physics as an executable testbed. It is demonstrated on excess radiated energy in Z-pinch plasma physics.

entry.title: What Is This Memory Useful For? Measuring Task-Conditioned Utility in Long-Term Agent Memory

author.name: Chih-Hsuan Yang, Anjir Ahmed Chowdhury, Feng Yan, Rajeev Thakur

entry.summary: The paper proposes measuring task-conditioned utility of agent memories instead of single importance scores, using a task-blind writer, a frozen reader with and without the memory, and a cost ledger for resource accounting. On LongMemEval-V2-derived tasks, answer-bearing memories yield a +0.33 mean paired reward gain over matched controls.

entry.title: Forgetting to Improve: Principled Data Removal in Active Learning

author.name: Manuel Wendl, Erik Englesson, Andreas Krause, Carl Henrik Ek

entry.summary: The authors propose Forgetting to Improve, an influence-function method for Gaussian process models that identifies and removes data that harms modeling under model mismatch, embedding the downstream task into the modeling framework. It offers a principled treatment of aleatoric-epistemic decomposition as a property of the model rather than the data-generating process.

entry.title: Palimpsestic Accountability in the US Federal AI Inventories

author.name: Dipto Das, Syed Ishtiaque Ahmed, Aditya Vashistha, Shion Guha

entry.summary: This study links entries across three releases of the US Federal AI Use Case Inventory (2023-2025), analyzing how accountability accounts are rewritten as the inventory grew from 710 to 3,611 entries, guided by the ADMAPS framework. It reveals governance dynamics over time that single-release audits miss, with implications for public-sector AI oversight.

entry.title: Benchmarking Unsupervised Jamming Detection in 5G Open RAN

author.name: Sneihil Gopal, Fernando J. Cintron, Richard A. Rouil

entry.summary: Benchmarks statistical and reconstruction-based unsupervised jamming detectors in 5G Open RAN using a symmetric evaluation interface combining detection confidence and temporal interval coherence, enabling comparison without ground-truth labels. It compares a Statistical Ensemble Method detector against vanilla, LSTM, and other neural detectors. Useful for deployments lacking labeled RF attack data.

entry.title: Large Language Model-Assisted Adaptive Heuristic Search for Agile Earth Observation Satellite Scheduling

author.name: He Wang, Yeye Liu, Ruijie Li, Xuemei Jiang, Junyu Wu, Lining Liu Zhuoqi Man, Tao Li, Yanjie Song

entry.summary: Proposes an LLM-assisted adaptive heuristic search for agile Earth observation satellite scheduling, where an LLM generates an initial task-selection heuristic and refines it during ant colony search based on performance feedback. Evaluated via paired statistical tests, the letter targets a real operations-research problem with attitude maneuvering and energy constraints. A compact applied contribution combining LLMs with metaheuristic optimization.

entry.title: Reconstruction-Based Diagnosis through G\"odel-Regularized Virtual Observability

author.name: Oliver Niggemann, Jonas Ehrhardt, Alexander Diedrich

entry.summary: This arXiv paper addresses fault diagnosis in technical systems where not all components can be instrumented with sensors, causing faults to be detected only after their effects have propagated. The authors introduce virtual sensors built from a novel neural observer trained only on normal operating data: it uses available sensor measurements where possible and reconstructs missing variables to predict nominal behavior, flagging deviations as local symptoms for fault isolation. External knowledge describes the fault-sensitive variables for each component-fault combination, and the approach is regularized in a formally inspired (Goedel-regularized) manner.

entry.title: Fast, Cheap, and Fair? Evaluating Decision Models

author.name: Muhammad Uzair Ul Haq, Davide Rigoni, Alessandro Sperduti, Flavia Fabris

entry.summary: This paper presents the first systematic bias and fairness audit of a compact typed-decision model intended for recruitment screening, motivated by the EU AI Act classifying such systems as high-risk. The study evaluates whether cheap System-1 decision models introduce fairness problems relative to general-purpose LLMs in high-stakes HR decisions.

entry.title: AgentAM: An AI Agent for Spatter- and Defect-Aware Process Optimization in Laser Powder Bed Fusion

author.name: Olabode T. Ajenifujah, Amir Barati Farimani

entry.summary: AgentAM is an LLM agent that gives process engineers natural-language access to CFD-trained surrogate models for melt pool geometry and spatter in laser powder bed fusion via the Model Context Protocol. Polynomial surrogates predict melt pool dimensions with R2 of at least 0.95 and classify defect regimes consistently with simulations, lowering the programming barrier to shop-floor use.

entry.title: Zero-Gated Cross-Attention

author.name: Basavaraj R M, Manav Verma

entry.summary: Inductively Gated Cross-Attention (IGCA) is a zero-initialized cross-attention bridge that preserves frozen language model behavior at initialization while enabling gradual multimodal conditioning, demonstrated across Falcon-40B, open_llama_30b, and Bloom-7b1 backbones. It acts as an exact algebraic no-op at initialization, addressing early optimization instability when injecting non-text modalities.

entry.title: EvoMemState: Evolving Memory State for Personal Agents

author.name: Zhishang Xiang, Yunbo Tang, Zhongqiao Liu, Junkai Chen, Zerui Chen, Qingguo Hu, Yuxuan Zhang, William Grant, Qinggang Zhang, Jinsong Su

entry.summary: EvoMemState proposes a state-centric framework for LLM agent long-term memory that augments stored facts with Relational States tracking how facts remain valid and interact, plus a Reasoning State capturing applicability and priority for the current request. This addresses limitations of fact-centric memory systems that miss conflicts and updates between facts.

entry.title: Stacking-Based Weighting for Large Language Bayes in M-Open Settings

author.name: Anant Bhide, Akarsh Gupta, Edmond Cunningham, Justin Domke

entry.summary: The paper improves Large Language Bayes, where an LLM generates candidate probabilistic programs for a natural-language problem, by replacing likelihood-based Bayesian model averaging with stacking-based aggregation that selects weights by predictive performance. This better handles misspecified candidate models in M-open settings while preserving the language-model-driven model generation.

entry.title: Must AI Spell It Out? Pragmatic Comprehension of Alerts in a Time-Critical Task

author.name: Anwesha Das, Vera Demberg, Anna Maria Feit

entry.summary: This HCI-focused study tests whether users can understand deliberately incomplete alerts from assistive systems using pragmatic inference, comparing a pragmatic planner that models listener knowledge against a fully explicit baseline. In a preregistered study with 114 participants performing a time-critical monitoring task, the authors assess how prior knowledge and time pressure affect detection of critical situations.

entry.title: Separating Common and Unique Directions for Data-Free Model Merging

author.name: Shiting Wang, Yingjie Zou, Ke li

entry.summary: The paper identifies a two-regime structure in task vectors — a low-dispersion common bulk shared across tasks and a high-dispersion task-dominated tail — and proposes CUSD, a data-free pre-merging method that separates common and unique directional components and merges each with tailored rules.

entry.title: IntentGEO: Intent-aware Generative Engine Optimization for Recommendation

author.name: Runlin Lei, Shiqi Zhang, Xiaokui Xiao, Zhewei Wei

entry.summary: IntentGEO formulates intent-aware generative engine optimization, showing that existing content-centric GEO methods produce visibility gains that vary with user need specificity and decision progression. It proposes optimizing shared item rewrites with awareness of how changing intent affects visibility in LLM-generated recommendations.

entry.title: From Watching to Steering: Enabling Human-Coding Agent Collaboration through Execution Traces

author.name: Xiaoke Yan, Jiaying Lei, Danqing Shi, Zichen Wang, Nan Cao

entry.summary: Vibetrace is an interactive system for visualizing and intervening in coding-agent execution traces, built on OpenCode, supporting an Observe-Understand-Intervene-Evolve workflow. Users can fork executions from prior steps for targeted corrections and distill traces plus human feedback for improvement.

entry.title: Polyp Matching Using Deep Learning

author.name: Kristian Dalsb{\o} Hindberg, Puneet Sharma, Benedicte Schelde-Olesen, Ulrik Deding, Jakob Frederik Fr{\o}kj{\ae}r Justsen, Jan-Matthias Braun, Esmaeil S. Nadimi
