The effect strengthens in certain conflict types, showing it is structuring rather than simple leniency.

entry.title: Completeness and Cost of Retrieval Structures for Multi-Tool Requests in LLM Agents

author.name: Shuyang Zhang

entry.summary: This work compares six tool-retrieval structures, from flat lexical and dense retrieval to LLM query decomposition, navigated hierarchies, dependency graphs, and trained set-level retrievers, on multi-tool requests using AppWorld and MCP-Bench testbeds. It measures completeness@k (whether the full required tool set appears in top-k) alongside LLM calls, tokens, and latency. The study fills a real gap since retrievers are typically evaluated on single-tool queries.

entry.title: An Empirical Study on Learning Rooftop Solar Potential from Satellite Imagery Directly Without Explicit Geometry

author.name: Joshua Lee

entry.summary: DRSP maps satellite imagery and coarse regional sunlight information directly to application-level rooftop solar outputs, bypassing explicit geometry reconstruction (DSMs, roof orientation, slope). It includes a programmatic data-curation pipeline from Google's solar panel dataset to enable large-scale study.

entry.title: Queryable Gaussian View Index: Text Retrieval and Selective Camera Localization

author.name: Tianyu Xiong, Rui Li, Jiaqi Yang

entry.summary: QGVI makes Gaussian splatting scene assets queryable: QGVI-T binds structured captions to camera poses for language-searchable view retrieval without online rendering, and QGVI-I filters geometric pose estimates using inlier query keypoints for selective RGB camera localization. It is evaluated on nine development scenes.

entry.title: Measuring What Matters: A Causal Reliance Score for Histopathology Image Segmentation

author.name: Samuel Thomas, Daniel Tweneboah Anyimadu, Ahmed Karam Eldaly, Somaia Elsheikh, Mohammed M. Abdelsamea

entry.summary: The paper introduces a causality-inspired evaluation framework and a Causal Reliance Score (CRS) that quantifies segmentation model sensitivity to foreground tissue perturbation versus background/domain variation under controlled interventions. It argues architecture improvements are insufficient if models depend on spurious correlations.

entry.title: CONSORT: Uncertainty-Constrained Multi-Robot Planning for Cooperative Localization in GPS-Denied Environments

author.name: Tony Zhang, Ryan Bartholomew, Kalliyan Velasco, Joshua Mangelson, Brady Moon

entry.summary: CONSORT tackles multi-agent path planning with cooperative localization in GPS-denied environments, a belief-space problem that is generally intractable. It derives a tractable surrogate by optimizing mean-state trajectories while propagating covariance only for terminal uncertainty constraint evaluation, under chance-constrained collision avoidance. This is important for real deployments such as underground or indoor multi-robot missions.

entry.title: Design and Validation of a Robotic Knee Exoskeleton with Musculoskeletal Simulation-Derived Biological Torque Control

author.name: Rajiv V. Joshi, Jimin An, Ilseung Park, Dawit Lee, Inseung Kang

entry.summary: This paper presents an open-source knee exoskeleton built from off-the-shelf components with a biological torque controller derived from musculoskeletal simulation, eliminating the need for device-specific data collection. Because existing open-source efforts release hardware, software, and controllers separately, this integrated release enables out-of-the-box deployment. It lowers barriers to reproducible exoskeleton research.

entry.title: The psychophysics of affect in large language models

author.name: Joseph Marks (NatWest Group, London, UK), Marius C. Vollberg (University of Zurich, Zurich, Switzerland, Swiss Center for Affective Sciences, Geneva, Switzerland)

entry.summary: Tests how LLMs anticipate that gambling or stock-trading outcomes would feel and whether those affective ratings influence choice. Models show human-like diminishing sensitivity to magnitude but rate gains more intensely than equivalent losses — an inversion of loss aversion termed silicon gain amplification — and the asymmetry drops out when ratings are compared jointly or in choice.

entry.title: LLM Detoxification via Transition-Aware Reward-Guided Representation Sampling

author.name: Aishan Liu, Yisong Xiao, Xianglong Liu, Yongxin Huang, Siyuan Liang, Zonghao Ying, Yang Qu, Jian Yang, Yaodong Yang, Dacheng Tao

entry.summary: TARGRS is a test-time detoxification framework that learns reward guidance over transitions between toxic and non-toxic states in latent representation space, converting sparse toxicity annotations into dense listwise supervision via progressively steered trajectories. This improves on static representation steering methods that provide imprecise guidance. It contributes to safer LLM deployment without retraining the base model.

entry.title: From 1D Benchmarks to Complex 3D Geometries: Can Agents Reliably Specify Problems for Automated PDE Simulation?

author.name: Akshat Jani, Sakhinana Sagar Srinivas, Venkataramana Runkana

entry.summary: This work studies whether LLM agents can reliably convert engineering requests into complete executable JSON specifications for automated geometry creation, meshing, PDE solving, and result export on complex 3D geometries, using deterministic scientific checks, explicit clarification, and validated local patches. It emphasizes that successful execution alone does not establish specification correctness. This probes a key reliability question for AI-driven scientific simulation.

entry.title: From the Zoo to the BULLPEN: Sample-Efficient LLM Profiling via Multi-Channel Model Embeddings

author.name: Russell Ro, Qiming Cui, Reza Abbasi-Asl

entry.summary: Introduces BULLPEN, a method for building compact LLM model embeddings that capture behaviors like verbosity, safety, and style rather than only correctness patterns, enabling prediction of many model properties from a fixed-length vector. This reduces the cost of profiling among the huge pool of available models. Useful for practical model selection at scale.

entry.title: Multimodal In-Context Learning with Explicit Rule Induction

author.name: Yuquan Li, Xinyang Jiang, Yuhao Xue, Cairong Zhao

entry.summary: Proposes ERIM, a framework for multimodal in-context learning that explicitly induces latent rules from demonstrations with dedicated supervision and rule-centric datasets, leveraging multimodal LLM reasoning rather than treating MICL as direct input-output mapping. This improves both performance and interpretability on ill-defined tasks requiring rule discovery. Contributes to understanding and improving in-context generalization.

entry.title: Optimizing Stochastic Policy Geometry for Few-Step Flow Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Zhuguanyu Wu, Congjia Chen, Ruihao Gong, Yang Yong, Shiqiao Gu, Yi Xu, Xianglong Liu

entry.summary: Introduces Geo-FSRL, which selects the admissible stochastic policy for GRPO-based few-step flow model reinforcement learning by minimizing the conditional KL divergence at fixed state-timestep pairs, resolving an underdetermined policy choice in prior constructions. It targets efficient RL post-training of diffusion/flow generators with few denoising steps.

entry.title: CLIC: Closed-Loop Intent Consistency for Securing LLM-Driven Control in Open RAN

author.name: Sunder Ali Khowaja, Kapal Dev, Joongheon Kim, Angelos Antonopoulos, Nikolaos Bartzoudis

entry.summary: CLIC targets security of LLM-driven control in Open RAN, addressing runtime prompt injection through the RAN Intelligent Controller and residual virtual prompt injection attacks planted during fine-tuning. It enforces intent consistency across the full control path rather than addressing only the runtime threat. This extends LLM security concerns into telecom infrastructure control loops.

entry.title: MUON-RT Reusing the Teacher's Trajectory for Momentum-Free Muon for LLM Self-Distillation

author.name: Aryan Das, Vinay Kumar Verma, Aakansha Mishra

entry.summary: Muon-RT eliminates the separate momentum buffer in the Muon optimizer during EMA-teacher self-distillation by reusing the teacher-student displacement, which provably encodes an exponentially weighted update history. The method removes the radial component, spectrally normalizes, and mixes with the post-Newton-Schulz gradient, with convergence analysis under stated assumptions. This reduces persistent training memory for LLM self-distillation runs.

entry.title: Implicit Assumptions About Tasks in Continual Learning

author.name: Kathrin Korte, Christian Metzner, Akshay Bedhotiya, Viet Anh Khoa Tran, Eleni Nisioti, Sebastian Risi

entry.summary: Analyzes how continual learning measurements implicitly conflate task definitions at the data, partition, and learner levels, and separates which properties acquire value at each level. Shows through controlled experiments that these levels do not coincide, affecting interpretation of reported results. A conceptual cleanup of a foundational assumption in continual learning benchmarking.

entry.title: Near-Optimal Second-Order Convex Finite-Sum Optimization under Individual Smoothness

author.name: Xinliang Zhang, Lesi Chen, Zonghan Li, Jingzhao Zhang

entry.summary: The paper proves a tighter lower bound for stochastic second-order optimization of convex finite-sum problems under individual smoothness assumptions and introduces a Taylor-corrected lazy Newton method achieving near-optimal complexity, improving on recent minimax results under averaged smoothness.

entry.title: Fair Recommender Systems for Intersecting Groups

author.name: Christine Ling, Juba Ziani

entry.summary: The paper studies dynamic recommendation with demographic groups that can intersect, proving any group-blind policy incurs linear regret, and introduces three group-aware UCB-based algorithms, including Intersection-Fitting, with sublinear group- and intersection-level regret guarantees.

entry.title: When can Optimally Trained Transformers Achieve Near-Lossless Token Prediction for non-Markovian Data?

author.name: Ka\u{g}an Akman, Jake Feldman Starosta, Naci Saldi, Serdar Y\"uksel

entry.summary: This paper develops mathematical theory explaining why Transformers succeed at next-token prediction on non-Markovian data, framing training as stochastic optimal control. It derives error bounds for stationary ergodic sources via an entropy gap and shows exponential decay in window length for finite-order Markov sources. This provides rare formal grounding for Transformer empirical success beyond Markovian settings.

entry.title: NormDetect: Anchored Calibration for Low-False-Positive Detection of Machine-Generated Web Text

author.name: Hanshuai Cui, Fanshuai Meng, Zhiqing Tang

entry.summary: NormDetect improves zero-shot AI-text detection for web platforms operating at very low false-positive rates. Building on Unicode normalization and Falcon-7B-based scoring, it anchors a learned calibration to recover machine text that homoglyph-style adversarial edits push into the human range, outperforming baselines like Binoculars at strict FPR.

entry.title: From fleet trajectories to single-cell promises: hierarchically weighted conformal prediction for battery SOH monitoring

author.name: Xiangyu Liu

entry.summary: The paper shows that pooled conformal prediction coverage on nested battery data reflects fleet averages rather than per-cell guarantees: pooled coverage looks healthy around 0.875-0.906 while the worst cell is covered only 0.1-2 percent of the time. It proposes a hierarchically weighted conformal engine using only prediction-time side information, which passes a preregistered repair criterion improving worst-cell coverage.

entry.title: Task Vectors Can Be Linearly Decomposed into Interpretable and Controllable Components

author.name: Yukiya Horiba, Hakaze Cho, Takahiro Yakoh

entry.summary: The authors decompose task vectors used to steer LLMs into Task Recognition, Task Learning, and residual components derived from candidate-label unembeddings, and use Bayesian optimization to tune component coefficients for more effective interventions. Evaluations span multiple model families and tasks, providing a finer-grained functional view of task vectors.

entry.title: Fast Privacy Loss Accounting for Random Allocation via Multiscale FFT

author.name: Vitaly Feldman, Moshe Shenfeld

entry.summary: Improves the privacy loss distribution accountant for the random allocation sampling scheme using a multiscale FFT algorithm that grids likelihood ratios uniformly within dyadic intervals, improving running-time dependence on the accuracy parameter while preserving guarantees. This speeds up tighter privacy accounting for private optimization and aggregation.

entry.title: Model-Agnostic Search for New Physics in the Presence of Imperfect Background by Smearing the Data

author.name: Soheun Yi, John Alison, Mikael Kuusela

entry.summary: Proposes MASSIB, a method for model-agnostic new-physics searches in high-energy physics that relaxes assumptions on both signal and background simultaneously by learning density ratios against a misspecified background distribution with data smearing. This addresses a gap where methods weakening one assumption typically require strong knowledge of the other.

entry.title: Adaptive Uncertainty Quantification on Simplicial Complexes with Conformalized Simplicial Neural Networks

author.name: Lekun Wang, Jaidev Goel, Yulia R. Gel, Yao Xie

entry.summary: Proposes CF-SNN, a conformal prediction framework for simplicial neural networks that generates prediction sets for all targets on a simplicial-complex entity simultaneously, with guaranteed per-target coverage under mild assumptions. This fills a gap in rigorous UQ for higher-order relational prediction.

entry.title: BYOD: Build Your Own DLM - Efficient Autoregressive-to-Diffusion Language Model Conversion

author.name: Ruurd J. A. Kuiper, Robert A. Bagheri

entry.summary: BYOD presents a LoRA-only recipe for converting pretrained autoregressive language models into diffusion language models without architecture-specific tuning or full pretraining, working on Gemma 2 9B, Llama 3.1 8B, Qwen2.5 7B, and Ministral 8B. Adapters comprise 4.1-5.8% of parameters with all base weights frozen, and each conversion takes 3-4 hours on modest compute.

entry.title: Adaptive Personalization Under Preference Epistemic Uncertainty

author.name: Priyanka Dey, Rajarshi Das, Vikas Bahirwani, Qi Zeng, Julia Kruk, Qi Qi

entry.summary: Formalizes adaptive personalization for conversational AI when human preferences remain valid, become uncertain, or are explicitly revised over time, backed by a human preference study showing people favor state-contingent strategies. The authors build a multilingual benchmark spanning 250 personas, 5 languages, and 25K turns that decouples strategy selection from response execution.

entry.title: TraceSpec: Understanding and Improving Speculative Decoding for LLM Agents

author.name: Jihao Zhao, Shuaishuai Zu, Pengfei Li, Biao Qin, Guanghuan Fang, Ben Feng, Baochuan Yang

entry.summary: Presents TraceSpec, a framework connecting trajectory-level evaluation with adaptive draft training for speculative decoding in LLM agents, combining dynamic execution with fixed-prefix replay and a corpus of 10,000 training and 2,500 test states across browsing and software engineering. Analysis of five baselines reveals aggregate acceptance metrics can hide phase-specific declines, informing where draft supervision is needed.

entry.title: Flide: Accelerating Decision Inference with Exact State Forking

author.name: Bobo Li, Jiajia Song, Hao Fei, Wynne Hsu, Mong Li Lee

entry.summary: Flide is an inference engine for decision models (as in the Jev/System One paradigm) that decouples the logical tree of a decision request from its physical execution in a flattened token stream, using ForkAttention with GPU-resident indices across standard attention and recurrent Gated DeltaNet layers to avoid prefix recomputation while preserving exact output probabilities. This targets a genuine gap in serving decision-model workloads. It complements the decision-model inference line of work represented in this batch.

entry.title: Segment Anything Pancreas: A Unified MRI Segmentation Model for Pancreatic Cancer Radiotherapy

author.name: Zach Eidex, Mojtaba Safari, Kundan Thind, Parag J. Parikh, Zhen Tian, Xiaofeng Yang

entry.summary: Pancreas-MedNeXt is a unified model segmenting the whole pancreas, subregions, tumors, and organs at risk from a single MRI volume, using shared pretraining and multitask fine-tuning with three output heads. An annotation-aware loss enables training on partially labeled data without treating unannotated structures as background.

entry.title: Beyond Trial-and-Error: A Geospatial-Guided Active Reasoning Framework for Robust Aerial Vision-and-Language Navigation

author.name: Jiawei Ge, Wenkang Gong, Jiuxin Cao, Bo Liu, Lei Cui, Haoran Wang, Xuelin Zhu, Biwei Cao, Chang Liu, Chen Feng, Ioannis Patras

entry.summary: GeoReasoner addresses aerial vision-and-language navigation for UAVs by exploiting stable geospatial structure rather than purely reactive local-observation updates, which are prone to distractor-induced errors. It shifts the aerial VLN paradigm from passive trial-and-error toward geospatially guided active reasoning.

entry.title: FoAViS: Analyzing Learned Fixation Strategies in a Foveated Active Vision System

author.name: Valentin Hassler, Jonathan Henrich, Yoha\"i-Eliel Berreby, Haoze Zhu, Alexander Ecker

entry.summary: FoAViS presents a foveated active vision system that samples with human-like resolution falloff, supports tasks from classification to dense prediction, and trains concurrently with a learned fixation policy. It enables systematic study of emergent gaze characteristics that can inform understanding of biological vision.

entry.title: Inter-Frame Predictive Contour Coding for Semantic Map Compression

author.name: Runyu Yang, Hyomin Choi, Fabien Racap\'e, Ivan V. Baji\'c

entry.summary: The paper proposes a lossless compression framework for dynamic semantic maps that exploits temporal correlation between adjacent frames, predicting blob positions, labels, and contours from a reference frame with a mode selection mechanism. This targets storage and transmission costs for semantic maps used in downstream vision applications.

entry.title: PBSR: Pseudo-Burst Super-Resolution via Zero-Shot Novel View Synthesis

author.name: Yuki Kondo, Norimichi Ukita

entry.summary: PBSR enables burst-style super-resolution from a single image by synthesizing pseudo-burst frames with realistic parallax via zero-shot novel view synthesis, with viewpoint sampling calibrated to real burst datasets. This extends BSR-quality reconstruction to archival photos where multi-frame capture is impossible.

entry.title: A Capability-Aware Backup-Recoverability Filter for Heterogeneous Multi-Robot Navigation

author.name: Joonkyung Kim, Yanze Zhang, Wenhao Luo, Yiwei Lyu

entry.summary: CA-BRF addresses decentralized safe navigation for heterogeneous multi-robot teams where differing braking and turning capabilities can make local collision-avoidance constraints infeasible. The method requires navigation actions to preserve access to a certified recovery maneuver, constructing a backup-recoverable set in a shared Cartesian operational space. It resolves a real failure mode of decentralized safety controllers in mixed-capability fleets.

entry.title: SAFARI: Semantic- And Frontier-driven Autonomous Risk Inspection

author.name: Ugur Kafkasyali, Mihnea Toader, Julia Richter, Turcan Tuna, Cesar Cadena, Marco Hutter

entry.summary: SAFARI is a framework for autonomous robotic exploration in hazardous environments that treats object detection as a native channel of a unified probabilistic map, coupling semantic detection with operating risk rather than optimizing purely for geometric coverage or information gain. It is validated in complex, unstructured field settings, addressing a gap where most risk-aware exploration work stays in simulation. Relevant to disaster response and industrial inspection.

entry.title: Flexibility-Aware Robotic Manipulation: Deformation Estimation, Kinematics, and Control via Distributed Inertial Measurement

author.name: Amir Hossein Barjini, Sadeq Yaqubi, Pauli Mustalahti, Jouni Mattila

entry.summary: This paper presents a framework connecting structural dynamics of flexible robot links to sensing, kinematics, and control. It derives a minimum observable IMU configuration, showing that m dominant vibration modes need only m slope measurements plus one reference IMU, and uses these measurements to reconstruct continuous link deformation. This addresses the breakdown of rigid-body assumptions in large flexible manipulators.

entry.title: How a group that cannot communicate knows itself by its enemy

author.name: Gregory Falco

entry.summary: This theory paper shows that teams of agents who cannot communicate can learn each other's private information by observing how a common adversary reacts to the group as a whole - the adversary's reaction acts as a tell equivalent to a message from every member. The analysis characterizes when a committed team strategy never loses and when it matches fully informed performance based on the opponent's incentives to hide. Applicable to silent multi-robot hunts, jammed robot teams, and adversarial settings.

entry.title: SERIAL-7: Deriving, Realizing, and Preserving Machine-Verifiable Outputs Across Representations

author.name: Youngkyung Seo, MiHyeon Kim, Jisoo Lee, Hwijung Ryu

entry.summary: SERIAL-7 is a Korean-English benchmark with an executable verification framework covering machine-verifiable generation across seven representations, using 177 validated canonical artifacts and 43 atomic representation constraints with executable checks. It separates three capabilities: semantic derivation, constrained artifact generation, and cross-representation preservation. This targets the gap where semantically plausible structured outputs fail downstream execution.

entry.title: When Can Unlabeled Data Pools Replace Membership Queries?

author.name: Dravyansh Sharma

entry.summary: The paper characterizes when a pool learner restricted to labeling sampled points can match the near-optimal label complexity of membership-query learners for halfspaces, giving an angular-law condition under which pools achieve strong uniform label bounds without density, moment, concavity, or isotropy assumptions.

entry.title: Intervention-Conditioned Counterfactual Human Digital Twin Generator

author.name: Saeed Farzi, Sofia Michopoulou, Christopher Kipps, Rahman Attar

entry.summary: Proposes CHDT, an intervention-conditioned human digital twin generator for multimodal longitudinal patient trajectories that handles irregular visit intervals and cross-mediator dependencies, targeting counterfactual trajectory estimation under alternative interventions for in silico clinical trials. It operates under standard causal identification assumptions.

entry.title: Language Models Show Conformity Bias in RAG: When the Majority Endorses a Poisoned Claim

author.name: Mehrdad Ghassabi, Audrina Ebrahimi, Zahra Zojaji, Amin Milani Fard

entry.summary: Tests whether the number of mutually agreeing poisoned documents in retrieved contexts affects misinformation detection, using SciFact questions with Gemma-3-12b. Detection rates drop from 25% with a single poisoned document among healthy ones to 10% when six poisoned documents agree, indicating a conformity effect in RAG robustness.

entry.title: SCRBench: Beyond Equivalence Checking for Semantic Change Reasoning in Code

author.name: Omid Saghatchian, Ali Mahzoun, Khashayar Etemadi, Saeed Reza Kheradpisheh

entry.summary: SCRBench introduces two new code-reasoning tasks, diagnosing which code change caused a semantic difference and reconstructing sequences of changes, alongside equivalence detection, using 67,658 Python program pairs with controlled semantic properties. Evaluations of five language models on 4,500 stratified pairs probe whether models understand the causal structure of code changes, not just yes/no equivalence. This deepens the evaluation of program understanding.

entry.title: FlowMoDE: Coarse-to-fine Flow Matching for Detail-aware Sim-to-Real Monocular Depth Estimation

author.name: Liangjing Shao, Wanhao Liu, Jinsong Lin, Zhiwei Fang, Hongliang Ren

entry.summary: FlowMoDE uses a coarse-to-fine flow-matching framework for monocular depth estimation, aiming to combine the fine structural detail and generalization of generative models with single-step inference efficiency. It targets sim-to-real and cross-scene generalization for robotic 3D perception.

entry.title: Geometry-Aware Humanoid Retargeting via Manifold ODEs

author.name: Pengyu Zhu, Heye Wang, Xi Wang, Xuyang Wu, He Kong, Guodong Shi

entry.summary: This paper recasts interaction-preserving human-to-humanoid motion retargeting, previously handled by framewise SQP optimization (e.g., OmniRetarget), as an ODE on the robot configuration manifold given by the continuous-time limit of framewise KKT conditions. This yields convergence guarantees for the SQP iterations and a more efficient ODE-based solver. A theoretically elegant improvement to a practically important retargeting pipeline.

entry.title: Incongruence-Aware Evaluation of Multimodal Speech Emotion Recognition in Audio Large Language Models

author.name: Fengji Jing, Guy Laban

entry.summary: Investigates whether disagreement between the textual content and vocal tone of speech degrades emotion recognition in audio-capable LLMs. The authors map text and audio into a shared valence-arousal-dominance space, derive a continuous incongruence score via Gaussian mixture modeling, and show it consistently raises error odds across three corpora when audio is present.

entry.title: Violet Teaming in Practice: Lessons from a Pilot Expert Workshop on Governing Complex AI Systems

author.name: Steph Batalis, Kait Connors, Ben C. Snyder, Vikram Venkatram, Josh Wentzel

entry.summary: Documents a pilot expert workshop applying violet teaming — integrating technical, policy, and societal perspectives into technology evaluation — to biodefense-relevant AI capabilities. A three-stage scenario exercise (capability development, misuse potential, implementation) yielded observations on how to examine benefits, misuse risks, and implementation challenges in an integrated governance process.

entry.title: Differential rank preservation manifold learning

author.name: Henry Han, Luyu Niu, Diane Li, Jiacun Wang

entry.summary: The paper introduces SR-tSNE, which adds a differentiable sigmoid-approximated rank term to the standard t-SNE loss so that the ordering of neighbors, not just the neighbor sets, is preserved in embeddings. It also proposes Ordinal DLP, an extension of the Degree of Locality Preservation metric that credits rank preservation. This matters because many downstream applications depend on neighbor ordering, which UMAP and t-SNE do not guarantee.

entry.title: TRIDENT and SHAKTI: A Framework and Benchmark for Hindi AI-Text Detection

author.name: Shifali Agrahari, Sujit Kumar, Sanasam Ranbir Singh

entry.summary: SHAKTI is a large-scale Hindi benchmark for distinguishing human-written from AI-generated text, covering four genres, eight LLM families, multiple prompting strategies, and adversarial transformations, with human annotation-based quality validation. TRIDENT is a round-trip translation-based detection framework with three variants built on the findings. This addresses the English-centric bias of AI-text detection research for a low-resource language with hundreds of millions of speakers.

entry.title: Self-Improvement with Auxiliary Rewards: Learning from Verified Traces and Evaluating Transfer

author.name: Minju Gwak, Alan Ritter

entry.summary: The paper studies whether auxiliary trajectory-level preferences improve self-improvement of small language models when answer-level rewards cannot distinguish equally correct reasoning traces, comparing confidence-based and entropy-based metrics (UID-Conj.) through online reward augmentation and offline training on verified correct responses. Experiments adapt Qwen3-1.7B on a small set of AIME problems and evaluate transfer, with UID-Conj. improving over TTRL by about 2 points. This targets efficient self-improvement under limited supervision.

entry.title: Do Transaction Prices Reflect Visual Preference? A Diagnostic Study with Multimodal Language Models

author.name: Fengxian Ji, Jingpu Yang, Fan Zhang, Junhong Liang, Qian Jiang, Yuke Li, Jinri Guo, Rongxin Zhu, Zhuohan Xie

entry.summary: Introduces MarketImage, a diagnostic framework for determining when marketplace transaction prices can serve as low-cost supervision signals for visual preference, accounting for confounds like demand and provenance. It evaluates whether multimodal language models can recover human-supported visual preferences from price data. This matters because it clarifies when behavioral economic data can substitute for expensive human annotation.

entry.title: Patch-Based Deep Kernel Learning for Data Assimilation and Bias Correction with Extremely Sparse Observations

author.name: Emanuele Mele, Angelo Coluccia, Massimo Cafaro, Italo Epicoco, Paola Nassisi

entry.summary: Proposes a patch-based deep kernel learning method for data assimilation and model bias correction in weather and oceanography, capturing state-dependent correlations and systematic biases that classical variational methods like 3D-Var cannot, while retaining interpretability and calibration properties. Targets extremely sparse observation coverage. Bridges classical geoscience estimation and modern deep learning.

entry.title: Sensorium: An Open-Source Multimodal Data Collection and Curation Library for Embodied Surgical AI

author.name: Lorenzo Mazza, Ariel Rodriguez, Stefanie Speidel

entry.summary: Releases Sensorium, an open-source Python library for recording, processing, annotating, and curating multimodal surgical data from robot and sensor streams via ROS/ROS2, evaluated across 1516 recordings of phantom, ex vivo, and in vivo porcine experiments. It addresses the costly, hardware-dependent nature of surgical data collection for embodied surgical AI.

entry.title: CausalGrade: Evidence-Guided Causal Graph Scoring with Jev

author.name: Jiangming Zhong, Jiawei Zhu, Guanting Wu, Qiaoxi Cai, Wanyi Chen, Jiale Li

entry.summary: CausalGrade addresses scoring candidate causal graphs when ground truth is unknown by combining observational evidence (association, conditional dependence, directionality) with edge probabilities from a causal discovery foundation model. A probabilistic judgment model called Jev produces edge-level judgments whose agreement with the candidate graph yields a graph-level score. Evaluation spans 300 synthetic datasets.

entry.title: TSFLab: A Self-Improving Agent-Agnostic Workbench for Time Series Forecasting Research

author.name: ChengAo Shen, Yanjun Zhao, Haoxin Liu, Bonnie Chen, Miles Ma, Dongjin Song, Hanghang Tong, Qingsong Wen, Jingrui He, Jingchao Ni

entry.summary: TSFLab is an agent-agnostic workbench that uses AI agents to benchmark time series forecasting research and support autoresearch such as developing new TSF models, motivated by the fact that only about 20% of surveyed arXiv TSF papers release code. It is designed to overcome high costs and limitations of directly applying coding agents like Claude Code and Codex. The workbench aims to standardize reproduction and maintenance of TSF methods.

entry.title: WebOverlay: High-Throughput Vision-Only Distillation for Extreme Aspect-Ratio Web Overlay Detection

author.name: Jiannan Huang, Jerry Ding, Li Yu, Zhenting Li

entry.summary: This paper presents WebOverlay, a lightweight vision-only detector that identifies web overlays like cookie banners and age gates that obstruct automated crawling. It uses distillation from a frontier vision-language teacher and a dynamic tiling strategy to handle full-page screenshots with extreme vertical aspect ratios, where standard resizing destroys text features. It matters for web-scale data ingestion pipelines that need cheap, fast overlay filtering.

entry.title: Coarse3D: Controllable and Faithful Sparse Structure Generation for Image-to-3D

author.name: Gaige Wang, Bowen Pan, Hao Ren, Jiangjing Lyu, Chengfei Lyu

entry.summary: Coarse3D improves the first stage of coarse-to-fine image-to-3D generation by producing orientation-controllable, image-faithful voxel structures from unposed images. It introduces a first-frame anchored canonical space and designs that strengthen 2D-3D grounding, fixing ambiguous canonicalization and structural inconsistency in prior coarse generators. Better sparse structures should improve the whole 3D-native generation pipeline.

entry.title: Sparse Text Diffusion under Dual Budgets: Context Connectivity and Expert Activation

author.name: Alexandros Christoforos, Chadbourne Davis, Paul Raj

entry.summary: Formalizes the compute costs of long-context text diffusion models as two separate budgets: attention-graph edges and activated experts per token, connecting local, dilated, and global attention with conditional expert computation. Derives graph and compute bounds, specifies normalized masked attention, and analyzes a DualBudget sparse-expert configuration across summarization, multi-hop QA, dialogue, and sentence-pair tasks. Offers a structured framework for reasoning about sparsity in diffusion LMs.

entry.title: SimXAI: A Simple Drop-in Layer Increases Interaction Quality and Understanding in Conversational XAI

author.name: Van Bach Nguyen, Qianli Wang, Nils Feldhus, J\"org Schl\"otterer, Christin Seifert

entry.summary: Presents SimXAI, a lightweight LLM-centric conversational layer that replaces multi-module GUS-style conversational XAI pipelines with a single tool-calling LLM providing access to external XAI resources. Introduces an evaluation suite covering single- and multi-turn parsing, faithfulness, and contextualization. Improves interaction quality and handling of context-dependent follow-up questions in explainable AI dialogues.

entry.title: MOSAIC: Addressing Disproportionate Task-Modality Dependencies via Modality-Partitioned Gradient Routing

author.name: Aryan Chowdhury, Yizheng Sun, Thomas Carroll, Riza Batista-Navarro

entry.summary: MOSAIC introduces modality-partitioned gradient routing for multi-task multimodal learning, explicitly modeling that individual tasks depend disproportionately on particular modalities so task gradients no longer contaminate parameters of unrelated modalities. This departs from conventional fusion architectures with a unified representation space.

entry.title: Localizing predictive concepts encoded in neural representations via hierarchical testing

author.name: Viktoriia Huryn, Marco Simnacher, Jim Berend, Wojciech Samek, Christoph Lippert, Sonja Greven, Uwe Ohler

entry.summary: The paper introduces CUTTIE, a cluster-tree unit testing method that identifies which units of a trained neural network encode human-understandable concepts with statistical error guarantees, applied to genomic deep learning models. Unlike exploratory or single-unit testing approaches, CUTTIE controls error across many sets of units via hierarchical testing. This supports trustworthy use of models in tasks like variant effect prediction.

entry.title: A Unified Framework for Probability Estimation of Data-Dependent Events

author.name: Vitaly Feldman, Satyen Kale, Vinod Raman, Kunal Talwar, Ambuj Tewari

entry.summary: This paper unifies the estimation of probabilities of data-dependent events, such as missing mass, adaptive data analysis targets, post-selection inference quantities, and test error of data-trained predictors, in a single framework. It analyzes the empirical plug-in estimator, whose error is exactly a generalization gap, and compares against other classical estimation approaches. This provides a common theoretical lens for several previously separate problems.

entry.title: What We Keep of What We Forget: Replacement Operators and Routing Semantics in Training-Free MoE Expert Pruning

author.name: Ezza Ali, Sehrish Bibi, Momina Moetesum, Faisal Shafait

entry.summary: This paper disentangles the two coupled decisions in training-free MoE expert pruning: which experts to remove and how the layer computes when a removed expert is selected by the router. Holding the mask fixed, it compares replacement operators across three families on OLMoE, DeepSeek-V2-Lite, and Moonlight with paired, multiplicity-corrected tests, finding the survivors' gate scale is the largest effect, with renormalization costing up to 8.5 points and reversing method rankings on some routers. This provides actionable guidance for MoE compression.

entry.title: Improving the Optimization Landscape of Matrix Completion with $\epsilon$-close Surrogates

author.name: Ziye Ma

entry.summary: The paper studies non-convex matrix completion and shows that injecting small epsilon-level perturbations into the nullspace of the observation mask yields noisy matrix sensing surrogates with improved optimization landscape. It mathematically connects noisy perturbations with over-parametrization in a classic recovery setting.

entry.title: FOCUS: First-Order Control Using Optimal Transport Supervision for Imitation from Observations

author.name: Jo\~ao A. C\^andido Ramos, Lionel Blond\'e, Hugues Vinzant, Jacopo Castellini, Alexandros Kalousis

entry.summary: FOCUS addresses imitation learning from state-only demonstrations by combining local optimal-transport alignment with short-horizon differentiable actor-critic learning in differentiable simulators. A soft best-of-K matching objective aligns rollout windows with expert segments, producing differentiable imitation rewards without requiring temporally aligned trajectories.

entry.title: Towards Out-of-Distribution Uncertainty Quantification for Machine-Learned Interatomic Potentials via Pre-Training

author.name: Stefan P. Schmid, Tobias Setzer, Maximilian Scheurer

entry.summary: Inspired by foundational MLIPs, the authors pre-train uncertainty quantification models on large, diverse materials datasets so that UQ generalizes across chemical space and can be applied to different interatomic potentials. They evaluate pre-trained UQ estimators on in-distribution and out-of-domain tasks, showing broader applicability than post-hoc methods trained in low-data regimes.

entry.title: When Does Jacobian Fine-Tuning Stabilize Neural PDE Emulators?

author.name: Shreeyam Bangera, Manya Gupta

entry.summary: Proposes a first-order decomposition separating physical error amplification from model-induced amplification in autoregressive neural PDE emulators, using a counterfactual Jacobian-propagation ratio. Across 21 configurations spanning four PDEs and five architectures, it characterizes when Jacobian fine-tuning reduces error growth at one Lyapunov time.

entry.title: Instance-dependent sequential limits as an exact information ledger

author.name: Akshay Balsubramani

entry.summary: Unifies proofs of instance-dependent limits for bandit regret, sequential testing, best-arm identification, and MDPs into a single exact chain from divergence decomposition through data processing to testing and optimization. The ledger formulation uses a one-parameter family of martingale identities to extend the decomposition across tilts and recovers classical limits.

entry.title: Combinatorial Residual Network: a decay-chain-aware classifier without explicit jet assignment

author.name: John Alison, Patrick Bryant, Alejandro Gomez Espinosa, Christian Guinto-Brody, Aniket Khanal, Chuyuan Liu, Sindhu Murthy, Guanglei Zhao

entry.summary: Introduces CoReNet, a neural classifier for high-energy physics that encodes assumed decay-chain structure directly in its architecture, evaluating jet-assignment hypotheses level by level with shared weights and residual networks. Symmetries are built in, network size is independent of hypothesis count, and explicit jet assignment is avoided.

entry.title: Meshless Latent Dynamics Models for Model Order Reduction of time-dependent Partial Differential Equations

author.name: Lorenzo Tomada, Federico Pichi, Gianluigi Rozza

entry.summary: Introduces a unified mathematical framework for mesh-agnostic latent dynamics models built on conditioning in neural fields, with a taxonomy of weak, strong, and pure conditioning mechanisms. Applied to model order reduction of time-dependent parameterized PDEs, removing the fixed-discretization constraint of autoencoder approaches.

entry.title: When AI Investigators Cannot Trust Their Tools: Conflict-Aware Evidence Verification for Cyber Threat Investigation

author.name: Yuchen Zhang

entry.summary: Studies what happens when LLM security-investigation agents receive conflicting or corrupted outputs from the detection tools they rely on, using corrupted detector labels on corrected CIC-IDS2017 data. Across open-weight LLMs from 3B to 14B, one corrupted detector out of four drops naive accuracy to roughly 0.5, showing fragility of unverified tool trust.

entry.title: Reliability-Weighted Direct Preference Optimization: Penalized Weights for Robust Preference Learning

author.name: Bin Luo, Param Venkat Vivek Kesireddy, Anil Vallepu

entry.summary: RW-DPO extends Direct Preference Optimization by assigning each comparison an unknown reliability weight in [0,1] estimated jointly with the policy under a minimax-concave penalty on the log-weight, keeping agreeing comparisons at weight one and down-weighting contradicted ones at negligible cost. The authors prove recovery of flipped comparisons requires margins of order log n and provide robustness guarantees.

entry.title: Learning Nonlocal Interactions in Large-Scale Heterogeneous Metamaterials through Scientific Machine Learning

author.name: Dex Doksoo Lee, Jehyeon Shin, Yue Yu, Sunkyu Yu, Junsuk Rho, Wei Chen

entry.summary: The paper presents DANO, a domain-decomposition attention neural operator that learns nonlocal interactions in multiscale metamaterial systems from data while tying network design to physical theory, without requiring prescribed analytic forms, ranges, symmetries, or periodicity. Applications span fracture mechanics, wave physics, and disordered systems, treating nonlocality as a design element.

entry.title: Qistas: A Pre-Registered, Portable Protocol for Fairness Evaluation of Large Language Models

author.name: Nawar S. Alseelawi, Mustafa S. Aljumaily

entry.summary: Presents Qistas, a pre-registered protocol for evaluating LLM treatment of a society's own social, confessional, and regional constituencies, instantiated first for Iraq, as an alternative to US-centric fairness benchmarks. It measures procedural symmetry across matched counterfactual pairs, differential refusal, stereotype reliance, and framing effects without requiring verdicts on contested truths.

entry.title: HyperRepair: Recovering Forgotten General Capabilities of Fine-Tuned Language Models

author.name: Junrong Tang, Jianghui Wang, Hao Kong, Yang Lin, Yibo Yang

entry.summary: Introduces HyperRepair, a framework that recovers general capabilities lost during domain fine-tuning while retaining specialization, at inference time only. A hypernetwork trained on source models uses activation fingerprints to generate a model-specific Repairing Side Net whose prompt-conditioned gate applies selective corrections, enabling generalization across models sharing a pretrained backbone.

entry.title: PsyInterviewee: Informational Invariance and Relational Adaptivity in Mental Health Interview Simulation

author.name: Jiawei Zhang, Huachuan Qiu, Ruocheng Guo, Zijun Shi

entry.summary: PsyInterviewee is an LLM-based simulated patient for mental health interviewer training that separates a protected truth channel from a dynamic interaction channel, verifying generated clinical claims against the patient profile. The framing of reliability as informational invariance plus relational adaptivity goes beyond the usual human-likeness objective. This improves the trustworthiness of simulated patients used for training and evaluating interviewing systems.

entry.title: RangeSWA: Training-Free Length Extrapolation for Continuous Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Guangfu Guo, Xiaoqian Lu, Linsey Pang, Weiran Yao, Haolin Chen, Long Cheng, Kunpeng Liu

entry.summary: RangeSWA is a training-free method enabling continuous diffusion language models to extrapolate beyond their training length by combining sliding-window attention, remote block summaries, dynamic retrieval, positional remapping, and stage-adaptive window scheduling. It mitigates repetition, semantic drift, and quality degradation during long generation. As a plug-in technique requiring no retraining, it is immediately applicable to diffusion LM deployments.

entry.title: Spatial Atlas-Informed Loss Ensembles for Whole-Body PSMA PET/CT Metastasis Segmentation

author.name: Grant N. Chau, Bashirul A. Biswas, Biratal Wagle, Matthew E. Maeder, Michael S. Leapman, James B. Yu, Indrani Bhattacharya

entry.summary: This work builds voxel-wise population metastasis atlases from 375 expert-annotated PSMA PET/CT scans and uses them to spatially weight nnU-Net training loss for prostate metastasis segmentation. The resulting SAILS ensemble is combined by majority voting and evaluated on validation data.

entry.title: RADI3N: GeometRic ImAge EDiting via ParametrIc 3D CoNtrol

author.name: Abdul Wasi, Akhil Gorugantu, Mahesh Bhosale, Anjan Dutta, Junsong Yuan, Sauradip Nag, David Doermann

entry.summary: RADI3N enables part-level, semantically grounded image editing with parametric 3D control, using a CS-ARAP deformation module that suppresses rotation-field discontinuities at part boundaries. It targets realistic appearance and texture under large geometry-intensive transformations that diffusion editors handle poorly.

entry.title: SketchDirector: Complex Scene Sketching via Agentic Layout Reasoning and Detail Refinement

author.name: Yiqi Liang, Xiaodong Cun

entry.summary: SketchDirector is an agentic framework for text-guided complex scene sketching that mimics human workflows: an LLM decomposes scenes into Bezier-curve draft assets, an iterative agentic loop plans spatial arrangement with self-evolving memory, and diffusion priors refine details. It moves beyond image-guided, single-object sketching.

entry.title: FlexReader: Towards Adaptive Decoding Paths for Efficient Arbitrary-Length Scene Text Recognition

author.name: Zhibin Ma, Pengwen Dai, Zhigang Yao, Xugong Qin, Wenqi Ren, Xiaochun Cao

entry.summary: FlexReader introduces a scene text recognition model supporting multiple decoding strides within a single trained model, using a Sub-string Perception module and parallel per-character decoding blocks. This decouples accuracy-efficiency trade-offs from the training paradigm, allowing one model to adapt to diverse deployment scenarios.

entry.title: Retrieval-Augmented Initialization with Dual-Guided Inversion for Flow-Based Inverse Problem Solvers

author.name: Hansam Cho, Seoung Bum Kim

entry.summary: RA-DGI improves flow-based inverse problem solvers by replacing random Gaussian noise initialization with a retrieval-augmented, dual-guided inversion scheme, systematically studying initialization while holding the solver fixed. Better initialization can meaningfully change reconstruction outcomes.

entry.title: PRIN: A Perceptual-Structural Retinex-Inspired Network for Low-Light Image Enhancement

author.name: Qiyi Xie, Wei Chen Ng, Ziyao Li, Yuning Wu, Huasen Wu, Tianshi Miao, Jian Ding Tan

entry.summary: PRIN is a low-light enhancement network that integrates Retinex decomposition with branch-specific frequency-domain refinement encoding the asymmetric restoration roles of reflectance and illumination. It aims to avoid over-smoothed textures, color shifts, and incoherent illumination common in learning-based methods.

entry.title: SemEllipsoid: Semantic-aware Shape Abstraction with Ellipsoid

author.name: Kuankuan Cheng, Haocheng Yuan, Changjian Li

entry.summary: SemEllipsoid adds semantic consistency to ellipsoid-based shape abstraction, ensuring primitives align with semantic parts rather than spanning multiple parts, which improves downstream part-level editing and manipulation tasks.

entry.title: TRACE: Target-State Risk-Aligned Conditional Execution for Embodied Tracking

author.name: Mingyang Lyu, Gongce Cao, Yiyang Jia, Lu Jia, Erliang Lin, Yuhao Zhang, Yinqian Sun, Pin Lyu, Feifei Zhao, Bo Wang

entry.summary: TRACE addresses embodied visual tracking of a language-specified person under occlusion and distractors, revealing that RL training (PPO on a 0.6B VLA planner head) improves tracking success but increases collisions because episodes that previously ended in target loss now end in contact. It introduces an execution-time risk gate that preserves the learned policy and intervenes selectively. The safety-performance coupling finding is a useful cautionary result for embodied RL.

entry.title: BioAgent: Self-Directed Skill Acquisition and Capability Growth for Long-Horizon Laboratory Protocols

author.name: Gaojing Zhang, Changwen Chen, Zichen Luo, Jialiang Li, Yuhan Wang, Yifei Xie, Wenzhao Lian

entry.summary: BioAgent is an embodied agent for executing unfamiliar laboratory protocols that matches human-reviewed requirements to validated skills, selects tool-based implementations for missing capabilities, requests human teaching when needed, and validates learned skills via sequential task-package checks with runtime precondition and state monitoring. It addresses the coupled problems of capability sufficiency and experimental validity over long horizons. Relevant to autonomous science and lab automation.

entry.title: GPU-accelerated Incremental Euclidean Distance Transform for Online Motion Planning of Mobile Robots

author.name: Yizhou Chen, Shupeng Lai, Jinqiang Cui, Biao Wang, Ben M. Chen

entry.summary: This letter presents a volumetric mapping system that computes occupancy grid maps and Euclidean distance transforms incrementally using GPU parallel computing. It maintains a global EDT while providing high-frequency local distance updates for online robot motion planning, integrating new sensor observations via a parallel wavefront algorithm. The work enables faster, real-time planning in dynamic environments.

entry.title: Language-Conditioned Behavioral Cloning for Autonomous Endoscope Guidance

author.name: Ariel Rodriguez, Lorenzo Mazza, Ortrun Hellig, Alejandra Toscano, Rayan Younis, Stefanie Speidel

entry.summary: The paper applies language-conditioned behavioral cloning to autonomous endoscope camera guidance in minimally invasive surgery, defining six clinically relevant guidance behaviors and collecting 235 subtask demonstrations. In phantom experiments the single visuomotor policy achieves strong success on focus, overview, and stop behaviors but weaker performance on search-tip and horizon leveling. This demonstrates feasibility of surgeon-intent-conditioned camera control from a single policy.

entry.title: Misalignment traps lie in wait

author.name: David Africa

entry.summary: This post argues that emergent misalignment findings (e.g., from insecure-code datasets) reflect a mundane but serious mechanism: highly sample-efficient models infer what kind of agent produced narrow training data and generalize broadly and unexpectedly, across pretraining, post-training, and potentially online learning. The author contends researchers over-dismiss these settings as toy, citing realistic triggers such as offensive-security Q&A data. The upshot is that misalignment-inducing data distributions are hard to avoid in practice, creating latent traps.

entry.title: SciGraphSelect: Auditable Scientific Data Selection through Knowledge--Reasoning Graphs

author.name: MiHyeon Kim, Ji-Eun Han, Eunkyeong Lee, Jeehyun Lim, Hwijung Ryu

entry.summary: SciGraphSelect is a reference-grounded framework for auditable scientific data selection that organizes domain knowledge, reasoning operations, and reference-attested relations into a typed knowledge-reasoning graph, scoring candidate documents by concept coverage, path co-support, and directional alignment while exposing the evidence behind each retention decision. This addresses the opacity of relevance-score-driven data curation. Explainable data selection matters for trustworthy AI-assisted science.

entry.title: Multi-Test Nation Bias Benchmarking of LLMs with Explicit Unbiased Baselines

author.name: Jonghyeon Choi, Yeonjun Choi, Beakcheol Jang

entry.summary: Benchmarks nation-level bias in LLMs for international relations applications using 722 UN Security Council records across five bias tests (ranking, association, vote simulation, opposition attribution, framing), with an explicitly defined unbiased reference baseline. This enables more quantitative, ground-truth-anchored bias measurement. Important for responsible deployment of LLMs in geopolitically sensitive contexts.

entry.title: ID2Pattern: Pretraining Generalizable Identity Behavior Patterns for Transaction Risk Foundation Models

author.name: Ze Zhao, Haoyu Jiang, Weiyu Han, Ruobing Zuo, Xiao Tan, Shuai Chen, Tianyi Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes ID2Pattern, a pretraining framework that encodes high-cardinality identity fields (card, device, account IDs) via Local Anonymous ID tokens capturing behavior patterns across transaction sequences, for transaction risk foundation models in payment systems. It sidesteps the vocabulary-growth and semantics problems of standard ID encodings.

entry.title: CAMEL: Cross-Architecture Masked Embedding Learning for Ultra-Lightweight Retinal Foundation Models

author.name: Andre Guarnier De Mitri, Giovani Decico Lucafo, Miller Matheus Lima Anacleto Rocha, Diego Furtado Silva

entry.summary: CAMEL uses cross-architecture masked embedding learning to build ultra-lightweight retinal foundation models, aiming to close the gap between RETFound-class foundation model performance and clinical scalability requirements. It distills rich representations into much smaller models suitable for deployment in ophthalmology screening. This targets accessibility of medical AI in resource-constrained settings.

entry.title: ProSearch: Benchmarking Multi-Constraint Protocol Retrieval in Experimental Science

author.name: Wenliang Liang, Zhiyuan Ning, Haolin Chen, Yuanchun Zhou, Wenjuan Cui, Yi Du

entry.summary: ProSearch is a benchmark for multi-constraint retrieval of experimental protocols in science, built from real experimental records with 60 fields, dependency-aware constraint selection, and 3-5 explicit constraints per query including numerical and negation constraints. It targets the underexplored capability of satisfying interdependent constraints during retrieval for experimental design and method reproduction. Construction combines LLM extraction with controlled verification.

entry.title: OT-CAL: Optimal-Transport-Guided Adaptive Sample Selection for Efficient Visual Learning

author.name: Suryansh Talukdar, Jin Soung Yoo

entry.summary: Proposes OT-CAL, a method that uses optimal transport to adaptively select informative training samples for backward passes as informativeness criteria shift over training, from difficult to improving to diversity-relevant samples. Avoids costly per-sample gradient computation and fixed selection rules. Aims to reduce training computation in image recognition without sacrificing accuracy.

entry.title: Generated storm lifecycles fill the rare-event tail of short rainfall records

author.name: Valerie Tsao, Nathaniel W. Chaney, Manolis Veveakis, Marta Zaniolo

entry.summary: StormGen is a generative machine-learning model that transforms the initial hours of an observed storm into complete, physically plausible hourly rainfall lifecycles within minutes, addressing the scarcity of rare-storm data. On a decade of southeast Texas rainfall, it produced close counterparts for a much larger share of the most severe storms than stochastic storm transposition while maintaining spatial coherence over 24-hour sequences. This helps infrastructure planning cope with increasingly frequent historically rare storms.

entry.title: When Links Mislead: Label-Free Structural Polarity for Zero-Shot Classification of Web Pages

author.name: Hanshuai Cui, Zhiqing Tang, Zhi Yao, Weijia Jia, Jun Luo

entry.summary: This work tackles zero-shot web page classification where LLM labels are noisy and hyperlinks can be misleading when linked pages differ in class. It introduces structural polarity, a label-free quantity readable from excess agreement of LLM labels among neighbors, which determines whether links should attract or repel in prediction, avoiding costly homophily estimation.

entry.title: Hyperbolic Inverse Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Iulia Rusu, Anoop Praturu, Sergei Gepshtein, Tatyana Sharpee

entry.summary: Proposes parameterizing IRL reward functions using hyperbolic distance between feature and parameter vectors, motivated by geometric organization observed in neural circuits, alongside a Euclidean distance variant. This brings explicit geometric assumptions into reward inference, aiming to improve predictive accuracy and interpretability.

entry.title: Co$^2$ODE: Conditionally Coarse-Grained Model Discovery for Rewiring in Biochemical Networks

author.name: Theodore de Pomereu, Fabian Fr\"ohlich

entry.summary: Co2ODE introduces conditionally coarse-grained ODEs for discovering how biochemical network dynamics rewire under context shifts, modeling only the rewired portion as a sparse neural or symbolic ODE with a conditional mask and a variational autoencoder. This sidesteps the poor identifiability of learning a full network from sparse, correlated measurements.

entry.title: Empirical Evaluation of Quantum Kernel Methods for Classification: A Comparative Study with Classical Kernels

author.name: Ronak Bhalgami

entry.summary: Argues that published disagreements on whether quantum kernels beat tuned classical kernels stem from uncontrolled comparison protocols, and imposes three controls: symmetric bandwidth tuning budgets, per-fold kernel recomputation, and cost accounting beyond simulator time. The study treats the comparison methodology itself as the object of analysis.

entry.title: Do Open Language Models Invent Scripture? BILAL-BENCH: Benchmarking Islamic-Source Fabrication in Bengali

author.name: Sabah Nushra, Md Kishor Morol

entry.summary: Introduces BILAL-BENCH, a 240-question expert-verified benchmark for open-ended Islamic-source fabrication in Bengali, covering Qur'anic attribution, hadith, fiqh, contemporary issues, and adversarial false-premise prompts with a two-axis rubric separating source errors from assertiveness. Evaluating seven open-weight models (1B to 120B) on 1,680 double-annotated responses finds six of seven confidently fabricate on 79.3-95.3% of cases.

entry.title: Stepwise-Querying: Distilling Reasoning without Access to Teacher Chain-of-Thought

author.name: Dicong Yu, Wenhua Wang, Tian Wang

entry.summary: The paper proposes Stepwise Querying, a black-box reasoning distillation method that elicits step-specific explanations, validity checks, and corrections from a teacher via independent queries, without access to the teacher's internal chain-of-thought. Assembled step-level solutions then supervise student fine-tuning. This expands the feasibility of reasoning distillation when teachers expose only final answers and brief solutions.

entry.title: Prior-Guided Single-Exposure HDR Novel View Synthesis via Base-Gain Representation

author.name: Armin Shafiee Sarvestani, Sheyang Tang, Jialu Xu, Zhou Wang

entry.summary: PriorGS is a 3D Gaussian Splatting framework for single-exposure HDR novel view synthesis that uses pseudo-HDR supervision and a base-gain representation to learn LDR-to-HDR reconstruction and camera response function priors without HDR ground truth. It addresses underconstrained supervision from LDR-only views.

entry.title: Hawkeye: Reading Illegible Text with Vision Language Models

author.name: Brian Tang, Kang G. Shin

entry.summary: The paper introduces BSTRB, an 8,398-sample benchmark for reading motion-blurred and low-resolution scene text from 1,699 real videos, plus Hawkeye, a fine-tuned VLM that reads illegible text using contextual priors and pixel-level alignment. It targets egocentric applications like smart glasses.

entry.title: DrawSplat: Atlanta World-Guided Implicit Gaussian SLAM for Indoor Reconstruction

author.name: Fan Zhu, Zhisong Xu, Ziyu Chen, Zhenjun Zhao, Takayuki Okatani

entry.summary: DrawSplat is an RGB-D SLAM framework for indoor scenes that first sketches structural layout with explicit point-line geometry guided by an Atlanta world assumption, then fills in details with implicit neural Gaussians. This improves tracking, rendering, and geometric consistency in weakly textured, planar-heavy indoor environments.

entry.title: ObjectGuidedMap: An Object-Aware Model for Robust Bird's Eye View Map Prediction in High-Occlusion Scenarios

author.name: Christian Bohn, Harsh Yadav, Klaus Friedrichs, Hasan Tercan, Tobias Meisen

entry.summary: The paper proposes a multitask BEV map prediction architecture built on Mask2Map that jointly predicts maps and 3D objects with explicit cross-task information exchange, leveraging the fact that traffic participants occlude and implicitly encode road geometry. This improves robustness in high-occlusion scenarios relevant to autonomous driving.

entry.title: AC-SMPC: Differentiable Actor--Critic MPC with State Constraints for Safe and Fast Robot Navigation

author.name: Chaoran Wu, Jiayu Fan, Qichen Tan, Yuyi Liu, Jin Wang

entry.summary: AC-SMPC is an actor-critic model predictive control framework that supports explicit state constraints within differentiable MPC layers, using vertex-based robot and obstacle representations, local linearization of dynamics, and convexified hyperplane collision-avoidance constraints. This enables learning-based navigation that handles collision avoidance explicitly rather than relying on penalty terms. It targets safe, fast navigation in confined dynamic environments.

entry.title: ROSTrans: Empirically Benchmarking LLMs for ROS1-to-ROS2 Migration

author.name: Yichen Zhao, Minghao Shao, Zhuoyan Yu, Yijun Shen, Boyuan Chen, Yik-Cheung Tam, Muhammad Shafique

entry.summary: ROSTrans is a benchmark of 108 scaffolded completion tasks for LLM-based migration of Robot Operating System code from ROS1 to ROS2, covering challenges like inter-node coordination, middleware configuration, and lifecycle semantics. Correctness properties only emerge at runtime when migrated nodes communicate, requiring launch-time evaluation. It fills a real gap in evaluating LLMs on robotics software engineering.

entry.title: Backpropagation-free Deep Learning for Time-Series Classification

author.name: Miha Kap\v{s}, Bla\v{z} Bertalani\v{c}, Carolina Fortuna

entry.summary: Adapts backpropagation-free learning rules (DFA, DRTP, and NoProp) to univariate time-series classification with 1D convolutional architectures, presenting the first systematic study across 112 UCR datasets. Optimized learners reach mean F1 of 0.76-0.79, below ROCKET at 0.83, showing a performance gap remains. Provides a useful empirical baseline for biologically plausible and parallelizable learning rules outside vision.

entry.title: SPT-Flow: One Integration, Many Futures in Continuous-Time World Models

author.name: Mingyang Lyu, Yinqian Sun, Gongce Cao, Yuhao Zhang, Lu Jia, Qian Zhang, Bo Wang, Pin Lyu

entry.summary: The paper diagnoses a supervision-shortcut failure in continuous-time world models: ground-truth intermediate states can make the model ignore stochastic conditioning, with posterior means varying only about 1% of the prior scale in a teacher-forced baseline. SPT-Flow addresses this by sampling one latent per trajectory and matching a free-running ODE rollout to demonstration states at multiple readout times. Re-anchoring experiments support the proposed mechanism, with evaluation on the LIBERO benchmark.

entry.title: Towards Understanding the Impact of Plasticity Loss on Reinforcement Learning in Stochastic Environments

author.name: Philipp Bordne, Andr\'e Biedenkapp

entry.summary: Systematically studies plasticity loss in deep RL under stochasticity, training SAC agents on three DeepMind Control tasks with controlled observation and action noise. It finds plasticity-preserving methods improve robustness on harder tasks with benefits growing with observation noise, and that combining resets with layer normalization can underperform resets alone.

entry.title: DeepWeave: Weaving Neural and Symbolic Evidence for ML-Based Network Intrusion Detection System

author.name: Raoul Saad, Enkeleda Bardhi, Andrea Agiollo, Fernando Kuipers

entry.summary: DeepWeave is a probabilistic neuro-symbolic network intrusion detection system that constructs and validates interpretable logic rules, treats neural predictions as probabilistic predicates, and reconciles both evidence sources through explicit coupling policies across packet-, flow-, and hybrid-views. The resulting proofs provide intrinsic explanations for rule-supported alerts while improving low-data detection performance across datasets.

entry.title: Task-Performance Routing for Multi-Teacher Distillation in CT Medical Image Segmentation

author.name: Jiaye Yang, Yao Liu, Die Dai, Hanwen Zhang, Peiyuan Jiang, Qiao Liu, Yutong Xie, Peng Wang

entry.summary: Task-Performance Routing (TPR) determines multi-teacher distillation weights for CT organ segmentation using region-wise segmentation errors, without learned routing parameters: favoring accurate teachers in hard regions and uniform weighting in easy ones. A hierarchical spatial partition varies routing granularity across encoder depth.

entry.title: SAR-TS-BERT: Physics-Guided Self-Supervised Pre-Training With Polarimetric Features for SAR Time-Series Crop Classification

author.name: Jieqiu Wang, Yuhan Zhang, Bo Zheng, Shaoming Zhang

entry.summary: SAR-TS-BERT is a BERT-style self-supervised pre-training framework for SAR time-series crop classification that integrates backscatter intensities and polarimetric ratio features with dual-polarization physics guidance. It reduces labeled-data dependency for agricultural monitoring in cloudy regions where optical imagery fails.

entry.title: DiRAFT: Privacy-Aware Financial Transcript Synthesis from Aggregate Discourse Priors

author.name: Yunbai Zhang, Yunyi Gao, Han-Tai Shiao

entry.summary: Presents DiRAFT, a pipeline for synthesizing privacy-preserving financial conversation transcripts by extracting concept graphs, pooling first-order transition statistics across records, and sampling new discourse plans from aggregate priors. This avoids reproducing individual conversation structure while aiming to retain discourse fidelity for training and evaluating financial language models.

entry.title: Payroll Fraud Detection in Synthetic HR/ERP Graphs: An Inductive Comparison of Rules, Path Features, and Graph Neural Networks

author.name: Xiaobo Chen, Genliang Zhu, Ziyuan Wang, Chu Wang

entry.summary: Formulates payroll-fraud screening as inductive link prediction and entity ranking on synthetic HR/ERP graphs with matched benign twins and unseen organizations, comparing analyst rules, explicit path features, and GNNs. A gradient-boosted model on chained-join features beat a GraIL-style GNN (AP 0.823 vs 0.663; 4-hop AP 0.646 vs 0.272), challenging assumptions about GNN superiority in multi-hop relational fraud detection.

entry.title: Online Evidence-Containment Prediction over Text Spans under Distinct Queries

author.name: Xiang Liu, Haochen Ding

entry.summary: Formalizes Online Evidence-Containment Prediction (OECP) for evidence-grounded NLP, showing span containment is a triangular 2D product order reducible to online isotonic regression, with near-linear worst-case regret in general and Theta(log m_eff) regret for single-target QA. Demonstrated on Natural Questions episodes. Provides theoretical grounding for efficient sequential verification of nested text spans.

entry.title: Advancing Clinical Trial Outcome Prediction with Domain-Specific Large Language Models

author.name: Burak Bakkar, Hana Moalla, Mohamed Salem Jedidi, Haifa Ben Messaoud, Nicolas Lopez Carranza

entry.summary: Evaluates BioBERT and BioMistral on phase-level clinical trial outcome prediction using the TOP benchmark (12,477 trials) with text built from ten ClinicalTrials.gov fields, comparing fine-tuning versus probing. Extends structured approaches like HINT by exploiting free-text trial registrations. Useful evidence on where domain-specific LLMs add value in drug-development prediction.

entry.title: Structure-Aware Skill Retrieval and Arbitration for Optimization Modeling

author.name: Anran Liu, Benzhao Hou, Zongsheng Cao, Daichao Wang, Lang Chen, Shitong Chen

entry.summary: Introduces ArchOR, an archetype-centric skill agent for turning natural-language optimization tasks into solver-checked answers, adding centroid-aware representation learning and signature-guided retrieval over cached skills with a baseline-preserving arbitration mechanism. It moves skill reuse from instance-level memory to robust archetype-level retrieval.

entry.title: Bayesian Distribution System State Estimation with Flow Matching

author.name: Nan Lin, Peter Palensky, Pedro Vergara Barrios

entry.summary: PoSE applies flow matching to distribution system state estimation in power grids, learning only the unknown distribution of substation injections while power flow equations, topology, and measurements are handled exactly. This preserves the Bayesian structure of DSSE rather than collapsing the prior to a mean and variance as in weighted least squares, or tying everything to a fixed measurement set as in supervised deep learning. It targets medium-voltage feeders with sparse real-time measurements.

entry.title: One Verdict Is Not Enough: Regression Testing Learned World Models and Their Test Harnesses

author.name: Junyu Huo, Zihao Wan, Ziqi Mao, Gouri Ginde

entry.summary: The paper presents TetraState, a regression-testing protocol for learned world models evaluated on paired possible/impossible video tests. It runs each test under four fixed model-native configurations, assigns four outcome classes, and separately reports inconclusive tests and harness faults that produce wrong verdicts without crashing. This brings software-engineering rigor to evaluating how world-model releases regress across versions and configurations.

entry.title: ORION: An Outcome-Driven LLM Advisor for RL-Based Multi-Domain 6G Slice Placement

author.name: Mahmoud S. Mayaleh, Fetia Bannour, Nour-El-Houda Yellas

entry.summary: Addresses NP-hard online placement of 6G network slices across administrative domains, showing empirically that no fixed planning strategy dominates across topology regimes. Introduces ORION, a hierarchical orchestrator where two LLM agents translate service intents and guide an RL-based placement layer. Demonstrates that the planning layer is the decisive performance lever in multi-domain 6G slicing.

entry.title: TensorSSM: Memorizing Spatial Position in Dynamic State Space for Tensor Core Generation

author.name: Sheng Zhang, Xinyi Wang, Maolin Wang, Xiangyu Zhao

entry.summary: TensorSSM is a state-space-based implicit neural representation for functional tensor decomposition that avoids flattening high-order tensors into 1D sequences, instead memorizing spatial positions within a dynamic state space to capture cross-mode dependencies and improve compression expressiveness.

entry.title: Omniprediction for All Mixable Proper Losses and Beyond

author.name: Junyan Liu, Haipeng Luo, Lillian J. Ratliff

entry.summary: This work studies omniprediction in online learning, asking whether sublinear regret is achievable when predictions must be simultaneously accurate under an infinite class of proper losses, extending prior results for finite loss classes. The authors establish new results on simultaneous regret guarantees against every predictor in a class and every mixable proper loss. This advances the theoretical foundations of multi-loss prediction.

entry.title: A Positional Realizability Theory of Length Generalization in Single-Head Attention

author.name: Jiasong Han, Yunkai Chai, Jintao Wang

entry.summary: The paper presents a realizability theory for length generalization in a single positional-only attention head, deriving the well-known empirical dependence on positional encoding type (relative vs. absolute) from first principles. It introduces a simulation transfer operator and a computable scalar witness that predicts where extrapolation holds or breaks before any training. This formalizes why growing offsets challenge existing positional schemes.

entry.title: Less Loss, Fixed Weights: Logit Corrections for Forgetting

author.name: Hanyu Yang

entry.summary: Investigates whether forgetting in fine-tuned language models can be undone with fixed output-layer adjustments, fitting per-token vocabulary biases and temperatures across 14 base/derived model pairs from 1B to 7B parameters. The study finds limited recovery — under 10% from top-4K biases alone, up to 36% with temperature — with math-pretrained models recovering almost nothing.

entry.title: Physiological Trajectories and Observation Patterns in ICU Mortality Prediction: Transportability Under Changing Measurement Conditions

author.name: Benjamin T. Pike

entry.summary: Disentangles whether ICU mortality prediction performance derives from physiological trajectories versus observation-pattern features (measurement frequency and timing), using nested representations evaluated across MIMIC-III, MIMIC-IV, and eICU with large patient counts and cross-dataset transfer. It assesses whether measurement timing affects performance independently of observation quantity.

entry.title: FGSM Attack Transferability from Simulation to Quantum Hardware in Network Intrusion Detection

author.name: Zeeshan Ajmal, Kimmo Halunen, Marc Mau{\ss}ner, Volker Reers, Arif Ali Khan

entry.summary: Tests the adversarial robustness of a hybrid variational quantum classifier for network intrusion detection under label-flipping and FGSM attacks, comparing simulation with real IBM Heron r2 hardware. Key finding: models with similar accuracy can differ sharply in attack susceptibility, with low-confidence models losing half their detections to small perturbations.

entry.title: Single-Annotation, Multi-Hypothesis Segmentation with Semantic-Spatial Residual Banks

author.name: Armin Dadras, Robert Sablatnig, Franziska Proksa, Markus Seidl

entry.summary: Formalizes the problem of returning multiple plausible segmentation masks when training data has only one annotation per image, revealing a tradeoff between image-learned banks (boundary variation) and frozen semantic features (structural grouping). The Semantic-Spatial Residual Bank combines a frozen semantic bank with a learned spatial residual bank to cover held-out annotator masks.

entry.title: Riemannian Optimization on Unknown Manifolds via Stochastic Proximal Refinement

author.name: Ruixiang Wu, Jiahao Ai, Tinko Sebastian Bartels, Xuanzhuo Liu, Yifei Wu, Yu Mao, Tongxin Li, Costas Courcoubetis

entry.summary: The authors study Riemannian optimization when the manifold is only accessible through feasible samples, without explicit tangent spaces, projections, or retractions. They propose PRISM, an iterative procedure that samples objective-aware distributions and refines proximal steps, addressing sparse representation of low-objective regions.

entry.title: Peeling the Matryoshka: Extracting Ontological Structure from Retrieval Embeddings

author.name: Eunchan Kim, Inwhee Joe

entry.summary: The paper reports that in Matryoshka Representation Learning embeddings, the leading prefix length aligns with coarse-to-fine granularity of gold taxonomies, with shuffled and reverse-dimension controls isolating the effect to learned early dimensions across three architecturally distinct models. The authors leverage this regularity to build taxonomy hierarchies without task-specific training, offering an alternative to costly clustering or LLM pipelines.

entry.title: Beyond Response Scoring: An AI-aware Cognitive Supervision Framework for Automated Mathematical Short Answer Grading

author.name: Shengran Guo, Min Chi, Feifei Qiao, Varad Patwardhan

entry.summary: This paper proposes AICG, a two-branch multi-task framework for automated grading of mathematical short answers that combines RoBERTa-based regression, ordinal, and classification heads with cognitive supervision. It addresses the limitation that score-only graders ignore skill states and the upward bias introduced when students use generative AI in their responses. The work matters for fair and informative assessment in education as AI-assisted answers become common.

entry.title: Agentic Systems for Calibrating Cosmological Simulations

author.name: Chaipat Tirapongprasert, Matthew Ho

entry.summary: AgenticTuner uses a present-day LLM as the optimizer proposing parameter trials for calibrating expensive cosmological simulations, exploiting informal human-readable priors such as codebase documentation and heuristic guides that black-box Bayesian optimization cannot consume. Agents achieve competitive calibration at a fraction of the CPU cost. It is an early signal for LLM-driven scientific simulation tuning.

entry.title: AVID: A Weakly Aligned RGB-Infrared Dataset and Perturbation Benchmark for Tiny Aerial Targets

author.name: Dharini Raghavan, Vishnu Rao, Sethu Selvi S

entry.summary: AVID is a benchmark of 32,040 RGB-infrared frame pairs from real bird-drone surveillance footage, with 35,952 annotations, specifically studying tiny-target detection under weak cross-modal alignment and quality perturbations. It was curated for the IEEE ICIP 2025 Video and Image Processing Cup.

entry.title: BDNet: Fast-slow thinking is all you need

author.name: Chenzhi Zheng, Zhuoran Zheng

entry.summary: BDNet is a hierarchical image classification backbone that uses fast image features against slow statistical reference buffers, computing baseline-relative residuals with linear token complexity rather than pairwise attention. A four-stage pyramid achieves a 20.7M-parameter classifier evaluated on ImageNet-1K.

entry.title: A Patch is More Than a Token

author.name: Zixiong Wang, Haiping Ma

entry.summary: PMTT proposes extending canonical ViT patch tokens to a canonical-centered Representation State Family of identity-preserving variations, opening a patch-level local feature space. It develops acquisition of dense orbital views, visible-to-hidden prediction, and intrinsic analysis of low-dimensional patch structure.

entry.title: IGDA-ICMH: an Importance Guided Feature and Network Dual Adaptation Framework towards Image Compression for Machine and Human Vision

author.name: Yanbo Gao, Xinyu Zhao, Shuai Li, Xun Cai, Mao Ye, Li Li
