entry.summary: FARMS transforms computational mathematics into AI-ready knowledge by linking formal statements to source context, algorithmic meaning, and quantitative guarantees through a pipeline of source preparation, reusable representations, and semantic review. Across 171 targets in randomized numerical linear algebra and numerical PDEs, 157 were accepted at low per-target cost, with learning experiments suggested in the abstract.

entry.title: Are Seismic Foundation Models More Than Glorified Feature Extractors?

author.name: Laura Laurenti, David Liu, Brian Kulis, Men-Andrin Meier, Christopher Johnson

entry.summary: This paper argues that seismic foundation models imported learning objectives from audio and vision that only capture fixed-window wave propagation, ignoring the sparse, self-exciting process that governs when earthquakes occur. The authors develop nine model designs sharing a single Mamba encoder-decoder to respect both timescales in one training objective, probing whether current seismic FMs are essentially feature extractors.

entry.title: From Error Prediction to Causal Influence: Auditing SAE Features in Multiple-Choice QA

author.name: Aria Nourbakhsh, Adelaide Danilov, Oleksandr Marchenko Breneur, Salima Lamsiyah

entry.summary: This interpretability study distinguishes correlation from causation in sparse autoencoder features associated with model errors on multiple-choice QA, analyzing Gemma 3 1B and 4B with Gemma Scope SAEs across eight datasets. The proposed pipeline filters features correlated with format and content artifacts such as prompt and answer permutation, then evaluates survivors via causal interventions on logit margins.

entry.title: Jailbreak Connectivity: Towards Diverse, Transferable, and Universal Multimodal Large Language Model Jailbreak

author.name: Xu Zhang, Ziqing Hu, Shuo Han, Ren Wang

entry.summary: The authors propose Jailbreak Connectivity, a visual jailbreak framework for multimodal LLMs that optimizes continuous adversarial paths through low-loss image regions rather than isolated adversarial examples. Path sampling produces diverse jailbreak images, surrogate classifiers guide cross-model transfer, and a distribution-level objective enables universal attacks, achieving 84-98% attack success rates on MM-SafetyBench against models including Qwen variants.

entry.title: Do Audio LLMs HEAR Pain? Tracing Acoustic Evidence from Speech to Language Reasoning

author.name: Wenqi Li, Xiangjue Dong, Sulaiman Vesal

entry.summary: The paper introduces HEAR, a four-stage diagnostic framework tracing how large audio language models use non-lexical acoustic information, applied to pain recognition across seven LALMs using the TAME-Pain dataset. The striking finding is that on Harvard sentences where pain must be inferred from voice alone, all models perform at chance, with references and few-shot examples improving accuracy by at most six points.

entry.title: Explore Where It Matters: Targeted Exploration for Efficient Rover Adaptation

author.name: Jacob Levy, Arthur Bouton, Tristan D. Hassler, Hari Nayar, David Fridovich-Keil

entry.summary: This paper introduces TERRA, an online adaptation framework for planetary rovers operating on deformable terrain where wheel slip and sinkage create sim-to-real gaps. TERRA adapts a simulation-trained world model using a reward-weighted prediction loss and trains a loss predictor to target exploration where performance-relevant model errors are likely. This matters because rover missions have extremely limited opportunity for trial-and-error learning.

entry.title: Distilling the Shape of Uncertainty: What On-Policy Distillation Learns and How to Predict It

author.name: Shiping Yang, Chuanqi Tang, Hossein Hajimirsadeghi, Layla El Asri, Mohammad Amin Shabani, Angel X. Chang

entry.summary: Shows that on-policy distillation transfers not only which tokens to branch on but also where in a sequence to keep reasoning paths open, introducing the entropy shape (the sequence of next-token entropies) and an Entropy Shape Correlation metric to measure student-teacher agreement. This reframes why stronger teachers sometimes fail to improve students and gives a predictive tool for distillation success.

entry.title: Learning to Formulate: Agentic Hardware-Software Co-Design of AI Infrastructure through Progressive Optimization and Verification

author.name: Yi Ding, Li Shang

entry.summary: Formulaic is a workflow in which an LLM agent writes the mathematical formulation of a hardware-software co-design problem, a solver optimizes within it, and verification and measurement check assumptions and results, progressively refining from computation graph toward jointly optimized designs. This lets agent-driven optimization cross layer boundaries that fixed formulations exclude.

entry.title: Turing LLM Post-Training: Calibrated Distillation and Efficient Dynamic-MoE Execution

author.name: Yue He, Jiahui Hu, Shaman Tang, Hua Zhou, Qiman Wu, Menglin Li, Yizhao Wang, Yuheng Zhang, Da Zhu, Zhou Wang, Anhua Liu, Hanlin Chen, Mingyuan Wang, Rui Xin, Yuhua Wei, Shuang Su, Siqi Liu, Kai Yang, Weichao Huang, Hang Zhang, Honggou Yang, Xianming Liu

entry.summary: The paper presents post-training methods for dynamically routed mixture-of-experts models, combining calibrated multi-teacher on-policy distillation (C-MOPD) with execution techniques including bounded-width dispatch, final-route replay, and asynchronous rollout-training overlap. On a 20B A2B model, the approach achieves a four-domain integration score of 0.9988, retaining over 90% of specialist gains.

entry.title: Scaling Mathematical Proof Supervision from Structured Textbooks

author.name: Youqing Fang, Zhouqi Hua, Yinhao Tang, Yuzhe Gu, Lingkai Kong, Bin Liu, Weiming Zhang, Kai Chen, Yanan Sun, Wenwei Zhang

entry.summary: The authors introduce TOME-Math, a corpus converting 2,118 university mathematics textbooks into roughly 380K structured proof-supervision records that preserve chapter order, proposition-proof links, dependency references, and provenance, and use these structural signals for curriculum learning and scaling analysis across mathematical subjects. Fine-tuning on the full corpus improves mathematical reasoning performance. It matters because high-quality, structured mathematical supervision data is a key bottleneck for LLM reasoning.

entry.title: Fast and accurate neural triage decoding of ultra-high-rate quantum LDPC codes

author.name: Hong-Ye Hu, Zhenlai Wang, Binzhao Luo, Tao Xiang, Chen Zhao

entry.summary: This arXiv paper introduces neural triage decoding, a method for decoding high-rate quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes with both high accuracy and low latency. It addresses a key practical obstacle to fault-tolerant quantum computing: qLDPC codes reduce physical qubit overhead, but existing high-accuracy decoders are too slow to keep up with quantum hardware, and neural decoders had not previously been demonstrated for this code class.

entry.title: TextSeal2: Distortion-Free LLM Watermarking with Copula Mixing and Memoryless Races

author.name: Tom Sander, Pierre Fernandez, Itai Gat, Haiming Bao, Jiaxin Shi, Jason Park, Valeriu Lacatusu, Sylvestre-Alvise Rebuffi, Hongyan Chang, Hady Elsahar, Tom\'{a}\v{s} Sou\v{c}ek, Tuan Tran, Surya Parimi, Alexandre Mourachko

entry.summary: TextSeal2 is a distortion-free watermark for large language models that remains effective under speculative decoding, preserves output diversity, and adds no measurable inference latency. It improves on TextSeal by merging multiple keys into a single virtual key coupled to fresh noise through a Gaussian copula, avoiding the detector's need to average scores from unknown keys.

entry.title: Improving Data-Constrained Scaling with Hyperparameter Transfer and Ensembling

author.name: Ethan Baron, Shmuel Berman, Anirudh Satheesh, Akshay Vegesna, Samip Dahal, Andrew Gordon Wilson

entry.summary: The paper addresses limitations of data-constrained LLM scaling prescriptions: fixed hyperparameters across scale and neglected ensembling, showing prior prescriptions can even yield loss that increases with compute budget. The authors fit power laws prescribing hyperparameter transfer with scale and incorporate ensembling as a scaling axis under data constraints.

entry.title: Separability Is Not Alignability: Representations for Spectrum-to-Molecule Retrieval

author.name: Karol Musielinski, Fanurs C. E. Teh, Takahiko Koyama, Artur Dubrawski

entry.summary: This paper audits the popular recipe of pretraining separate spectrum and molecule encoders and aligning frozen representations for tandem-mass-spectrometry molecule retrieval, on MassSpecGym with contamination-free retrained encoders. It proves that some predictive objectives fix molecular identity without fixing the metric needed for alignment, and shows candidate-based objectives reward degenerate solutions, separating representational separability from alignability.

entry.title: Nearly Minimax Optimal Regret for Adversarial Linear Bandits with Strong Corruptions

author.name: Qiwei Di, Quanquan Gu

entry.summary: This paper resolves an open question in adversarial linear bandits under strong corruption, proving a nearly minimax regret bound of roughly d*sqrt(T) + dC, improving the previous best leading term by a factor of sqrt(d). The analysis handles adaptive adversaries that corrupt rewards after observing actions, which breaks standard importance-weighted estimators.

entry.title: Loss is Not Behavior: A Unified Output-Space Analysis of Gradient-Based Machine Unlearning

author.name: Xingjian Zhao, Mohammad Mohammadi Amiri, Malik Magdon-Ismail

entry.summary: The authors derive closed-form expressions for the output-space gap between gradient-based unlearners and true retrained models, first in linear regression and approximately for nonlinear models via Gauss-Newton approximations. They show that optimizing forget and retain losses does not certify behavior matching retraining, and provide a unified parameterization of existing methods. This sharpens the theory of what machine unlearning actually achieves.

entry.title: Dobb: Shard-Local Preconditioning in Block-Diagonal Eigenbases

author.name: Shi-Yuk Fong, Shuhua Yu, Jiawei Zhang

entry.summary: Dobb is a matrix-aware optimizer for sharded language model training that performs preconditioning locally within parameter shards under tensor parallelism or FSDP, avoiding the communication overhead of global matrix operations needed by optimizers like Muon. It approximates the input-activation second moment with diagonal blocks and applies sign normalization to momentum projected into per-shard eigenbases.

entry.title: Accuracy is not compatibility: two Evo 2 checkpoints hinge on one FP8 matrix multiplication

author.name: Xun Ding (Independent researcher), Ziyuan Qin (Emory University)

entry.summary: This paper investigates why Evo 2 DNA language model checkpoints fail on hardware other than their target, tracing the failures to FP8 matrix multiplication behavior. Using a bit-exact H100 FP8 GEMM emulator called mmaemu, the authors localize the sensitivity to a single projection layer in the 1B checkpoint, showing that accuracy can paradoxically break checkpoints when hardware summation order differs from what the training stack assumed. The work exposes a fundamental gap between FP8 value storage semantics and unspecified accumulation behavior, with implications for checkpoint portability across GPU generations.

entry.title: Closing the Log Gap: Minimax-Optimal Regret for Episodic RL

author.name: Guy Zamir, Victor Boone, Matthew Zurek, Yudong Chen

entry.summary: Achieves the first expected regret bound scaling as sqrt(H^3 S A K) for episodic tabular MDPs, matching the minimax lower bound without extra polylog factors. The UCBVI variant uses MOSS-style exploration bonuses with adaptive logarithmic terms and handles under-optimism error propagation via occupancy-weighted analysis.

entry.title: A Pretrained Model for Bayesian Filtering in Heterogeneous Dynamical Systems

author.name: Ke Fan, Wen Wu, Haitao Su, Yilin Wang, Yuan Zhou, Chao Zhang

entry.summary: FilterFM is presented as the first pretrained foundation model for Bayesian filtering, estimating latent states across heterogeneous dynamical systems from a single checkpoint despite differing dynamics, scales, and noise levels. It uses a hierarchical two-level observation sequence encoder and prior design to enable a reusable shared representation for state estimation.

entry.title: The Endgame of FSDP Communication: Layout-Aware Collectives on Copy Engines, RDMA, and NVSwitch

author.name: Zejian Wang, Yifan Zhao, Kaihui Ren, Xiaoling Zhou, Yubin Wang, Chenhao Guan, Lin Zhang, Yufeng Li, Zhikang Mo, Zhuoru Ma, Yingtong Xiong, Jihu Guo, Yiqiao Liao, Chengru Song

entry.summary: The paper identifies that FSDP2's per-parameter tensor layout forces costly conversions to flat collective buffers, accounting for 6.4% of step time in Llama-3.1 70B training, and that default NCCL reduce-scatter can delay concurrent GEMMs by 69%. It introduces TIDE, zero-copy collectives built on public NCCL 2.31+ APIs that eliminate layout conversion while preserving per-parameter storage.

entry.title: ROAD: Modern Adversarial Training for Simple One-Step Distillation at Scale

author.name: Xiaoou Li, Shan You, Tao Huang

entry.summary: ROAD distills text-to-image diffusion models into fast one-step generators using a single adversarial objective with a lightweight representation-space critic, replacing convolutional critic heads with a Lipschitz-controlled Transformer head with token-level text conditioning. It demonstrates that pure adversarial distillation can work at modern text-to-image scale with far less machinery.

entry.title: Scoring Explanations Without Reading Them: Structural Shortcuts in Automated-Interpretability Evaluation Data

author.name: Xupeng Chen

entry.summary: Shows that standard automated-interpretability evaluation pipelines for SAE features can be gamed without reading the explanation: on Neuronpedia GPT-2 small fuzzing runs, 91.3% of activating examples are center-cropped, and trivial rules based on center-token marks or mark counts beat the stored LLM scorers (balanced accuracy 0.979 vs 0.838). This exposes serious structural shortcuts in how interpretability methods are scored. A cautionary result for the mechanistic interpretability evaluation ecosystem.

entry.title: Holistic Diversity Management in LLM-Guided Evolutionary Search

author.name: Seockbean Song, Youngsik Yoon, Sungjae Lee, Siwei Wang, Wei Chen, Jungseul Ok

entry.summary: The paper proposes HoliDivEvo, which manages diversity across the full lifecycle of LLM-guided evolutionary search, including island initialization, trajectory development, and cross-island discovery sharing, rather than relying on the island model alone. This addresses premature convergence in program search. It is relevant to the growing area of LLM-driven open-ended search and automated program discovery.

entry.title: Gold vs.~Translation: Are We Measuring Language, Knowledge, or Locality in Translated Benchmarks?

author.name: Klaudia-Doris Thellmann, Bernhard Stadler, Dan Saattrup Nielsen, Michael F\"arber, Jens Lehmann

entry.summary: The paper rigorously tests whether translated MMLU proxies measure the same constructs as natively created benchmarks, comparing DeepL-translated versions against six native benchmarks in seven pairings across five Nordic and Baltic languages with 29 models. It introduces incremental proxy validity analysis controlling for model size and language proficiency. Findings show proxy validity varies substantially, cautioning against uncritical use of translated benchmarks.

entry.title: How Specific Do I Need to Be? Effects of User Query Underspecification on Deep Research Agents

author.name: Yi Wen, Xiangjue Dong, Bingxuan Li, Hangxiao Zhu, Leo Zhicheng Liu, Yu Zhang, James Caverlee

entry.summary: The paper introduces UNDERSPEC-DR, a framework for evaluating how underspecified user queries affect deep research agents, showing that underspecification substantially degrades answer quality even when answers remain grounded in cited evidence. Analysis of intermediate search behavior suggests agents respond with broader, less targeted searches. This reveals a real gap between how agents are trained and evaluated versus how real users query them.

entry.title: KV Cache Quantization for Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Yan Tai, Yunan Ding, Guangzhao Li, Siqi Luo, Chaoyang Zhang, Guangtao Zhai, Guodong Guo, Xiaohong Liu

entry.summary: This paper studies KV cache quantization for diffusion language models, where bidirectional attention means cached token representations change as masked tokens are revealed during denoising. The authors adapt existing quantization methods (KIVI, KVQuant) to Fast-dLLM-style cache reuse and introduce TRACE, a calibration trajectory reconstruction method, plus dLLM-KVQ. This matters because efficient inference is a key barrier to practical adoption of diffusion LMs.

entry.title: When Requirements Interact: Scaling Long-Horizon Coding via Interdependent Specifications

author.name: Yishuo Cai, Minzheng Wang, Liang Zhao, Linghao Zhang, Lei Li, Shicheng Li, Xu Sun, Fuli Luo

entry.summary: Introduces CodeSpecWeave, a framework for synthesizing coding-agent tasks with rich, interdependent specifications such as interface compatibility and error handling, designed to force joint reasoning rather than checklist completion. It tackles both task synthesis and verification of subtle requirement interactions to better evaluate long-horizon software development.

entry.title: Hidden Commitment: When Language Models Silently Pick a Side and How Steering Can Surface It

author.name: Samuel Dawit Assefa, Jae Won Cho

entry.summary: This interpretability study shows that in conflicting-context QA, small language models (Qwen 0.8B, Gemma 3 1B) can internally commit to one document while giving no outward sign of the conflict, even when prompted to disclose disagreement. A residual source-choice direction tracks which document the answer uses, sparse middle-layer MLP components write to it, and steering the coordinate changes the chosen source.

entry.title: Annotation-Free Representation Learning for Polyp Retrieval in Colonoscopy Videos

author.name: Luca Parolari, Lamberto Ballan, Carlo Biffi, Loic Le Folgoc

entry.summary: This work introduces an annotation-free, temporally self-supervised framework for learning polyp tracklet representations directly from raw colonoscopy video, removing the dependency on manually annotated bounding boxes. On the REAL-Colon dataset it achieves state-of-the-art tracklet retrieval and re-identification, beating both self-supervised and supervised baselines.

entry.title: Video Generation Meets Agent Harness: Agentic Video Generation, Agentic World Modeling and Recursive Self-Improvement

author.name: Liaoyuan Fan, Yuhao Zheng, Dongxing Mao, Hangyu Ran, Siyuan Hu, Weijia Mao, Rui Zhao, Weijia Wu, Guian Fang, Yanzhe Chen, Zeyu Zhu, Yuxin Jiang, Yiren Song, Yuchao Gu, Junchao Yi, Qi Hu, Dan Kong, Alex Jinpeng Wang, Kevin Qinghong Lin, Mike Zheng Shou, Wei Liu

entry.summary: A position/report-style paper examining the intersection of video generation and agent harnesses: executable runtimes that construct context, expose tools, maintain state, route feedback, and manage budgets around video models. It covers three directions: agentic video generation with production-pipeline coordination, agentic world models as interactive agent environments, and recursive self-improvement, along with associated evaluation challenges.

entry.title: DexSuite: An All-in-One Framework for Dexterous Manipulation Across Arms, Hands, and Tasks

author.name: Anas Houssaini, Hugo He, Junming Shi, Amin Abyaneh, Ricardo Chahine, Shuo Wen, Mohamad H. Danesh, Charles-\'Etienne Fr\'echette, Mariana Sosa Guzman, Mathias Desrochers, Rayan Houssaini, Adam Landa, Theophile Soulie, Charlotte Morissette, Annie Tims, Martino Russi, Jonathan Lussier, Gregory Dudek, Doina Precup, Julen Urain, Hsiu-Chin Lin, David Meger

entry.summary: This paper introduces DexSuite, a simulation framework built on the Genesis simulator for dexterous manipulation research, covering the full workflow from robot setup through demonstration collection to policy evaluation. It provides 30 tasks, 10 arms and 12 end-effectors that compose into over 100 single-arm and thousands of bimanual robot configurations, plus teleoperation, tactile sensing, and a 16-pair benchmark.

entry.title: Open-World Object Motion Anticipation via Meta-Learned Semantic Adaptation

author.name: Mason Peterson, Gage MacLin, Camilla Tabasso, Jonathan P. How, Joshua Migdal, Tye Brady, Taskin Padir

entry.summary: This paper proposes a meta-learned graph neural network that predicts how novel objects move, including induced motion where one object moves another, using semantic, geometric, and relational history. It targets a key gap in robot navigation safety: anticipating motion of objects the robot has not seen before. Better motion anticipation could enable less conservative and safer trajectory planning in open-world environments.

entry.title: ScheduleGen: Demonstration Generation via Skill Scheduling for Multi-Arm Imitation Learning

author.name: Neel Jawale, Stephan Pleines, Soha Pouya, Yuke Zhu, Ajay Mandlekar, Caelan Garrett

entry.summary: ScheduleGen synthesizes multi-arm robot demonstrations by scheduling skills from a few source demonstrations, explicitly respecting multi-arm constraints that existing demonstration-generation methods ignore. This targets the data bottleneck for bimanual and humanoid manipulation, where naive synthesis yields unsafe or unsuccessful behavior. Strong author list (Yuke Zhu, Ajay Mandlekar, Caelan Garrett) supports credibility.

entry.title: Surrogate Uncertainty for Black-box Visual Grounding

author.name: Hanbo Zhang, Tianrun Hu, Cedar Site Bai, Anxing Xiao, David Hsu

entry.summary: The paper tackles uncertainty quantification for visual grounding with black-box vision-language models, arguing that VLM-derived uncertainties inherit the model's biases. It provides a Bayesian formulation treating VLM predictions as observations and uses an external surrogate model calibrated on held-out data to quantify per-query uncertainty. This enables safer robot grounding of free-form language instructions.

entry.title: JEDI: Joint-Embedding Demonstration Compression for In-Context Imitation Learning

author.name: Jiazhao Liang, Zhewen He, Shuaihang Yuan, Hao Huang, Yi Fang

entry.summary: JEDI addresses the context-length bottleneck in in-context imitation learning by compressing demonstrations into latent slots trained to predict next-stage keyframes in a frozen video-JEPA space, using task and process counterfactuals to preserve execution details. It enables many-shot contexts, improved success and demonstration following on LIBERO, and human-hand conditioning on real robots via keypoint tokens.

entry.title: The Reality Gap in Automated Driving Systems Testing: Landscape, Challenges, and Research Directions

author.name: Stefano Carlo Lambertenghi, Oliver Weissl, Johannes Betz, Andrea Stocco

entry.summary: A systematic literature mapping of 235 primary studies (from 4,195 screened publications) on the simulation-to-reality gap in automated driving systems testing. The paper builds a taxonomy across six test components that separates real-world information used to construct testing approaches from actual evidence supporting simulation-to-reality correspondence claims.

entry.title: AI #192: Anthropic Is Going Public

author.name: Zvi

entry.summary: A weekly AI news roundup discussing Anthropic's S-1 filing for an IPO, including analysis of its corporate governance structure and how investor messaging may differ from its public safety rhetoric. It also covers Google's announcement of Gemini 4 Carbon topping a benchmark index just one day before the coverage date, and ongoing reporting on The Hackening AI security incidents.

entry.title: Verifiable LLM-Guided Focal SMT Solving for Quantified Arrays

author.name: Kunhang Lv, Rui Han, Fuqi Jia, Yuhang Dong, Feifei Ma, Jian Zhang

entry.summary: The authors present LinguaArray, a framework where an LLM proposes a small Semantic Focus Set of ground terms and constraints to guide SMT solving over quantified arrays, through a narrow solver-verifiable interface so untrusted LLM outputs cannot corrupt results. It exploits the observation that many instances hinge on a few focal terms, analogous to SAT backdoor sets. This is a clean example of LLM guidance with formal correctness guarantees.

entry.title: FVH-Bench: Evaluating Image Generator Safety Beyond Overtly Harmful Imagery

author.name: Zihao Zhu, Yuhan Liu, Siwei Lyu, Baoyuan Wu

entry.summary: FVH-Bench introduces functional visual harm (FVH): harm from what generated images enable, such as phishing interfaces or fake records, rather than what they depict. The benchmark contains 669 prompts across five harmful visual functions and ten risk domains, exposing a gap in current image generator safety alignment, which largely targets overt content.

entry.title: A Case Study of a Multi-Agent Kernel-Optimization Loop That Learns a New AI Accelerator

author.name: Byonggon Chun

entry.summary: This case study presents an LLM agent loop that optimizes Gemma-4-12B decode kernels for the FuriosaAI RNGD NPU, a rarely documented accelerator programmed in a sparsely documented Rust DSL, over 12 days on a shared device. The loop autonomously builds target knowledge via documentation summaries, microbenchmarks, and compiler-derived legality rules, revising them as the toolchain changes. It demonstrates that agentic self-directed learning can unlock hardware far outside frontier models' training distribution.

entry.title: On-Policy Self-Distillation with Teacher Evolution

author.name: Shufan Shen, Zhongni Hou, Chao Bi, Yufei Zhang, Guojun Yin, Shuhui Wang

entry.summary: The paper identifies that on-policy self-distillation (OPSD) plateaus because the self-teacher gives unreliable guidance on certain samples, and proposes Teacher-Evolution Self-Distillation (TESD), which lets the self-teacher generate rollouts and receive environmental feedback based on task correctness and context independence. This evolving teacher is then used to align the student's token-level distribution and mitigate reward sparsity in post-training.

entry.title: MAS-Loop: Beyond One-Shot Orchestration towards Self-Evolving Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Hehai Lin, Qi Yang, Chengwei Qin

entry.summary: Identifies that most learned multi-agent system orchestration is one-shot, learning only from terminal outcomes, and proposes MAS-Loop, which couples an Orchestrator with a trajectory-conditioned Refiner that uses execution trajectories to revise and re-evaluate systems iteratively. This closes the feedback loop for self-evolving MAS design, a timely direction as agent frameworks proliferate.

entry.title: Judging Before Propagation: Task-Graph Contextual Integrity for Multi-Agent Privacy

author.name: Hengyu Wu, Blaise Delattre, Yang Cao

entry.summary: The paper extends Contextual Integrity privacy norms to multi-agent LLM systems, arguing that a disclosure appropriate in isolation may become inappropriate when propagated downstream through persistent memory and inter-agent communication. Task-Graph CI evaluates releases against the planned workflow rather than local interactions only.

entry.title: MCCL: Training Pytorch models across a fleet of Macs at Skywalker Sound

author.name: Kevin Sasso, Chris Fiegel, Francis Aitken, Nicolas Tsingos, Nicholas Tong

entry.summary: Engineers at Skywalker Sound introduce MCCL, the first open-source Metal Performance Shaders backend enabling multi-node PyTorch distributed training over Ethernet across idle M4 Max Mac Studios, evaluated on 24 nodes. This unlocks large pools of unified-memory Apple hardware for distributed ML, a notable systems contribution for non-NVIDIA training infrastructure.

entry.title: How Architecture, Typology, and Adaptation Strategies Shape ASR for Low-Resource African Languages: A Controlled Empirical Study

author.name: Mercy Muchai (Microsoft Research Africa, Nairobi), Kevin Chege (Microsoft Research Africa, Nairobi), Nick Mumero Mwangi (Microsoft Research Africa, Nairobi), Samuel Chege Maina (Microsoft Research Africa, Nairobi), Felermino Ali (Microsoft Research Africa, Nairobi), Elizabeth Ankrah (Microsoft Research Africa, Nairobi), Ignatius Ezeani (Lancaster University)

entry.summary: This controlled study from Microsoft Research Africa compares three ASR architectures (Phi-4-multimodal-instruct, Whisper-large-v3-turbo, MMS-1B-all) across five low-resource African languages plus Swahili, analyzing data sufficiency, monolingual versus multilingual adaptation, domain fine-tuning, and adapter transfer. Phi-4 achieves the best accuracy while Whisper suffers from known hallucination failure modes. The results offer actionable guidance for practitioners deploying ASR in low-resource settings.

entry.title: A 211K Parameter Foundation Model: Genetic Prompting in Neural Cellular Automata

author.name: John Kalkhof, Niklas Ihm, Daniel Kirste, Anirban Mukhopadhyay

entry.summary: Foundational-NCA is an extremely lightweight (211K parameter) foundation model for medical image segmentation built on Neural Cellular Automata, adapting to diverse segmentation tasks without retraining via genetic optimization over a latent task space and compact task vectors. It targets low-resource clinical environments that cannot run models like SAM.

entry.title: PhysAg3D: Bridging 3D Generative and Agentic Models for High-Fidelity and Physically-Interactive Assets

author.name: Bi'an Du, Fanpeng Meng, Jiemin Fang, Chen Yang, Pufan Li, Daizong Liu, Qi Tian, Wei Hu

entry.summary: PhysAg3D couples 3D generative models with agentic reasoning to produce physically interactive 3D assets from a single image: a VLM agent infers semantic parts, candidate interactions, and physical priors, while a 3D generator produces a textured mesh, linked through a hierarchical interaction representation with iterative refinement guided by observations.

entry.title: LucidLyra: Feed-Forward Generative 3D Scene Reconstruction and Joint Understanding via Multi-Task Distillation

author.name: Oliver Hahn, Rodrigo Marcuzzi, Sangeetha Grama Srinivasan, Alessandro Burzio, Sherwin Bahmani, Jiahui Huang, Stefan Roth, Shengyu Huang, Qunjie Zhou, Laura Leal-Taix\'e

entry.summary: Presents LucidLyra, a feed-forward framework that distills knowledge from a camera-controlled video diffusion model and frozen 2D vision foundation models into a unified model, making generatively reconstructed 3D scenes directly queryable for semantics and instances from video latents. This targets robotics and physical AI applications where generative 3D reconstruction currently lacks semantic and object-identity access without expensive per-scene optimization.

entry.title: OpenFlyV2: An onboard vision-language-action model for aerial perception and navigation

author.name: Junli Liu, Zhongrui You, Chenhui Li, Zhen Li, Yuyang Tian, Qizhen Chen, Delin Qu, Haoming Song, Dong Wang, Xuelong Li, Zhigang Wang, Bin Zhao

entry.summary: OpenFlyV2 is a unified onboard vision-language-action model for drones that shares a vision-language representation across semantic understanding, language-grounded perception, spatial reasoning, and continuous control within one model. A compact action expert enables closed-loop operation on resource-constrained airborne platforms without offboard compute. Bringing VLA-style architectures to aerial robots at the edge is a notable direction.

entry.title: CHORD: Cross-Model Hallucination Detection via Relational Graph Discrimination

author.name: Yongxin Deng (University of Technology Sydney), Zhen Fang (University of Technology Sydney), Guansong Pang (Singapore Management University), Sharon Li (University of Wisconsin-Madison), Ling Chen (University of Technology Sydney)

entry.summary: CHORD addresses cross-model hallucination detection: training detectors on source LLMs that transfer to unseen target LLMs despite heterogeneous internal representations. It uses relational graph discrimination to abstract away model-specific hidden-state semantics, improving generalization of representation-based hallucination detectors.

entry.title: Beyond fabrication: Misattributed numbers in papers written by AI research agents

author.name: Mosab Alfaqeeh, Omar Hourani, Muath Hourani, Hashem Alfaqeeh

entry.summary: The authors re-analyze all 540 judgments from a public benchmark of AI research agents and manually label 256 numerical claims from 18 submissions to characterize numerical integrity failures. They find failures concentrate on misalignment between the paper and the underlying work rather than overt fabrication, with roughly four in five unchecked claims problematic in some way. The paper argues single-judge integrity checks mischaracterize the nature of agent errors.

entry.title: Goal-Aware Dynamic Multi-Agent Collaboration for Long-Horizon Tasks

author.name: Xu Shen, Lingyong Yan, Shuaiqiang Wang, Jianmin Wu, Zhikai Chen, Jiliang Tang, Jie Ren

entry.summary: Through a preliminary study of single-agent long-horizon execution, the authors find that verification correlates most strongly with task success but happens too late, and that duty-relevant information dilutes as shared context accumulates. They propose a goal-aware dynamic multi-agent system that assigns duties like planning and verification to different agents at the right moments. The design targets more reliable LLM agents on extended tasks.

entry.title: Reward-Adaptive Co-Evolution of Policy and Rubric

author.name: Yizhu Chen, Jianguang Jiang, Jiameng Huang, Chuyu Fang, Bojun Zhang, Zhenyu Jiao, Xing Yuan, Tong Lin

entry.summary: RACE is a framework for jointly evolving RL policies and reward rubrics in open-ended reinforcement learning. It routes per-rollout training signals by classifying groups as informative, diversity-collapsed, or rubric-failed, updating the policy only on informative groups and using event-triggered phase switching to adapt rubrics as the policy distribution shifts.

entry.title: EnvOS: Auditing Computer-Use Agents When the World Moves On : Phenomenon-Based Task Construction, Certification, and Evidence-Based Evaluation

author.name: Ankush Kadu, Athira Gopal, Niharika Singh, Arpit Jain, Aswanth Krishnan

entry.summary: EnvOS is a framework for building and certifying computer-use agent environments that change mid-task, verifying before agent runs that changes fire correctly and tasks remain solvable, and re-checking verdicts from archived evidence after runs. It disentangles agent failures from environment-change failures and grader errors.

entry.title: Collaborative AI agents for autonomous experimental research with solid-state quantum spins

author.name: El Mustapha Mansouri, Eikichi Kimura, Masato Koga, Keigo Arai

entry.summary: The authors demonstrate an autonomous research laboratory where LLM-based agents cross-assess each other's work, can stop or redirect investigations, generate and reject research questions, and require independent theoretical checks, demonstrated on ensembles of quantum spins in diamond. The multi-agent mutual-critique design aims to curb unsupported conclusions.

entry.title: Network Topology Does Not Matter: The Breakdown of Classical Consensus in LLM Populations

author.name: Sahil Rajesh Dhayalkar

entry.summary: Across eight instruction-tuned models and 73,080 controlled exchanges, the paper measures the empirical LLM belief-update operator and shows LLMs systematically violate convexity assumptions of classical consensus theory, updating outside the hull of observed opinions. Consequently, network topology fails to predict convergence in LLM populations.

entry.title: Spokes, not a Ring: Revisiting the Weekday Manifold in Language Models

author.name: Diksha Gupta, Rieke Fruengel, Stefan Heimersheim

entry.summary: This interpretability paper tests the assumption that multi-dimensional concept manifolds in LLMs vary continuously, using the prototypical circular weekday representation. Despite its ring-like geometry, the authors show the weekday representation behaves as seven discrete states, with step-like mapping between representation and behavior under on-manifold steering.

entry.title: Interpretable Feature Discovery from Unstructured Data Using LLMs and Statistical Choice Models

author.name: Baptiste Arnaudo, Amine Bennouna, S\'ebastien Martin

entry.summary: The authors propose a method for discovering interpretable, decision-relevant features from unstructured data by having an LLM articulate differences in interpretable terms via pairwise comparisons between items, then consolidating them with statistical choice models. This bridges opaque embeddings and costly hand-engineered features.

entry.title: What Can Firms Do in the Face of Model Distillation?

author.name: Diptangshu Sen, Jibang Wu, Juba Ziani

entry.summary: This economic-theory paper models the strategic interaction between an incumbent provider of proprietary closed-weight models and a competitor that distills capability from conversation transcripts, characterizing how incumbent model characteristics affect market outcomes. It explores what strategic responses are available to firms facing distillation-driven competition.

entry.title: Is it my preference? Role Grounding Attack against Agent's Memory via Social Interaction

author.name: Haoran Bu, Yiting Shen, Litian Zhang, Ruihan Hu, Xi Zhang

entry.summary: This paper formalizes Role Grounding Attack (RGA), a vulnerability in LLM agent memory systems where an attacker's social interaction causes a victim agent to misattribute an attacker-designed preference as belonging to the victim's own user. Via nested conversation structures and experience-sharing posts, the attack corrupts memory formation at the role-to-principal attribution step, a previously unexamined failure surface for socialized agents.

entry.title: The Indian Financial Automated Advice Bias (IFAAB) Dataset : Auditing Socioeconomic and Demographic Disparities in LLM-Generated Financial Advice in India

author.name: Kriti Mahajan

entry.summary: IFAAB is a counterfactual audit benchmark of 31,734 GPT-4o-generated financial-advice responses for synthetic Indian personas varying by gender, caste, education, and other attributes. Holding requests fixed, the audit finds large disparities, e.g., male-labelled profiles receive 60.1% higher implied total resources. It is notable for auditing fairness in a Global South financial context that is rarely covered.

entry.title: AtomSteer: Test-Time Constraint Steering for Atomistic Generative Models

author.name: Pengfei Cai, Katharina S. C. J\"ager, Utkarsh Utkarsh, Nofit Segal, Bowen Deng, Akshay Subramanian, Rafael Gomez-Bombarelli

entry.summary: AtomSteer is a test-time inference framework that steers pretrained atomistic diffusion and flow-matching generators with structural constraints such as crystallographic symmetry, geometry, and stereochemistry. It applies bounded local projections, graph-rigid stereochemical transformations, and periodic symmetry projections during sampling, accepting corrections that preserve the pretrained model's captured geometry.

entry.title: Discovering Jailbreaks via Curriculum of Models

author.name: Micha{\l} Burzy\'nski, Noah T. Rossi, Shomit Basu, Andy Arditi

entry.summary: The paper improves automated jailbreak discovery, where an RL-trained investigator model generates prompts that elicit prohibited behavior from a safety-trained target model. It introduces a curriculum-over-models approach building on the propensity-bound (PRBO) proxy reward to address the sparse reward problem caused by near-universal refusals from the target.

entry.title: HERA: Assessing an Autonomous Agent for Quantum Device Measurement

author.name: Zachary W. Gomez, Nathan Bittner, Jordan T. McCourt, Qingrui Cao, Sandesh S. Kalantre, Benjamin H. Alexander, Zhiren Zheng, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Aaron Sharpe

entry.summary: Presents HERA, an autonomous LLM agent that performs cryogenic transport measurements of quantum devices using a curated lab knowledge base, evaluated with a blinded trial against a human expert, a knowledge-base ablation, and hundreds of offline replays. It is a notable example of rigorous, controlled evaluation of AI agents doing real laboratory science.

entry.title: RetroChessBench: A Benchmark for Reconstructing and Proving Chess Histories

author.name: Tidor-Vlad Pricope

entry.summary: RetroChessBench is a 12-task benchmark for retrograde chess analysis, requiring models to reconstruct legal game histories and distinguish possible from forced events, with references, rubrics, and a terminal-reward environment. Frontier model GPT 6 Astra High failed to produce required final answers in most attempts both with and without code execution, exposing persistent rule-based reasoning failures in existing frontier systems.

entry.title: Well-Specified and Well-Tested? Assessing SWE-bench-Style Datasets with a Self-Evolving Agent

author.name: Zhonghao Jiang, Xuyang Zheng, Yanfu Yan, Zhongxin Liu, Lingfeng Bao, Shuiguang Deng

entry.summary: The paper examines quality issues in SWE-bench-style datasets for evaluating coding agents, where task clarity and test coverage determine solvability and verifiability. It proposes an LLM-based self-evolving annotation agent that adapts to nuanced scenarios instead of relying on static general rubrics, aiming to reduce the high false-positive rates of prior automated approaches.

entry.title: Sandman: Building and Operating Sandboxes for Agentic Reinforcement Learning on Shared Kubernetes

author.name: Yiming Yan, Hongyang Wang, Wenbo Chen, Xuan Wang, Jingguo Liu, Xian Li, Chen Qi, Leo Fan, Siwei Li, Qianli Wu, Yichuan Li, Ruochen Wen, Qian Qu, Zheshen Wang, Benoit Dumoulin

entry.summary: Sandman is a production sandbox service built at Amazon for agent tool execution and evaluation in agentic RL, creating Kubernetes-pod-based environments in bursts of thousands on shared clusters. It provides persistent files and processes across tool calls, managing creation, readiness, and cleanup, with demonstrated behavior at scale.

entry.title: Rethinking Neural Thickets Without Weight Perturbations

author.name: Nicolas Dufour, Elouan Gard\`es, Amil Dravid, Patrick P\'erez, Loic Landrieu

entry.summary: This paper reproduces reported gains from the Neural Thickets hypothesis — that pretrained LLMs lie near task-specific experts reachable by Gaussian weight perturbations — but shows the geometric explanation is unnecessary: perturbing a single decoder block, or even adding random bias to frozen output logits, matches or exceeds full-weight perturbation. It formalizes the alternative as Perturb-Select-Vote (PSV), based on output diversity, validation-based selection, and voting.

entry.title: Generative modeling for fusion: a large-scale benchmark of stellarator fast-ion simulations

author.name: Misha Padidar, Teresa Huang, Mark Goldstein, Michael Czekanski, Jeffrey Soules

entry.summary: The authors release a large-scale benchmark dataset for machine learning surrogate modeling of stellarator fast-ion guiding-center simulations, aimed at accelerating fusion reactor design optimization. The dataset captures both design diversity and high-fidelity simulation outputs, enabling rapid generation and evaluation of new stellarator configurations.

entry.title: Integral Probability Boundaries

author.name: Bogdan Kulynych, Shahab Asoodeh

entry.summary: The paper introduces Integral Probability Boundaries, a non-linear generalization of Integral Probability Metrics that yields bounds tight at the extremes where IPM-based bounds are loose or vacuous for rare events and under-represented groups. The authors derive basic properties, estimation algorithms, and applications in generalization, alignment, fairness, and privacy settings.

entry.title: Transportable Offline Reinforcement Learning in Presence of Unmeasured Confounding

author.name: Junyi Liao, Hangqi Ren, Zhuoran Yang

entry.summary: This work studies offline policy learning when both domain shift and unmeasured confounding are present, developing a causally adjusted transportability framework that combines instrumental variables, negative controls, and proxies to identify target-domain causal quantities. For confounded contextual bandits it reduces identification to tractable problems.

entry.title: Rethinking LLM Jailbreak Evaluation: Continuous Risk Landscapes Beyond Binary Outcomes

author.name: Yukai Zhou, Wenjie Wang

entry.summary: This paper argues that binary attack-success-rate indicators obscure the structure of LLM jailbreak behavior, and introduces a continuous, context-conditioned risk landscape over first-token branches estimated by repeatedly sampling continuations of candidate openings. This perspective reveals graded risk structure around jailbreak prompts rather than a single pass/fail outcome.

entry.title: Contextual Embeddings Beyond the Gold Chunk

author.name: Sedigheh Eslami, Markus Krimmel, William Barber, Antoine Chaffin, Maximilian Schall, Jonas Golde, Louis Milliken, Ekaterina Glazkova, Denis Bykov, Bo Wang

entry.summary: The authors introduce pplx-embed-v2-context, a family of contextual embedding models trained by distilling graded chunk-level relevance from a query-aware context compression model, removing the need for gold-chunk labels and making training independent of chunking. Using a vision-language backbone, the retriever surfaces multi-chunk answers plus supporting verification evidence. This improves realism of retrieval training relative to single-gold-chunk assumptions.

entry.title: Achieving Minimax-Optimal First-Order and Best-of-Both-Worlds Regret Simultaneously in Multi-Armed Bandits

author.name: Mengxiao Zhang

entry.summary: The paper proposes an efficient, parameter-free bandit algorithm that simultaneously achieves minimax-optimal worst-case regret and the optimal first-order regret bound O(sqrt(K L*)), removing a logarithmic gap left by prior work of Pogodin and Lattimore. This settles the best-of-both-worlds regret problem in multi-armed bandits more tightly.

entry.title: Rural Readiness: Domain Generalization with Adversarially Chosen Domains

author.name: Cynthia Dwork, Andisheh Ghasemi, Lunjia Hu

entry.summary: Motivated by deploying clinical algorithms for data-scarce rural populations using knowledge from data-rich hospitals, this theory paper formulates domain generalization with adversarially chosen target domains, asking learners to match the worst hypothesis consistent with observed sources. It characterizes sample complexity up to logarithmic factors assuming only a universal predictor with small error on the k source domains.

entry.title: sDMD: Sinkhorn Distribution Matching Distillation

author.name: Jaihoon Kim, Lingxiao Li, Soshi Shimada, Roshni Cooper, Minhyuk Sung, Yiwei Zhao

entry.summary: The paper analyzes Distribution Matching Distillation through the lens of Wasserstein gradient flow, showing its gradient derives from a fixed-point formulation with integral KL as the energy functional. This motivates adding an optimal-transport (Sinkhorn) term that guides low-density outlier samples toward the teacher distribution and mitigates reverse-KL mode collapse. The result is an improved distillation method for compressing multi-step diffusion models into few-step generators.

entry.title: NEOPIC: A Neural Operator Framework for Particle-based Kinetic Plasma Simulations

author.name: Sriramkrishnan Muralikrishnan, Chelsea Maria John, Jeffrey Kelling, Michael Bussmann, Robert Speck, Paul Gibbon

entry.summary: NEOPIC learns the field operator in particle-based kinetic plasma simulations using a neural operator evaluated directly at particle positions on the empirical measure, avoiding mesh deposition that aliases particle noise. It acts as a plug-and-play field solver trainable on particle-in-cell, particle-in-Fourier, or tree-code data and composable with any time integrator. This could substantially accelerate plasma physics simulation.

entry.title: Tracing the Influence of Retrieved Literature on Scientific Ideation in LLMs

author.name: Zhipin Wang, Koel Dutta Chowdhury, Christoph Leiter, Steffen Eger

entry.summary: This study isolates how retrieval strategy shapes LLM-generated research ideas by comparing five retrieval strategies against a no-literature baseline under a shared generation protocol, using 45,000 ideas across 15 ML topics and ten open-weight models. Retrieval reduces diversity among ideas from the same paper set while increasing diversity across different sets. The findings have implications for AI-assisted scientific ideation and homogenization of research ideas.

entry.title: Unlimited OCR Works 2

author.name: Shu Wei, Jingjing Wu, Qunyi Xie, Lingshu Zhang, Xiangcheng Du, Yannian Fu, Mengjie Wang, Zuyi Wang, Zhichao Liu, Yangliu Xu, YY, Yi Yang

entry.summary: Unlimited OCR 2 is a document parsing model for ultra-long documents that upgrades decoder attention to Sparse Reference Sliding Window Attention, bounding active reference tokens to a fixed capacity for constant memory cost per decoding step. Inspired by human transcription with localized focus, it mitigates the computational blowup of parsing hundreds of pages. This is a meaningful efficiency advance for long-horizon document understanding.

entry.title: Elucidating the Design Space of LM Data Attribution

author.name: Steven Yu, Sheng-Yu Wang, Kimia Hamidieh, Antonio Torralba, David Bau

entry.summary: The authors introduce CATT, a controlled benchmark for LM data attribution in which models are fine-tuned on fictitious knowledge with unambiguous ground truth, enabling systematic isolation of one dataset property at a time (redundancy, lexical distractors, etc.). This diagnoses why attribution algorithms fail where existing multi-variable evaluations cannot. Strong authorship (David Bau, Antonio Torralba groups) grounds the work in the interpretability community.

entry.title: Diagnosing the Reference Gap: What Visual Scaffolds Can and Cannot Fix in Multimodal Reasoning

author.name: Guizhen Chen, Weiwen Xu, Wotao Yin, Anh Tuan Luu, Hou Pong Chan

entry.summary: Introduces the concept of a reference gap, where multimodal LLM reasoning failures stem from failure to bind language to visual entities rather than perception alone, and presents ReGap-Bench with paired tasks where only the reference varies. Task-matched references like numbering improve accuracy up to 25 percent, while mismatched references can hurt, clarifying what visual scaffolding can and cannot fix.

entry.title: Venus-DefakerOne2: A Vision-Forensics Foundation Model with Broader Coverage

author.name: Chenfan Qu, Yachao Liang, Mingqi Fang, Jiangwei Xie, Zhenming Wang, Baoyue Zhang, Changjiang Jiang, Zheng Chang, Fanli Jin, Xuekang Zhu, Kaiwen Feng, Junchi Li, Weihong Zhang, Haoyue Wang, Chenfeng Zhang, Yinan Xia, Fangming Cui, Dong Fan, Jingjing Liu, Tianyi Zhang, Luobin Chen, Ji-Zhe Zhou, Sheng Li, Wei Wang, Bin Li, Ran He, Xinpeng Zhang, Linna Zhou, Jian Liu, Weiqiang Wang

entry.summary: Presents a unified vision-forensics foundation model trained on tens of millions of samples that covers digital manipulation, physical spoofing, and both image and video media. Key designs include Tide-Style-Tuning, which alternates LoRA and full-parameter fine-tuning to balance generalization and hard-sample fitting while mitigating catastrophic forgetting, and an entropy-based component for broad forgery coverage.

entry.title: PulmoWorld: An Asynchronous Multimodal Medical World Model for Longitudinal Pneumonia Dynamics

author.name: Cheng Tang, Xinyu Zhang, Jiawei Chen, Minghui Zhang, Shaocong Wei, Wei Li, Yuxing Chen, Kongcheng Zhang, Chun-Mei Feng, Nanqing Dong, Xinyuan Zhu, Ziyan Huang, Junjun He, Yirong Chen, Lingtong Huang, Min Cen, Ming Hu

entry.summary: PulmoWorld is a medical world model for longitudinal pneumonia dynamics combining asynchronous state estimation, recursive simulation, and evidence-constrained planning. History-aware filtering separates state propagation from observation correction, and a Cap-MBRL component searches imagined continuations within an authorized clinical action set with a frozen fallback policy.

entry.title: Seeing and Imagining as One: Unified Video Generation and 4D Perception for Embodied World Modeling

author.name: Haitang Feng, Zhuoman Liu, Zhennan Wang, Sheng Wang, Juelin Li, Chengzhi Zhao, Hexiang Wei, Lin Shao

entry.summary: GenSight unifies future video generation and dense perception (depth, embodiment segmentation, 2D flow) in a single pretrained video diffusion transformer with a shared DiT backbone, jointly optimizing all modalities in one velocity prediction space and supporting both generation and perception modes at inference.

entry.title: TactoHand: Learning Geometry-Based Dense Hand-Surface Interaction Fields from Video

author.name: Ziheng Xi, Weibo Li, Jiayi Yu, Sipeng Zheng, Wanpeng Zhang, Haiweng Xu, Hao Luo, Chuan Mao, Zongqing Lu

entry.summary: Introduces TactoHand, a temporal transformer model predicting dense contact, proximity, and 3D force fields on the hand surface from monocular video, trained with geometry- and motion-derived labels from a curated ~50 million frame collection, plus a differentiable physics component. It enables scalable understanding of hand-object physical interaction without tactile hardware.

entry.title: AB-Attention: Accurate Block Attention for Accelerating Video Diffusion Transformers

author.name: Bin Xu, Mo Zhang, Zhengfeiyang Zhang, Xinfeng Yang, Yixing Ma, Wei Wang, HeXin Wang, Pengfei Zhou, Wangbo Zhao

entry.summary: AB-Attention is a training-free block-sparse attention method that accelerates video diffusion transformers at high sparsity while preserving fidelity. It addresses weaknesses of prior dynamic block-sparse attention through intra-block clustering for accurate importance estimation and a corrected softmax treatment of pruned blocks rather than coarse tile-level keep/drop decisions.

entry.title: VideoMemBench: How Well Do MLLMs Remember in Video Conversations?

author.name: Zhengdong Hu, Chao Wang, Kaituo Feng, Huanjin Yao, Mingfei Lu, Hehe Fan, Yi Yang

entry.summary: Introduces VideoMemBench, a benchmark measuring in-context video memory: whether multimodal LLMs can retrieve and reuse information from earlier turns of a long multi-turn dialogue about a single video, including what the model itself previously said. Existing video QA benchmarks have mutually independent questions and thus never test cross-turn information carrying.

entry.title: RFW-A: Agentic Procedural Generation of 400K Articulated Assets over 500 Categories

author.name: Yuanbo Lyu, Changjian Pan, Saining Zhang, Yi Yang, Peishuo Li, Zhiheng Li, Jialu Liu, Junhao Chen, Jiawei Weng, Yupeng Gao, Weiqing Xiao, Wenyi Li, Jiarui Guo, Rui Zhang, Jingrun Du, Weiyi Lin, Zenan Meng, Hu Wei, Lin Qu, Zongzheng Zhang, Hao Zhao, Chaojian Li

entry.summary: Presents RFW-A, a framework combining agentic program synthesis with procedural generation to create 400K articulated 3D assets across 500 categories: agents write reusable construction programs once per category, and procedural execution instantiates many varied assets. This addresses the cost of manual annotation and the repeated per-asset reasoning of prior agentic asset-construction systems.

entry.title: L3G-World: Real-Time Infinite World Generation with Latent 3D Gaussian Memory

author.name: Jinhyeok Choi, JoungBin Lee, Jongmin Lee, Minkyeong Jeon, Jiyoung Kim, Kaeun Han, Yoonjin Yoon, Seungryong Kim

entry.summary: L3G-World introduces a Latent 3D Gaussian Memory that combines fast feed-forward reconstruction with a compact, quickly renderable scene representation, enabling real-time, spatially consistent world generation over unbounded horizons. A memory updater and video diffusion generator condition on this latent memory instead of re-encoding RGB renderings. This tackles the key scaling and latency bottlenecks of interactive world models.

entry.title: ELEVATE: Agentic Controller Acquisition from Task Failure for Quadrupedal Manipulation

author.name: Shiqi Liu, Radu Corcodel, Ding Zhao

entry.summary: ELEVATE uses persistent failures during task-program refinement to detect missing whole-body control capabilities in quadrupedal manipulators, then has a coding agent formulate and iteratively refine an RL problem with rewards, curricula, and termination conditions. Validated controllers join a capability library and compose with existing controllers to retry tasks, expanding autonomy from a single pretrained loco-manipulation controller.

entry.title: Catch It All!: Generalizable Dynamic Catching with a Dexterous Hand

author.name: Arth Shukla, Kehlani Fay, Huaze Liu, Darin Djapri, Alexiy Buynitsky, Nicklas Hansen

entry.summary: A sim-to-real framework for humanoid robots with dexterous hands to catch unseen objects with variable geometry and physical properties, using only an egocentric camera and real-time grasp adaptation. It includes safety-aware curricula for high-frequency actions near hardware limits. Dynamic whole-body catching is a demanding testbed for generalizable manipulation and control.

entry.title: From Reasoning to Action: Consequence-Grounded Alignment for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Yixue Zhang, Wenke Xia, Kun Wu, Wenbo Yu, Pei Ren, Junnan Nie, Di Hu, Zhengping Che, Chang Liu

entry.summary: CoRAct explicitly aligns embodied chain-of-thought reasoning with actions in VLA models via reward-guided optimization in action noise space, treating movement and waypoint components of ECoTs as verifiable signals. Prior work conditions actions on ECoTs without optimizing for consistency; this makes the reasoning-action link explicit. A unified Mixture-of-Transformers backbone jointly models the components.

entry.title: PASA-KV: Attacking Action-Facing Visual Routes in World Action Models

author.name: Zhongbo Wu, Jiakai Huang, Zheng Zhang, Siyu Xu, Kaixiang Chen, Xiaohong Liu, Shan You, Chang Xu, Tao Huang

entry.summary: This work studies adversarial robustness of world action models, revealing a mismatch between how perturbable internal visual representations are and how consequential they are for closed-loop behavior. The analysis identifies attention keys and values in action-conditioned readout as the critical attack surface, motivating a targeted key-value attack. The findings inform where robustness efforts in robot foundation models should focus.

entry.title: AcrossDEX 1.0: From Human Motion Pretraining to Bimanual Dexterous Manipulation across Hand Embodiments

author.name: Xiaoyu Yang, Nan Wu

entry.summary: AcrossDEX 1.0 is a learning system that transfers bimanual dexterous manipulation skills from human video pretraining to robot hands across different hand embodiments. It pretrains on the HOT3D Aria dataset to predict bimanual motion from short image sequences, then adapts to robots via simulation-based expert learning and real demonstrations while preserving the visual encoder and temporal backbone.

entry.title: [Paper] Propensities Please: Exposing Alignment-Faking LLMs using Synthetic Document Finetuning

author.name: florkowski

entry.summary: From the LASR Labs Fellowship, this work presents a method to detect alignment faking without chain-of-thought access: the model is convinced there is no effective oversight, widening the gap between misaligned behavior under claimed no-oversight versus evaluation conditions. Across alignment-faking model organisms, this intervention widens the measured oversight gap by 24 to 68 percentage points.

entry.title: Encode Once, Answer Many: Internalizing Context via Parametric Flow

author.name: Xinhao Zhong, Mengxuan Wu, Chonghua Liao, Linxi Xie, Ruicheng Feng, Yanpei Guo, Hao Tan, Jiaxin Hong, Jason Li, Panpan Zhang, Ziheng Qin, Qinglin Lu, Yuzhang Shang, Tongliang Liu, Damian Borth, Haggai Maron, Yongxiang Hua, Zhixiang Wei, Jian Hu, Yunfei Wu, Xing Sun, Xin Li, Haoyu Cao, Zhangyang Wang, Kai Wang

entry.summary: CLIK proposes a context-conditioned LoRA parameter generator that maps a context to adapter weights in a single forward pass, internalizing contextual knowledge into a frozen model without per-task fine-tuning or re-encoding the context at inference. This amortizes the cost of long-context prompting across many queries.

entry.title: Think Before You Act: Decision Gate for LLM Agents

author.name: Iftach Shoham, Yuval David, Offer Akrabi, Erez Bilgory, Ido Levy, Sami Marreed, Sergey Zeltyn, Segev Shlomov

entry.summary: JevAct is a runtime verification framework that intercepts selected LLM agent actions before execution and enables feedback-driven correction. Domain policies are compiled into executable state checks plus structured questions evaluated by a prefill-only decision model producing probability-based judgments without generation. It combines deterministic verification of tool-state facts with probabilistic context assessment to catch invalid actions and premature task termination.

entry.title: What Does "Now" Mean to Your Computer-Use Agent? Stale Screenshots, Page Loads, and Which Check to Run Before a Click

author.name: Vasundra Srinivasan

entry.summary: This measurement study shows that staleness risk for computer-use agent clicks lies mainly in page loading, not the planning interval: 17 percent of clicks planned in the first second after page open become stale versus 0.4 percent on fully loaded pages. Waiting roughly one second for network activity to cease removes most risk, yet eight of ten widely used open-source agents fail to apply adequate wait rules. It yields an actionable check agents should run before clicking.

entry.title: Tactus: Tactile & Pose Sensing Glove for Natural Dexterity Data Collection

author.name: Li Guan, Rachael Granberry, Sahar Aseeri, Sahar Rostami, Taylor Niehues, Sai Dhanooshi Marri, Mia Huang, Dingtian Zhang, Ziyi Kou, Jason Pursel, Eric Whitmire, Vatsal Mehta, Ashish Deshpande, Tristan Trutna, Reed Belcher, Emelia Black, Julian Blake, Roger Boldu, Sean Bonaventure, Einar Boyovich, Jordan Brennan, Elizabeth Casillas, David Christensen, Tyler Christensen, Nicholas Colonnese, Stuart Dealey, Gaige DeHaven, Katie Doran, Chris Doughty, Robert Drury, Silvia Espino, Gabriel Geyne, Beth Goodrich, Kyra Gould, Joe Grisso, Susana Guerrero, Andrew Gwozdziowski, Monica Ha, Ehsan Hajiesmaili, Kate Healy, Rose Hope, Michael Hurst, Claire Ikemiya, Daisy Isibor, Rick James, Yashasvi Joginapally, Samuel Johnson, Tyler Jorgensen, Kristy Jost, Ben Kamath, Slava Karulin, Alexander Keener, Woo Kim, Alison Krauskopf, Ankit Kumar, Joshua Lang, Lizzy Li, Cameron Lynch, Daniel Ma, Hector Martinon, Christina Matos, Keagan McCurdy, Lee Mincey, Stuart Nezlek, Tiffany Nguyen, James O'Hara, Jason Osborne, Jacky Pai, Roham Pardakhtim, David Perek, Alexandre Poulin, Nick Raines, Salwa Rasheed, Leah Resneck, Kevin Rhodes, Ergys Ristani, Douglas Roberts, Anik Sarker, Harrison Scarborough, Jonas Schmidtler, Brian Shieh, Benjamin Shuman, Garrett Simard, Forrest Smith, Udara Somarathna, Eliot Sosin, Jonathan Stewart, Kristine Strom, Adam Swett, Hal Talbot-Mantooth, Julia Tanner, Sai Sharan Thirunagari, Curtis Torrey, Simge Uzun, Eileen Wachs, Rylan Wasson, Henry Wei, Jesse White, Beau Woodbyrne, Antonio Woods, Noah Young, Chandler Yount, Joseph Zhang, Sean Keller

entry.summary: Introduces Tactus, a textile-integrated sensing glove providing calibrated fingertip force sensing and occlusion-resilient IMU-fused hand tracking in a thin 1.5mm 3D-knit form factor that preserves natural manipulation. It targets high-quality human demonstration data for robot dexterous manipulation policies and world model learning, a key data bottleneck in embodied AI.

entry.title: UMI-Live for In-The-Wild Bimanual Robotics Data Collection

author.name: Govind Velamoor, Adrian Lin, Sam Jung, Spencer Mateega, Brandon Y. Yang, Amish Sethi

entry.summary: UMI-Live is a full-stack open-source bimanual Universal Manipulation Interface system for in-the-wild robot learning data collection, integrating camera and LiDAR-inertial sensing, onboard compute, and power without external tracking or in-environment calibration. It includes an asynchronous pipeline for parallel SLAM reconstruction and publishes training-ready datasets with released hardware and software.

entry.title: Mind The Gap (MTG-AD): Dataset and Fine-grained Evaluation for End-to-End Inline Audio Descriptions

author.name: Subhashini Venugopalan, Jenny Tan, Taylor Roper, Jimmy Tobin, Anton Kast, Alicia Martin, Sam Sepah, Amy Pavel

entry.summary: MTG-AD is a professionally annotated 36-hour dataset with 8k+ inline audio descriptions co-created by paired blind and sighted AD professionals, designed to benchmark MLLM-generated audio descriptions that must fit within existing video silences. The work provides fine-grained evaluation of MLLMs on accessibility-critical inline AD for user-generated content.

entry.title: Floor It, Then Fill It: Simulating Creator Ecosystems for Fair Video-Content Recommendation Systems at Billion User Scale

author.name: Sohini Roychowdhury, Long Sha, Sunand Agarwal, Payal Kamboj, Shuyang Chen, Junlin Zhang, Scott Chen, Hui Zhang

entry.summary: This industry-authored paper presents a user-simulation framework modeling roughly 42K creators and coupled viewer interactions over 12 weeks to evaluate equitable view-allocation policies formulated as budgeted multi-armed bandits. The simulator captures creator diversity, behavioral dynamics, and platform constraints, aimed at countering rich-get-richer dynamics that disadvantage emerging creators.

entry.title: Event2Reward: Learning Robotic Rewards from Progress Relations

author.name: Junnan Nie, Zitian Fan, Jiachen Zhang, Junyi Lao, Likui Zhang, Chenghao Liu, Xiaoyang Lu, Yunbo Wang, Yixue Zhang, Linbo Zhai, Jiayi Li, Mengzhe Wang, Xichang Wu, Bin Wang, Chang Liu, Tianle Zhang, Songfang Huang

entry.summary: Event2Reward learns dense shaping rewards for robotic RL from demonstration progress relations, exploiting that stalls, regressions, and recoveries in suboptimal or failed executions establish local relative progress even when absolute progress labels are unreliable. This corrects the common flaw of treating normalized demonstration time as monotonically increasing progress.

entry.title: Hierarchical Diffusion for Camera-controlled Autoregressive Video Generation

author.name: Kaihua Chen, Yiming Gong, Deva Ramanan, Tarasha Khurana

entry.summary: Proposes a lightweight framework combining autoregressive generation (WanAR) with hierarchical long-context denoising (FixAR) to reduce error accumulation and geometry drift in long, camera-controlled video generation from a single image. The approach avoids the overhead of self-forcing and explicit 6-DOF pose conditioning while keeping scene geometry consistent with input cameras.

entry.title: OneScene-Bench: Do Vision-Language Models Integrate Evidence Across Views?

author.name: Swathi Suhas, Anurag Das, Bernt Schiele, Jonas Fischer

entry.summary: OneScene-Bench is a controlled benchmark that isolates whether VLMs truly integrate information across multiple views of the same scene, testing unique object counting, cross-view consistency, and spatial reasoning on real-world multi-view data with controlled object overlap. It distinguishes genuine cross-view correspondence from independent per-view processing.

entry.title: InfantNet: A Large Scale Dataset for Infant Body Pose and Shape Estimation

author.name: Zhipeng Hui, Jiahao Wang, Xun Dong, Guofeng Zhang, Xingrui Wang, Jiawei Peng, Qihao Liu, Xiaoding Yuan, Yi Zhang, Junjie Oscar Yin, Wufei Ma, Qinfan Lyu, Sara N. Lupolt, Keeve Edward Nachman, Adam Kortylewski, Alan Yuille

entry.summary: Releases InfantNet, the largest real-image infant dataset for body pose and shape estimation, comprising 108,902 RGB images of infants aged 6-18 months with 2D keypoint annotations and a curated 11,642-image subset with 3D pose and shape (SMIL) parameters verified via multi-view reprojection filtering. It addresses the failure of adult-designed methods transferred to infants due to different proportions, articulation, and occlusion, with applications in childcare and medical monitoring.

entry.title: LRMoE: Demand-Side Load Re-Calibration for Efficient MoE Training on Memory-Constrained Nodes

author.name: Jiaming Hu, Zhida Jiang, Zhaolong Xing, Yu Li, Zhen Chen, Ke Zhang

entry.summary: LRMoE is a memory-aware training system for sparse Mixture-of-Experts models that jointly plans expert placement and retention quotas during forward execution, then recalibrates backward-pass workload by estimating each token-expert pair's contribution to expert updates. This addresses computation and communication bottlenecks from uneven routing without the memory cost of extra expert replicas.

entry.title: Detecting Covert Collusion between AI Agents through Partner-Outsider Positive Listening

author.name: Kevin Yandoka Denamgana\"i

entry.summary: Proposes PoPLi, a behavioral test for detecting AI agents that coordinate via secret message conventions that look innocent to message-level monitors. The method compares how much a suspected partner versus an uninvolved outsider changes its action when a message is reworded with meaning preserved, computable by replaying logged prompts, and is validated in a simulated market with five collusion conditions.

entry.title: Decompose, Don't Expand: Capability-Independent AI Systems by Construction

author.name: Tejaswi Gowda

entry.summary: This paper argues that many tasks delegated wholesale to LLMs are mostly deterministic with a small generative core, and that decomposing them yields parity by construction: performance on extracted sub-tasks becomes independent of model size. Empirical results across nine models support the claim that decomposition beats model expansion for such tasks.

entry.title: Predict the Reward, Not the World: World Reward Models for ML Agents

author.name: Yuxiao Lee, Zherui Yang, Fan Liu, Hao Liu

entry.summary: This paper proposes World Reward Models (WRMs) for search-based ML agents that write, execute, and select candidate programs. Instead of using an LLM world model to predict execution outcomes (which can inject false information), WRMs learn from real execution results to directly choose which candidate will perform better. This reframing aims to save expensive execution time while avoiding misleading predictions.

entry.title: Context Compaction for World Models

author.name: Hayder Tirmazi

entry.summary: The paper reframes inconsistent world regeneration when observers revisit regions as a context retrieval problem, spanning both KV-cache design at the model layer and harness-level context selection. The authors contribute a benchmark that generates fresh worlds per episode to prevent memorization, plus context compaction techniques. This connects world-model research with the practical context engineering used in LLM agent stacks.

entry.title: Does Scaling Toward AGI Depend on What System-1 Lets System-2 Execute?

author.name: Qi Wang, Yun Qu, Lizhou Cai, Heming Zou, Haoang Chi, Yiqin Lv, Xiang Li, Haiyan Feng, Mengyu Ge, Yize Geng, Yuhang Jiang, Yixiu Mao, Xiangyang Ji

entry.summary: The paper proposes conditional interaction, a predict-gate-execute-update loop in which a lightweight System-1 predictor estimates candidate action utilities so that the resource-intensive System-2 only executes actions worth their cost. The authors argue that co-designing fast and slow systems may be the next stage of scaling toward AGI beyond simply enlarging models and compute.

entry.title: Cheap Retrieval and Observation Credit Assignment from One Quantity: The Value of Information

author.name: Daniel Strauss, Nikolaos Sotirakis, Zhenshan Bing, Alois Knoll

entry.summary: The paper argues that memory retrieval cost and credit assignment in RL are both governed by a single quantity, the value of information, estimated from archived rollouts via a learned world model. Reading it at the observation yields a provable lower bound on the optimal value of the acquiring action that floors the TD target, while at decision time it defines the optimal retrieval set.

entry.title: DynaRev: Benchmarking Web Agents under Dynamic Goal Revision

author.name: Shiqi Zhang, Guochen Zhou, Zesheng Wei, Hai Zhao, Zhisong Zhang

entry.summary: DynaRev is a benchmark of 181 tasks that evaluates web agents when users revise goals mid-task, delivering revisions at semantic milestones including additive revisions, unconditional overrides, and runtime-conditioned overrides. Evaluations of five models show agents often satisfy only part of revised requirements, with trajectory-grounded assessment of correctness, responsiveness, and efficiency.

entry.title: Distributional Reward Calibration and Budget-Neutral Credit Assignment for Multimodal RLVR

author.name: Lang Chen, Zongxin Xu, Borui Wang, Anran Liu, Shitong Chen

entry.summary: The paper factorizes GRPO token-level advantage estimation into sample-level baselining and token-level credit assignment, showing existing estimators mishandle heavy-tailed verifier reward distributions and need not conserve total credit. It proposes TACE, a two-stage calibrated estimator for multimodal RLVR that addresses both stages.

entry.title: Retrieval as Traversal: Value-Indexed Memory for Stateful Long-Context Agents

author.name: Daniel Strau{\ss}, Zhenshan Bing, Alois Knoll

entry.summary: This paper proposes reframing retrieval for long-context agents as a persistent local traversal through an address space, separating memory content from its address and defining utility by the information revealed on retrieval. A cost-regularised indexing objective exploits overlap between neighboring retrieval steps, unlike attention or recurrent compression that re-solve similar retrieval problems each pass.

entry.title: Bouba Beats Kiki, and Other Regularities in the Subjective Preferences of LLMs

author.name: Katy Blumer, Jon Kleinberg, Ravi Kumar, Andrew Tomkins

entry.summary: This paper takes early steps toward evaluating how LLMs make choices among multiple viable responses where no option is objectively correct, focusing on short-form comparison tasks. Notably, it finds models reproduce the bouba/kiki sound-shape association and other systematic regularities in subjective preference.

entry.title: Poisoned Skills: Propagating Jailbreaks Through Agent Markdown Files

author.name: Kashyap R Manjusha, Murali Emani

entry.summary: The paper demonstrates that jailbreaks embedded in Markdown skill files can act as an injection channel, propagating through an agent's initialization context to induce prohibited behavior. Using a LangChain-based QA agent with persona manipulation plus a GPTFUZZER-style attack, the authors evaluate effectiveness across seven open-weight models.

entry.title: Estimating Implicit Expected Log Density Ratios

author.name: Avi Amalanshu, Chandler Squires, Yizhou Lu, Pradeep Ravikumar

entry.summary: The authors introduce the expected log density ratio (ELDR), a log density ratio integrated under a third measure, and show that many problems where naive density ratio estimation is applied with implicit densities are actually ELDR estimation tasks. They prove fundamental finite-sample limitations of ELDR estimation, argue that standard DRE approaches are unsuitable, and lay foundations for dedicated estimation methods.

entry.title: Precedent or Intent? What Coding Agents Follow When Evolving Existing Code

author.name: Haichao Zhu, Geyang Xu, Zhaorui Yang, Jiyuan Wang, Qian Zhang

entry.summary: This paper studies how coding agents resolve conflicts between existing repository conventions and new task instructions, using bidirectional controlled experiments in purpose-built and real-world repositories. It isolates three competing guidance sources: the agent's defaults, repository precedent, and task intent. The question is central to how reliably agents can evolve mature codebases.

entry.title: RoleFUZZER: User-Behaviour Fuzzing for Role-Specification Adherence in Large Language Models

author.name: Kshitish Ghate, Michael Saxon, Tadayoshi Kohno, Aylin Caliskan

entry.summary: RoleFUZZER adapts coverage-guided fuzzing from software testing to search over plausible user behaviors that can lead LLMs to violate system-prompt role specifications during multi-turn interactions. It uses a user-behaviour coverage grid crossing grounded traits to construct scenarios systematically. This brings principled testing methodology to the understudied problem of role adherence in deployed LLM personas.

entry.title: Persona Learning from Feedback for Personalized AI Assistants

author.name: Yiran Shen, Yu Xia, Liuyi Yao, Prithviraj Ammanabrolu

entry.summary: Persona Learning from Feedback (PLF) learns reusable, preference-grounded assistant personas as independent LoRA adapters on a frozen backbone, using a frozen self-teacher that conditions on persona specifications and response-specific feedback to give token-level supervision. This goes beyond persona prompting by grounding personalization in concrete behavioral feedback per response.

entry.title: Geometry Matters in Packed 3D Attention

author.name: Amil Khan, Anantajit Subrahmanya, B. S. Manjunath

entry.summary: The paper identifies a failure mode in attention over packed 3D volumes: sequence position encodes memory layout rather than object geometry, so positional mechanisms can learn the wrong structure. It proposes PACK3D, a local-global attention operator that keeps neighborhood attention exact, compresses distant context into 3D block summaries, and applies axial RoPE indexed by true grid coordinates.

entry.title: Learning to Bound: Monotonic, Calibrated Neural Upper Bounds for MPE Inference

author.name: Akshay Vyas, Hailiang Dong, Shivvrat Arya, Brij Malhotra, Tahrima Rahman, Vibhav Gogate, Nicholas Ruozzi

entry.summary: L2B trains a neural predictor to produce admissible, calibrated upper bounds for Most Probable Explanation inference in probabilistic graphical models, amortizing the cost of classical bound computation like Mini-Bucket Elimination within branch-and-bound search. The framework targets the admissibility and tightness properties needed for effective systematic search.

entry.title: LLM Agent-Based Design of RISC-V CPUs with FPGA-in-the-Loop Evaluation

author.name: Leo Itoh, Junichiro Kadomoto

entry.summary: The authors build a development environment where LLM agents implement CPU candidates on an FPGA and use on-board performance measurements to guide design, avoiding slow RTL simulation. Applied under human supervision, the flow evolved a single-cycle RV32I core into a three-wide out-of-order RV32IM core reaching 5.61 CoreMark/MHz, with FPGA evaluation 9.6x faster than RTL simulation.

entry.title: Heterogeneous Co-Evolution Learning for Tool-Efficient Search Agents with Zero Labels

author.name: Qin-Wen Luo, Sheng Ren, Xiang Chen, Rui Liu, Jun Fang, Naiqiang Tan, Jun Wang, Hua Chai, Sheng-Jun Huang
