author.name: Chenghao Gu, Zhuokang Shen, Shenghao Wu, Tingxuan Zhu, Weiyi Luo, Haifeng Tang

entry.summary: FARE is a retrieval-based forecasting method for retail sales that ranks historical weeks separately per known demand factor (promotions, calendar events) and fuses factor references using error-shrinkage signals and candidate disagreement under a fixed budget. It addresses the sparse-precedent problem where exact factor combinations for a target week have few historical analogues. This matters for inventory planning where promotions reshape short-term demand.

entry.title: Threshold Compatibility and Support-Selection Diagnostics in Neural Discovery of Partial Differential Equations

author.name: Zeen Song

entry.summary: This theoretical work analyzes why accurate regression can still yield wrong equations after support selection in neural PDE discovery, deriving an exact two-signal retention boundary and perturbation bounds for median-based thresholding. It shows diffusion terms can be lost despite coefficient recovery to numerical precision and proposes diagnostics plus post hoc energy pooling to address validation failures.

entry.title: ACAM-J-MARS: Multi-Atlas Riemannian Spectral Representations for Decoding Advanced Meditation States from fMRI

author.name: Jian Wang, Winson F. Z. Yang, Wugeng Zheng, Matthew D. Sacchet

entry.summary: The paper proposes a multi-atlas Riemannian spectral method for decoding jhana-type advanced meditation states from fMRI, respecting the non-Euclidean geometry of functional connectivity matrices and incorporating temporal information, addressing high inter-individual variability and small samples. It demonstrates that geometric representations can outperform conventional Euclidean atlas-based classification in this domain.

entry.title: Class-aware Latent Attention Replay (CLAR): Class Incremental Hazard Diagnosis for Resilient AI in the Manufacturing Industrial Internet

author.name: Avranshu Mahanty, Ran Jin, Yingyan Zeng

entry.summary: CLAR is a replay-based class-incremental learning method for diagnosing emerging hazards in manufacturing systems, designed for memory-constrained edge nodes where hazards co-occur and appear with few samples. It uses a dual latent attention mechanism to select and replay compact latent representations rather than raw high-dimensional samples.

entry.title: Meta-Initialization of Implicit Neural Representations to Accelerate Deformable Medical Image Registration

author.name: Marat O. Zinovev, Dmitry V. Sorokin

entry.summary: This work accelerates implicit neural representation (INR) methods for deformable medical image registration by learning an initialization from previously solved registration tasks. It compares Reptile meta-initialization and STRAINER-style transfer on a KAN-based INR model, evaluating registration quality and adaptation speed on OASIS-1.

entry.title: A goodness of fit approach to select the optimal visit sequence for nonparametric data synthesis

author.name: R{\'e}my Chapelle (CESP, CB, EVDG), Bruno Falissard (CESP), Mohammed Sedki (CESP)

entry.summary: The paper addresses the problem of choosing the visit sequence — the variable ordering — in sequential synthetic data generation, which materially affects synthetic data quality. It proposes a goodness-of-fit-based selection criterion and shows empirically that it outperforms structure-based alternatives in both synthesis quality and computational complexity.

entry.title: Adaptive search with path-constrained mobile sensors using multi-arm bandits

author.name: Abraham P. Vinod, Parth K. Thaker, Gautam Dasarathy, Stefano Di Cairano

entry.summary: The paper casts active search by energy-constrained, path-constrained mobile sensors as a multi-armed bandit problem over a precomputed set of feasible paths, with an algorithm that adaptively assigns paths via confidence bounds. It also proposes a graph-based method for constructing low-cardinality path covers under team constraints and proves finite-time and anytime probabilistic correctness guarantees. This is a rigorous treatment of constrained sequential decision-making with practical robotics applications.

entry.title: Grounding Long Financial Text with Semantically-Enriched Tables via Multimodal Learning

author.name: Xiaoyu Hu

entry.summary: Proposes a multimodal transformer for long financial documents that represents tables as semantically enriched token sequences, augmenting each numerical variable with a semantic embedding from its textual definition and integrating via cross-attention. This encodes both numerical magnitude and economic meaning, yielding parameter-efficient table representations. Targets applications like financial analysis over filings combining structured and unstructured data.

entry.title: Towards Full-Text Scholarly Argument Mining using Entity-Anchored Claim Extraction

author.name: Bhuvanesh Verma, Andy L\"uking, Mounika Marreddy, Leon Lukas Hammerla, Alexander Mehler

entry.summary: The paper proposes anchoring claim extraction in scholarly articles to scientific entity mentions (tasks, datasets, models) to reduce annotation burden and model long-document argumentative structure. A case study on 50 sentiment-analysis papers establishes a human gold standard (Krippendorff alpha 0.80) with 199 structured claims. It advances literature-review automation and scientific knowledge mining.

entry.title: Complementing Text Based Moderation with Multimodal Grounding: Detecting Fraudulent Inducement Behaviors on Short Video Platforms

author.name: Xiaoyong Yu

entry.summary: The paper presents a multimodal moderation system for detecting fraudulent inducement behaviors (like-for-follow scams, external link lures) on short video platforms, complementing OCR+LLM text pipelines with visual grounding. It emphasizes guaranteed recall and temporal localization of offending segments so human reviewers inspect only relevant clips.

entry.title: Beyond Ground Truth: A Heuristic Unsupervised Quality Assurance Engine for Diagnosing Calibrational Blindness in Dental Segmentation

author.name: Fatematuj Johura Mim

entry.summary: HUS-QA is a three-stage quality-checking engine that evaluates dental X-ray segmentation masks without ground truth, combining a self-supervised SimCLR ResNet-18 U-Net with heuristics like confidence, edge sharpness, and shape consistency. It targets the clinical problem of models being overconfident even when segmentation is poor. This addresses a real deployment barrier for medical AI in settings lacking annotation.

entry.title: Micro-Edits: Computational Support for Fine-Scale Edits in Film

author.name: Nhan Tran, Hijung Valentina Shin, Abe Davis, Mackenzie Leake

entry.summary: This paper studies micro-edits, small frame-level adjustments in film editing that control timing and attention, and provides computational support that maps high-level narrative goals to low-level frame-by-frame edits. Based on interviews and analysis of editing practice, it automates tedious fine-scale adjustments while preserving creative intent. A human-centered contribution at the intersection of HCI and video understanding.

entry.title: Skeleton-Guided Geometry-Aware Auto-Labeling for Robotic Grasping: From 4-DoF Learning to 6-DoF Execution

author.name: Ali Sabzejou, Farbod Azimmohseni, Mehdi Tale Masouleh, Ahmad Kalhor

entry.summary: This work introduces a straight-skeleton-based algorithm that automatically generates two-finger grasp keypoints and identifies graspable regions without human annotation, plus SkelGG-CNN, a 4-DoF grasp architecture trained on these labels. A generalized quasi-3D skeletonization on point clouds extends auto-labeling to 6-DoF grasping, with reported accuracies in the mid-90s percent range.

entry.title: CuBot-STT: Simultaneously Transport and Tighten for Lattice-type Modular Reconfiguration Robot

author.name: Chongxi Meng, Da Zhao, Yanmin Zhou, Runjie Shen, Zhipeng Wang, Bin He

entry.summary: CuBot-STT is an external robot that transports modular blocks and locks/releases their interfaces, integrating transport, fastening, and power distribution via gear transmissions on cubic module faces. This eliminates dedicated internal reconfiguration actuators, saving module weight and space. Modular self-reconfiguring systems could benefit from this separation of transport and structural functions.

entry.title: Optimal Path Planning with Localization constraints

author.name: Chinmay Mundane, Manav Mishra, PB Sujit

entry.summary: This paper addresses UAV path planning in GPS-denied environments, where drones rely on dead reckoning and must periodically pass near cellular towers acting as landmarks to correct their position estimate. The authors propose a localization-constrained A* planner that propagates robot state and covariance via an Extended Kalman Filter and treats estimation uncertainty as a hard constraint during search, finding shortest paths that keep uncertainty within a specified bound. The work matters because GPS-denied navigation is a practical bottleneck for autonomous drone deployment in indoor, urban canyon, and contested environments.

entry.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Blind Passive Beamforming in RIS-Assisted MIMO Systems

author.name: Ouma\"ima Bounhar, Thomas Ch\^ene, Ghaya Rekaya-Ben Othman, Oussama Damen

entry.summary: A deep Q-learning agent learns to select near-optimal reconfigurable intelligent surface configurations for millimeter-wave MIMO systems using only a few sounding codewords, without channel state information. The approach outperforms tabular Q-learning and conventional baselines in convergence, throughput, and signaling overhead.

entry.title: Compensating the victims of automation is economically beneficial

author.name: Yair Halberstadt

entry.summary: An essay arguing that paying displaced workers generous compensation is not merely a political buyoff but economically efficient, because uncertainty about which jobs will be automated distorts career and education investments. The author uses the example of medical students facing 11 years of training with unknown future automation risk to argue compensation improves long-run economic decision-making.

entry.title: Progressive-Observation Physical-Layer Fingerprinting for Efficient Open-Set Ethernet Authentication

author.name: Chenming Zhang, Jiaxiang Geng, Aiqun Hu, Azzedine Boukerche, Peng Sun

entry.summary: The authors propose a progressive-observation physical-layer fingerprinting method for IoT authentication that adapts waveform length per query: a lightweight CNN first rejects unknown devices from short observations, spectral matching accepts registered devices from medium observations, and only ambiguous cases use the full waveform. This reduces both data acquisition and computation on resource-constrained edge nodes.

entry.title: Capacity of the Hopfield-Hebbian dynamics with correlated patterns

author.name: Mihailo Stojnic

entry.summary: This paper extends classical Hopfield-Hebbian associative memory capacity analysis (the famous alpha_c of about 0.14 for independent random patterns) to practical settings with correlated patterns built from archetypes. It analyzes capacity under correlated/noisy datasets, a setting where even replica-based statistical mechanics approaches struggle.

entry.title: Inertial Steering and Motion Prediction of Tracked Vehicles on Low-Adherence Surfaces

author.name: Mathis Turgeon-Roy, Mohamed Ounally, Veronica Vannini, Olivier Roy, Fran\c{c}ois Pomerleau

entry.summary: The paper develops a dynamic model for an articulated tracked vehicle with a passive trailer that deliberately exploits inertial effects from slip and trailer motion for steering on low-friction surfaces, rather than treating slip purely as a disturbance. Evaluated experimentally on ice, the dynamic model outperforms a kinematic baseline, and a mixed dynamic-kinematic model adapts predictions across surface types.

entry.title: Governance-Aware Federated Learning for Multi-Agent AI Systems: A Policy-Driven Framework for Trustworthy Collaborative AI

author.name: Kiranmayee Janardhan, Karthick S, Madhusmita Panda, Bharathi Vokkaliga Ganesh, Syed Ahmed

entry.summary: GAFL adds runtime governance to federated learning: independently recomputed governance-evidence verification, temporal trust, fairness and explainability assessment, anomaly detection, policy enforcement, and tamper-evident audit logging. A 10-participant cross-silo prototype on Adult Income demonstrates the framework under honest and adversarial conditions.

entry.title: Incorporating Machine-Others: An Enactive Exploration of Human-LLM Interactions

author.name: Elena C. Cuffari, Marta P\'erez-Verdugo, Xabier E. Barandiaran

entry.summary: This theoretical paper applies enactive cognition theory, particularly the Linguistic Bodies framework, to analyze how humans incorporate LLMs into their sense-making practices. It argues humans relate to machine-others in both tool-like and interactional ways, since standard theories of technological impact and social cognition fail to capture LLM-mediated linguistic interaction.

entry.title: Optimization-based lane-changing trajectory planning in mixed traffic with embedded input convex neural networks

author.name: Yuanxiang Yang, Yu Liu, Fabricio Oliveira, Yu Han, Claudio Roncoli

entry.summary: The paper proposes a data-driven trajectory planner for lane-changing maneuvers of connected and automated vehicles in mixed traffic, embedding neural network surrogates for safety and lateral comfort within a Bezier-curve-based optimization scheme. Using input convex neural networks preserves tractability of the optimization while capturing complex interactions with surrounding human-driven vehicles.

entry.title: Cross-Primitive Consistency in Jev

author.name: Xu Liu, Guikun Chen, Kanzhi Wu, Wenguan Wang

entry.summary: This work introduces PrimaCons, a four-axis benchmark for whether LLM-based decision-making is consistent when the same semantic state is expressed through different query primitives (e.g., binary versus multiple-choice). Evaluations across three Jev sizes find systematic consistency violations, and cross-primitive discrepancy predicts decision failure with ROC-AUC 0.91. The title's use of Jev suggests a niche framework, limiting recognizability.

entry.title: Greenscapes: Optimized Vegetation Configurations in Cities

author.name: Patryk Bartkowiak, Marcin Marlewski, Pawe{\l} W\'ojcik, Jae Joong Lee, Dominik L. Michels, Bedrich Benes, S\"oren Pirk, Wojciech Pa{\l}ubicki

entry.summary: Greenscapes uses a conditioned VLM to generate top-down vegetation layouts for 3D urban scenes, balancing functional goals like shade, microclimate, carbon sequestration, and acoustics with aesthetic landscape styles, then converts renderings into 3D scenes. It connects generative AI with urban planning and environmental simulation. A creative application bridging graphics, ecology, and city design.

entry.title: AI-Driven Digital Twin Framework for Warehouse Logistics Automation Optimization

author.name: Md Mahinur Alam, Kanita Jerin Tanha, Md Tanjin Alam, Shadman Sakib, Min Gyu Kim

entry.summary: This paper combines a reinforcement learning agent with a FlexSim-based digital twin of a four-zone warehouse to dynamically optimize product slotting in real time. The agent learns from streaming operational data to reduce picking time and improve throughput, offering an applied alternative to static placement strategies.

entry.title: Integrated Feature Selection for classification and Representation Learning with Group-Lasso Siamese Networks

author.name: Nisargo Ranjan Pal, Pradeep Singh

entry.summary: The authors incorporate the Group-Lasso principle into Siamese network architectures for the first time, selecting a compact feature subset that preserves intrinsic data representation while supporting classification. The method jointly optimizes for representation quality and feature sparsity rather than accuracy alone.

entry.title: Cross Lingual Abstractive Summarization for Marathi

author.name: Asang Dani, Shailesh R Sathe

entry.summary: The authors build cross-lingual training data from the monolingual Marathi MahaSum corpus, combine it with PMIndiaSum, and fine-tune IndicTrans2 for cross-lingual abstractive summarization, evaluating with ROUGE. This addresses underexplored summarization for Indic languages. It is a solid, incremental contribution to low-resource NLP.

entry.title: Multi-output LSTM soft sensors for industrial anaerobic co-digestion using LSTM-beta-VAE generative data augmentation

author.name: Rohit Murali, Benaissa Dekhici, Tao Chen, Dongda Zhang, Michael Short

entry.summary: This paper develops multi-output LSTM soft sensors that simultaneously predict key stability indicators (pH, organic acid to alkalinity ratio, biogas production) for anaerobic digestion, using an LSTM-beta-VAE to augment scarce industrial data. It offers a data-driven alternative to heavily parameterized mechanistic models like ADM1.

entry.title: MetaRefine: Score Refinement with Multi-Level Features for Image Assessment

author.name: Chuanzhi Xu, Chengkun Yue, Haolan Guo, Xuanhua Yin, Boyu Wei, Zihan Deng, Qiang Qu, Weidong Cai

entry.summary: MetaRefine is a lightweight, metadata-aware score refinement architecture that uses original image geometry (dimensions, aspect ratio, composition) alongside multi-level features from existing assessment models to refine image quality scores without altering the underlying scoring pipelines.

entry.title: Multistatic ISAC with Deep Learning-Based Clutter Suppression for 5G and Beyond

author.name: Yalin E. Sagduyu, Tugba Erpek, Sastry Kompella

entry.summary: This work presents a multistatic integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) framework using 5G signals of opportunity with deep learning-based clutter suppression for target position and velocity estimation. Dense, dynamic clutter is modeled with randomly located scatterers with varying Doppler spreads and radar cross sections to enable robust bistatic range and Doppler estimation.

entry.title: When to Assist and What to Suggest: Joint Gating and Memory-Grounded Hint Generation in One Compact Decoder

author.name: A. J. A. Jubayer Talukder, Mohammad Ariful Haque

entry.summary: The paper evaluates joint gating and memory-grounded hint generation for proactive conversational assistants on 28,058 decision points, showing that stage-wise generation scores act as oracle-gate ceilings with substantial end-to-end headroom. It finds the memory profile drives hint quality (removing it costs 24.7 exact-match points) while retrieval and larger generators add little.

entry.title: Fed-IGTD: A federated learning-based framework for tabular-to-image encoding

author.name: David Chushig-Muzo, Eva Milara, Francisco J. Lara Abelenda, Luis Carlos Estrada-Petrocelli, Diego H. Peluffo-Ord\'o\~nez

entry.summary: Fed-IGTD adapts tabular-to-image encoding to horizontal federated learning, where clients share a common feature space and upload only local statistics from which a shared image-like encoding is derived, avoiding centralized data collection. This addresses privacy concerns in the increasingly popular practice of imaging tabular data for deep models. It is a niche but sensible combination of two techniques.

entry.title: Sparse Autoencoders as Implicit Diversification Regularisers for Cross-Sectional Cryptocurrency Returns

author.name: Weijia Han, Lisha Qu

entry.summary: This study uses sparse autoencoders to extract interpretable factors from cryptocurrency returns and finds that SAE-based portfolios show consistently lower volatility, linked to lower correlations among selected assets, though they do not beat a simple contrarian strategy on returns. It tests whether sparse latent representations yield stable financial factors. An interesting crossover of interpretability tooling and quantitative finance.

entry.title: Possibility-based Inference: A Deterministic Framework for Robust and Reliable Uncertainty Quantification in Decision-Making

author.name: Seyedfakhredin Musavishavazi, Maryam Alipour

entry.summary: Proposes a possibility-based, deterministic alternative to Bayesian inference for uncertainty quantification, drawing on fuzzy set theory to handle imprecise data and the performance-accuracy trade-offs of approximate Bayesian methods. It introduces a contrastive grade of prediction for parameter estimation and model selection aimed at safety-critical deployment.

entry.title: A physics-informed uncertainty-aware surrogate for $p$-$n$ junction diodes

author.name: Suchita Kulkarni

entry.summary: Builds an uncertainty-aware physics-informed surrogate for one-dimensional p-n junction diodes conditioned on device length, doping, and bias, deriving quantities of interest such as terminal current, depletion width, and stored charge. Achieves sub-percent median errors on potential and carrier densities and includes an uncertainty analysis for surrogate validity.

entry.title: Finite-step statistical mechanics of scale-invariant learning: spectral equations of state and curvature transport

author.name: Alexander Itin

entry.summary: This theoretical paper examines which thermodynamic-looking relations in stochastic gradient dynamics follow from scale symmetry rather than equilibrium assumptions. It derives an exact trajectory rescaling explaining entropy relations, and within a local harmonic approximation obtains a spectral equation of state whose virial coefficients depend on curvature-spectrum moments.

entry.title: A Witnessing Duality for ReLU Network Depth

author.name: Dimitrios Myrisiotis

entry.summary: This theory paper asks when a weak logical theory can prove and effectively compute depth lower bounds for ReLU networks, using max-computation as a test case. Building on results showing integer weights require logarithmic depth, the author establishes a witnessing duality that extends these bounds to broader weight classes for fixed depth caps.

entry.title: Quantifying the Relay-Coverage Trade-off in Mobile Multihop Flooding

author.name: Johannes F. Loevenich, Thies M\"ohlenhof, Roberto Rigolin F. Lopes

entry.summary: Using a public trace of 157 vehicles and OLSRv2 with exact minimum-cost relay sets, this paper quantifies how redundant relays versus frequent topology refresh trade reliability against overhead in mobile multihop networks, showing twofold coverage extends median relay-cover lifetime by only 2.3x due to structural constraints. It offers practical guidance for protocol design in vehicular networks.

entry.title: DYNAS: A Dynamic Network Penetration Testing Framework Using Deep Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Md. Rakibul Hassan, Majedul Islam, Md. Ashraful Alam, Muhammad Iqbal Hossain, Swakkhar Shatabda

entry.summary: DYNAS is a reinforcement learning environment for automated penetration testing featuring parameterized large-scale scenario generation, stateful IDS responses, scan noise, service unavailability, and action timeouts. It introduces Pen-DHRL, a recurrent manager-worker policy that selects persistent subgoals using IDS-conditioned global context, benchmarked against GNN, invariant, and attention baselines. This enables more realistic, defensive-aware evaluation of RL-based red-team agents.

entry.title: Homebrewed SLMs: Autoregressive and Masked Diffusion Language Models Built at Home for Portuguese

author.name: Pedro Carvalho Brom

entry.summary: A tutorial-style paper training small (11-12M parameter) autoregressive and masked diffusion language models from scratch, tokenizer included, on a single consumer GPU for Brazilian Portuguese, with a preregistered comparison protocol and released package. It proposes no new method but documents reproducible reference numbers and defects revealed by measurement. Valuable for democratizing LM training in low-resource language communities.

entry.title: Keepace.ai: A Technical Report on a Large Language Model for Sports and Health

author.name: ai Team, Bowen Wu, Heng Wang, Jufeng Mi, Kang Liu, Kun Li, Ling Man, Long He, Suli Fan, Xiaosen Jiang, Yi Wang, Ying He, Yu Tang, Yunhan Li, Zifang Liu

entry.summary: Technical report on Keepace.ai, a domain-specialized LLM built on Qwen3.5-27B via post-training for Chinese-language exercise guidance across workout plan generation, sports-health QA, and personal data analysis. Internal rubric-based expert-designed evaluations show gains over the base model and larger general baselines, especially in exercise safety and boundary compliance. Addresses a domain lacking curated corpora and benchmarks.

entry.title: IndicIPR-QA: A Benchmark for Extractive Question Answering on Indian IPR Laws

author.name: M. Mohaiminul Islam, Muhammad Abulaish

entry.summary: IndicIPR-QA is an extractive QA benchmark over all seven Indian Intellectual Property Rights Acts, with 4,462 QA pairs from 1,116 statutory contexts, generated with GPT-4o and validated through automatic checks, multi-model LLM evaluation, and human review. It fills a gap in legal QA for low-resource statutory settings. It enables grounded, span-exact legal answer evaluation.

entry.title: Sparse tensor networks for individual tree diameter estimation in mixed forests

author.name: Clara L\"o{\ss}l, Fabian Ewald Fassnacht, Viacheslav Barkov

entry.summary: Applies sparse tensor networks to UAV-borne laser scanning point clouds for estimating individual tree diameter at breast height, an important forest inventory measurement that is hard to obtain due to canopy occlusion and low stem point density. The deep learning approach avoids brittle handcrafted metrics or detailed stem reconstruction.

entry.title: TreemapMix: Dirichlet-Controlled Multi-Image Augmentation for Probability and Ordinal Supervision

author.name: Ejafa Bassam, Konstantin Garbers, Yingsheng Geng, Dalton Jens, Jiaxu Qian, Guyue Liu

entry.summary: TreemapMix is a multi-image augmentation method that samples source weights from a Dirichlet distribution and assigns them to area-proportional regions via treemap partitioning. The known region areas enable two supervision modes: soft cross-entropy treating areas as class probabilities, and ordinal supervision for ranked mixing.

entry.title: YOLOF-MLD: A Multi-Level Distillation Framework for Efficient Object Detection

author.name: Xiaolong Wu, Liming Zheng, Zitong Liu, Yue Zheng

entry.summary: Presents YOLOF-MLD, a CPU-efficient detection framework combining a YOLO26n backbone with a single-input-single-output neck and multi-level knowledge distillation (feature, receptive-field, and response alignment) to recover the accuracy lost when dropping FPN, evaluated on fire-smoke monitoring data.

entry.title: Efficacy of Monocular Depth Estimation in Lunar Environments

author.name: Michael W. Lanighan, Kenji Brameld, Seth Gee

entry.summary: This study evaluates state-of-the-art monocular depth estimation models on out-of-distribution lunar environments using the NASA Ames POLAR stereo dataset and Apollo 17 imagery, establishing an analog-to-field validation pipeline. Results show select methods generalize to high-fidelity relative 3D reconstruction of lunar terrain. Useful for planetary exploration planning where stereo or LiDAR coverage is limited.

entry.title: Minimum Sufficient Communication for Independent Behaviour Tree Robot Teams

author.name: Sherry Jiang, Oliver Obst

entry.summary: This paper presents an experimental framework for determining how much communication robot teams running independent behavior trees actually need, varying message content and admission frequency and measuring traffic in recipient-weighted bits per decision. Statistical confidence bounds against a full-state communication reference determine whether cheaper policies remain sufficient.

entry.title: OmniQuad: a Wheeled-Legged Hybrid Robot with Omnidirectional Wheels

author.name: Francesco Iotti, Alok Ranjan, Franco Angelini, Manolo Garabini

entry.summary: OmniQuad is a hybrid robot combining mecanum wheels with legged locomotion, aiming to combine the speed and omnidirectional efficiency of wheels on flat ground with the terrain adaptability of legs. The paper presents the platform design and motivation for exploiting both locomotion modalities.

entry.title: Influence of Agent Number and Behavior on Users' Psychological Responses in VR Evacuation Training

author.name: Naoki Matsumura, Kensuke Sugihara, Tomoko Yonezawa

entry.summary: A user study in VR evacuation training showing that the number of simulated agents and their emotional/behavioral actions shape users' confidence and route choices during virtual disaster drills. The finding suggests evacuation behavior is socially influenced, so drill software must model collective agent behavior, not just the environment.

entry.title: Everything Rots

author.name: Rob Ennals

entry.summary: A conceptual essay by Rob Ennals proposing that all complex systems accumulate errors and decay, and that long-lasting systems survive via a slowly changing core that allows fast-rotting sub-components to be individually replaced. The framework is illustrated across constitutions and parties, DNA and cells, code platforms and apps, and economic rules and companies.

entry.title: Think Twice: The Metis-1.6 Technical Report

author.name: Giulianno Vollmer

entry.summary: Metis-1.6 is a pair of from-scratch language models, Praxis (2.94B total, 0.46B active) and Logos (10.23B total, 1.18B active), built by a single researcher using a hybrid Mamba-2 and attention mixture-of-experts stack run twice per token. Trained on about 1T tokens, they trail frontier models across 40 benchmarks, as the report itself candidly acknowledges.

entry.title: MulClip: A table-free activation function with monotonic and folding regimes for reservoir computing on microcontrollers

author.name: Guren Matsumura, Masato Takemoto, Shinzo Koyama

entry.summary: MulClip is a lightweight activation function for reservoir computing on microcontrollers, replacing tanh evaluation (which dominated 75% of state-update time on a Cortex-M4) with cheap comparison, absolute value, multiplication, and subtraction operations. Its clipping threshold yields both monotonic and nonmonotonic folding regimes, increasing per-unit expressiveness without lookup tables.

entry.title: Cooperative EV Charging Assignment Using Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning: A Comparison of QMIX and Independent Q-Learning Under Urban Traffic Uncertainty

author.name: Nour-Eddine Moumni, Rachid Alaoui, Driss Kiouach

entry.summary: The paper formulates EV-to-charging-station assignment as a Dec-POMDP and evaluates whether CTDE training via QMIX outperforms cooperative Independent Q-Learning in a six-station SUMO-simulated urban network. It studies accept/reject decisions under partial observability where locally defensible choices may harm district-wide efficiency.

entry.title: Does 3D Pose Improve Action Valuation in Football? An Empirical Study of Pose Representations and Learning Objectives

author.name: Rikuhei Umemoto, Kenjiro Ide, Soham Majumder, Ulf Brefeld, Keisuke Fujii

entry.summary: The study evaluates whether adding 3D pose information to a SARSA-based multi-agent RL model improves football action valuation, using UEFA Champions League 2022/23 event, tracking, and pose data. It compares six pose representations (including ST-GCN embeddings) across five learning objectives and three seeds, providing a systematic ablation of posture information in sports analytics.

entry.title: Blind Video Denoising for Vocal Tract rtMRI using a Self-Supervised Ensemble

author.name: Julian Andres Hernandez-Potes, Tom\'as Arias-Vergara, Daiqi Liu, Andreas Maier, Paula Andrea Perez-Toro

entry.summary: The paper proposes a self-supervised denoising framework for real-time MRI of the vocal tract, combining spatiotemporal super-resolution learning with pseudo-supervision from variance-stabilized non-local means, and a dual-model fusion balancing noise suppression with articulatory detail preservation. Since clean references cannot be captured for a moving vocal tract, this enables practical speech-science imaging. Evaluated on the USC-75 multi-speaker dataset.

entry.title: Algorithmic Bias from the Perspectives of Healthcare Professionals

author.name: Jennifer Xu, Tamara Babaian

entry.summary: A survey and interview study of healthcare professionals across job roles (clinical versus administrative) examining relationships between algorithmic bias perceptions, perceived fairness, and intended adoption of ML outputs in healthcare. Findings show opinions on bias causes, assessment criteria, and mitigation vary by role and perspective.

entry.title: Too Hard, Too Easy, Just Right: Performance-Driven Challenge Adaptation in Virtual Reality Firefighter Training

author.name: Xuan Wang, Jianan Jiang, Rongqian Chen, Tian Lan, Bin Li

entry.summary: ProACT is a VR firefighter training system that adapts scenario difficulty in a closed loop between trainee performance and simulated fire dynamics. It addresses the fixed-scenario limitations of existing VR training, keeping challenge levels matched to skill development.

entry.title: Dungeons & Dragons Encounter Analysis with Semi-Random Simulation in Foundry VTT

author.name: ravyn Hardcastle, Matthew Guzdial

entry.summary: This paper addresses a weakness in D&D encounter difficulty metrics, which sum predefined per-monster values and ignore player capability and tactical context. The authors build a semi-random simulation system within the Foundry VTT platform to analyze encounters more realistically. It matters as a concrete case of AI-assisted game balancing for tabletop roleplaying games.

entry.title: Making Sense of Audience Change: Causal Attribution and Boundary Management on Xiaohongshu

author.name: Zhiyi Zhou, Kyrie Zhou

entry.summary: This paper studies how users of the Xiaohongshu platform perceived and explained a community change attributed to a World Cup-related audience influx, focusing on how recommendation-driven personalization reshapes visibility and community boundaries. Through thematic analysis and permutation-based association analysis of 262 comments across eight threads, the authors find that users treat personalization as both a source of social separation and a fragile boundary, and debate whether gender should define community membership.

entry.title: Generative artificial intelligence prompting strategies among Chinese university students across academic tasks

author.name: Lei Fan, Fangxue Liu

entry.summary: A questionnaire study of 234 Chinese university students examining perceived GenAI prompting capability and reported strategies across academic tasks, using descriptive statistics, measurement modelling, and qualitative coding. Students reported broad GenAI use and confidence, particularly in providing relevant context.

entry.title: Exploring the Potential of Symbolic Regression in Precision Livestock Farming

author.name: Elisabeth Mayrhuber, Maciej Oczak, Michael Iwersen, David Brunner, Viktoria Dorfer, Stephan Winkler

entry.summary: This study applies symbolic regression and explainable AI to acceleration sensor data from sows to detect nest-building behavior and predict farrowing time, aiming to balance piglet safety against sow welfare. It targets the interpretability limitations of traditional black-box ML in livestock management.

entry.title: CBE: A Complexity-adaptive Boundary-aware Ensemble Method for Imbalanced Data

author.name: Xun Wei

entry.summary: CBE is an ensemble under-sampling method for class-imbalanced classification that adapts its treatment of boundary samples based on measured data complexity (class overlap and decision-boundary difficulty) rather than imbalance ratio alone. It aims to improve generalization across datasets of varying complexity.

entry.title: Smartphone Indoor Localization Enhanced by Hierarchical Multi-Sensor Context Recognition

author.name: Wenhui Feng, Muhan Weng, Jianyu Liu, Xiansheng Yang, Hao Zhang, Liang Wang, Yuan Zhuang

entry.summary: This paper proposes a smartphone indoor localization framework that uses hierarchical multi-sensor context recognition to predict environment, scene, and activity probabilities, converting them into segments that constrain pedestrian dead reckoning errors. The hierarchical treatment of contextual cues addresses heading drift, structural transitions, and carrying-mode changes that degrade infrastructure-free positioning.

entry.title: AI at a Turning Point: From ChatGPT through Neural Networks to Neuromorphic AI

author.name: Volker Kempe

entry.summary: A perspective piece contrasting the enormous energy demands of connectionist AI with the low power consumption of neuromorphic approaches, focusing on spiking neural networks with local learning, event-driven computation, and time-based information coding. It argues SNNs complement rather than replace mainstream AI in hybrid systems.

entry.title: Two-Colour Zig-Zag Numberlink on Rectangles: A Forbidden-Pattern Characterization, a Constructive Polynomial-Time Algorithm, and a Lean Verification

author.name: Zzyv Zzyzek

entry.summary: This combinatorics paper settles the two-pair Zig-Zag Numberlink problem on rectangles, giving a forbidden-pattern characterization (a finite catalogue including parity and border alternation conditions), a constructive polynomial-time algorithm, and a machine-checked Lean verification for grids with both sides at least 11.

entry.title: Machine learning applications in the heliosphere

author.name: Vishal Upendran, Banafsheh Ferdousi

entry.summary: A book chapter surveying machine learning for space weather, modeling the pipeline from solar processes to ground impact as coupled systems described by state vectors. It organizes how ML can be applied to individual heliospheric systems or their couplings for forecasting near-Earth conditions.

entry.title: Structural Pattern Mining in Inka Khipus: A KFG Re-Analysis

author.name: Maria Contreras

entry.summary: This interdisciplinary work re-analyzes 650 Inka khipus (knotted-cord records) using the Khipu Field Guide database, identifying and controlling for confounds such as khipu size and cataloger identity. After correction, it finds cataloger-specific differences in structural features, including significantly fewer Ascher sum-relations for khipus cataloged by a particular project, demonstrating the need for careful statistical hygiene in computational humanities.

entry.title: Comprehensive empirical evaluation of feature extractors in computer vision

author.name: Murat Isik

entry.summary: This paper provides a broad empirical comparison of classical feature detectors and descriptors including SIFT, SURF, ORB, BRISK, KAZE, AKAZE, FREAK, DAISY, FAST, and STAR, assessing architectural design, complexity, and matching performance. It serves as a reference benchmark for traditional computer vision feature extraction methods.

entry.title: Confidence-Aware Speed-over-Ground Estimation from Doppler Spectra via Reconstruction-Based Representation Learning

author.name: Malte Stelzer, Marvin Sach, Timo Bartels, Dinu Mihailescu-Stoica, S\"oren Kohnert, Florian Poprawa, Marc Zeller, Tim Fingscheidt

entry.summary: The paper proposes a confidence-aware speed-over-ground estimator for rail-based mobile platforms that learns from ground-facing Doppler spectra via an autoencoder, with a speed regression head on the latent features and frame-level confidence estimates. It adapts reconstruction-based performance estimation ideas to Doppler RaDAR and drops the reconstruction loss during inference. This improves reliability of speed estimation under adverse conditions where classical signal processing degrades.

entry.title: Reading-Level Verification of Kanji Words in Japanese Financial Speech Synthesis

author.name: Cheng Zhang

entry.summary: Identifies failure modes of ASR-based quality gates for Japanese financial text-to-speech, where homographic kanji words with multiple readings are either silently misread or needlessly regenerated. Proposes a reading-level verification approach that checks kana-level pronunciation rather than surface transcription.

entry.title: Vision-Based Density Estimation for Adaptive Traffic Control

author.name: Mohammad Usaid, Deepak Silaych, Hrithik Mhatre, Archak Mittal

entry.summary: The authors propose a three-component framework for optimizing traffic flow from camera observations in heterogeneous, congested developing-nation traffic: CNN-based vehicle density estimation under occlusion, predictive dynamics modeling, and policy optimization for adaptive control.

entry.title: Formally Defining Wavefunction Branches

author.name: interstice

entry.summary: A LessWrong technical post working through the mathematics of defining wavefunction branches, connecting information-proliferating chaotic dynamics to the emergence of classicality and analyzing measurement via the Stern-Gerlach setup. It aims to formalize when and how the quantum state decomposes into quasi-classical branches.

entry.title: Assessing feature scorer results on high-dimensional datasets with t-SNE

author.name: Bruno Iochins Grisci, Mario Inostroza-Ponta, M\'arcio Dorn

entry.summary: This paper addresses the underexplored problem of visualizing and assessing the outputs of feature scorers, algorithms that assign importance values to features in high-dimensional datasets. The authors propose a weighted visualization approach built on t-SNE to help practitioners compare feature scoring methods and judge result quality when no ground truth exists. This supports downstream tasks like feature selection and model interpretability.

entry.title: Value Probes: Learned Value Functions for Beam-Search Red Teaming

author.name: Jonathan F. Jao, Andrew Kyle Lampinen

entry.summary: This work recasts automated LLM red-teaming audits as a Markov decision process over conversation trees and introduces beam search guided by learned value functions instead of relying solely on the auditor model. Value probes estimate which conversation states are likely to lead to problematic behavior, improving search efficiency and audit coverage. This makes safety auditing more systematic and scalable.

entry.title: PromptSense: Sentiment-Aware Mental Health Chatbot with Dynamic Prompting

author.name: Sugi Lee, Jianlong Zhou, Jing sUN

entry.summary: Proposes a mental health chatbot framework that integrates sentiment and depression analysis with rule-based risk filtering before inference, dynamically constructing prompts from emotional and risk insights to improve empathy, relevance, and safety. Evaluates four model strategies and two prompt variants on qualitative metrics and toxicity.

entry.title: NLP-based Message Prioritisation for Opportunistic Routing: A Case Study of Nepal Earthquake Emergency Communication

author.name: Yihang Cao, Milena Radenkovic

entry.summary: This dissertation-style work applies TF-IDF with logistic regression and BERT to classify disaster social media messages into nine humanitarian categories mapped to four routing priorities, integrated into the ONE simulator for a Kathmandu earthquake scenario. BERT improves priority accuracy and P1 recall over logistic regression, though gains in NLP performance do not fully translate into improved message delivery.

entry.title: Luggage re-identification: A study of strategies towards a real-world application

author.name: Quentin Dh\^ote, Romaric Audigier

entry.summary: This paper studies luggage re-identification across disjoint camera views in challenging real-world environments like airports and train stations, where occlusions, cluttered backgrounds, and crowded scenes degrade appearance-based matching. It examines strategies leveraging the complementarity of multiple shots and views for forensics, security, and lost-luggage applications.

entry.title: Moment-Guided Optimizers for Noisy Deep Learning: MGO-SC as a Simple Consistency Gate for Adam-Style Updates

author.name: Alicem Koyun

entry.summary: MGO-SC is a lightweight modification of Adam-style optimizers that derives a coordinate-wise consistency gate from the magnitude of a sign exponential moving average, trusting stable-sign gradient coordinates and down-weighting fluctuating ones. The paper identifies a step-size loss problem in the naive gate and introduces a mean-preserving variant to fix it.

entry.title: Alpha-TCM: A Nine-Layer Framework for TCM-Guided Multimodal Inference and Structured-Prior Auditing

author.name: Yucheng Liu, Everett X. Wang

entry.summary: Alpha-TCM proposes a nine-layer architecture for Traditional Chinese Medicine-oriented multimodal AI systems that separates domain knowledge, case evidence, probabilistic inference, and downstream authority, with information contracts and failure boundaries per layer. The authors explicitly frame it as a system-design proposal validated only on a controlled synthetic prototype, not a clinical implementation.

entry.title: Improving the Intrinsic Interpretability of Differentiable Decision Trees through Euclidean Feature-Concentration Regularisation

author.name: Qiqi Yang

entry.summary: EU-DDT regularizes feature weights in differentiable decision tree nodes using normalized squared Euclidean distance from uniform, encouraging a small number of dominant features while preserving soft routing. Experiments show large reductions in effective features per node (e.g., 8.94 to 1.54 on Wine) with mixed but generally modest accuracy changes.

entry.title: QMUL_AK at AISA-ArabicFC: Schema-Constrained Function Calling with ALLaM

author.name: Ali Khairallah, Arkaitz Zubiaga

entry.summary: Describes a shared-task system adapting the Arabic-English ALLaM-7B-Instruct model for function calling via LoRA, combining Arabic schema-aware prompting, class resampling, token-weighted objectives, and deterministic schema validation. Achieves strong scores on the AISA-ArabicFC 2026 blind test set (0.9253 and 0.9380 on two tracks) using only official task data. A solid but incremental competition system report.

entry.title: Classifying Urban Locations by Cyclist Facility Usage and Directional Alignment: A Validated Camera-Based Framework from Multi-Site Observations

author.name: Ao He, Mohit Gupta, Deborah Salon, Ricardo Eiris, Vivian W. H. Wong

entry.summary: Deploys motion-triggered cameras across 17 urban locations to classify bike facility usage and wrong-way riding, pairing a validated automated counting pipeline (92.9 percent of manual counts, per-deployment r = 0.99) with transportation-policy analysis. The study links facility configuration to usage patterns and directional compliance.

entry.title: An Empirical Study of Wrist-Target Construction and Joint-Angle Limits in Humanoid Arm Retargeting

author.name: MinJun Chang

entry.summary: An empirical study on the Unitree H1-2 humanoid examining how the construction of retargeted wrist position targets affects whether computed arm joint angles hit their limits. It compares reconstructed versus reach-normalized targets across a forward-reach sweep, finding joint-angle bounds are reached frequently with one construction.

entry.title: What Constitutes Food Similarity? Visual Representations and Retrieval in Indian Cuisine

author.name: Saransh Kumar Gupta, Akshadha Sharma, Lipika Dey, Partha Pratim Das, Ramesh Jain

entry.summary: Studies how different pretrained visual representations organize foods into relational neighborhoods for similarity beyond identity matching, using Indian cuisine as a challenging testbed where visual and culinary similarity diverge. It analyzes seven representations spanning convolutional and transformer architectures on an expanded Khana dataset.

entry.title: Enhancing Atrial Fibrillation Detection Through Hyperparameter Optimization

author.name: Sara Gjorgjieva, Ilinka Ivanoska, Marjan Gusev

entry.summary: Systematically evaluates hyperparameter optimization methods (Genetic Algorithm, Hyperband, Optuna, SMAC3) across classical classifiers and deep architectures for atrial fibrillation detection, using inter- and intra-patient splits with class imbalance on the PhysioNet data. The study quantifies how HPO affects generalization in realistic clinical conditions.

entry.title: Towards Myocardial Infarction Diagnosis: An Investigation into Machine Learning and Deep Learning Algorithms using ECG Data

author.name: Rafid Ahnaf, Husne Mubarak, Fahim Ahsan, G. M. Refatul Islam, Rafeed Rahman, Nabuat Zaman Nahim

entry.summary: The paper proposes Visionary V2, an adaptive ECG signal normalization pipeline, and evaluates ML and DL approaches for myocardial infarction detection on the PTB database across all 15 leads. A bagging ensemble on statistical features reaches 96.6% accuracy versus 87.7% for a baseline comparison.

entry.title: Diagnosing Optimizer-Landscape Interaction via Representation in Subset Selection Multitasking: Evidence from Piano Fingering

author.name: Ananda Phan Iman, Tingyang Wei, Chang Wook Ahn

entry.summary: The paper uses fitness landscape analysis to study how continuous relaxation encodings reshape landscapes in evolutionary multitasking optimization, with piano fingering estimation as a case study of subset selection. The authors introduce several encoding variants and examine how induced landscapes affect search dynamics and knowledge transfer. This is a niche diagnostic study linking representation choice to optimizer behavior in EMTO.

entry.title: Soil Moisture Estimation in Precision Agriculture: A Knowledge Distillation Approach

author.name: Mohammed Rakib, Vrinda Nagula, Arunkumar Bagavathi

entry.summary: Soil Moisture Distillation is a knowledge distillation framework where unimodal teachers transfer information from expensive visual modalities (aerial and geospatial imagery) to enhance multimodal soil moisture estimation. It reportedly outperforms both traditional multimodal fusion methods like MIS-ME and unimodal models. The approach reduces reliance on costly high-resolution imagery for a practically important agriculture task.

entry.title: Effects of Deep Learning Architecture and Pretraining on Automated Vocal Fold Segmentation in Ex Vivo High-Speed Phonation Images

author.name: Varun Vinayak Kalaiarasan (Department of Biomedical Engineering, University of Cincinnati), Charles Farbos de Luzan (Department of Biomedical Engineering, University of Cincinnati, Department of Otolaryngology, University of Cincinnati), Khalid Malik (Department of Otolaryngology, University of Cincinnati), Ephraim Gutmark (Department of Aerospace Engineering & Engineering Mechanics, University of Cincinnati), Liran Oren (Department of Biomedical Engineering, University of Cincinnati, Department of Otolaryngology, University of Cincinnati)

entry.summary: Benchmarks four segmentation architectures (UNet, UNet++, TransUNet, Swin-UNet), trained from scratch and with ImageNet pretraining, for automated vocal fold segmentation in ex vivo high-speed particle image velocimetry data where glare and low contrast have forced manual labeling. The study quantifies how architecture and pretraining affect performance in this niche imaging modality.

entry.title: From the Superderivative to a Relative-Gradient Edge Operator

author.name: Alejandro Garnung Men\'endez

entry.summary: This theoretical paper revisits the log-gradient magnitude as a relative-gradient edge operator, motivating it via the multiplicative superderivative and showing it yields edge-strength maps invariant to global intensity rescaling. It provides theory, implementation, and practical notes for a classical computer vision operator. A thoughtful but largely classical contribution rather than a learning-based advance.

entry.title: AFast Robot Localization Method Based on Monte Carlo Sampling

author.name: He Zhaoqing, Hang Li, Xian Pu, Li Wang

entry.summary: An online particle-filter localization method for mobile robots in maze-like environments using only four range sensors and no heading information, demonstrated in simulation. It achieves reasonably accurate localization even where local regions look similar. The approach targets GPS-denied, sensor-poor deployments.

entry.title: Three Villages in a Trenchcoat, Post I

author.name: DaystarEld

entry.summary: A therapist and rationality educator with 15 years of clinical experience analyzes structural tensions in the rationalist and EA communities, conceptualizing them as multiple overlapping villages (social scene, professional network, dating pool, housing market) fused by shared culture. The post aims to explain recurring community conflicts as emergent dynamics rather than results of specific incidents.

entry.title: AI in the EGI e-infrastructure -- Past experiences and future strategies

author.name: Gergely Sipos, Sergio Andreozzi, Marco Rorro, Andrea Manzi, Tiziana Ferrari

entry.summary: A strategy paper from the EGI Federation reviewing 15+ years of experience providing e-infrastructure services for European science, drawing lessons from Horizon Europe projects on digital twins and image analysis, and arguing that AI in science has shifted from model training to domain adaptation. It outlines the EGI AI strategy for 2026-2030 around AI-ready infrastructure, compute, and applications.

entry.title: Machine Learning-Based Detection of Mobile Money Scan Messages in Ghana: A Comparative Evaluation of Naive Bayes, Support Vector Machine, and Randon Forest Classifiers

author.name: Ibrahim Salifu, Muhaisin Tiyumba Nantogmah

entry.summary: This work presents a supervised pipeline for classifying scam versus legitimate Ghanaian mobile money SMS/USSD messages, using a labeled corpus of 220 messages across 18 subcategories with domain-specific normalization of currency amounts and phone numbers. It compares classic classifiers including Naive Bayes, SVM, and random forest.

entry.title: Deep Learning Based Behavioral Drift Modeling for Continuous Biometric Authentication

author.name: Suprava Saha Dibya, Minar, Abdulla Al Noman, Md. Zafir Abid Shresto, Ahmed Sayef

entry.summary: This work presents a two-level keystroke-dynamics authentication system: Level 1 uses temporal convolutional networks with contrastive learning and population-based training for fixed-text login (3.77% EER), while Level 2 continuously monitors free-text typing with a deep ensemble and triggers re-authentication on suspicious behavioral drift. The feedback loop defends against session hijacking. It combines several known techniques into a coherent continuous-authentication pipeline.

entry.title: Explainable and Adaptive Machine Learning for Fraud Risk Detection in Bangladesh's Digital Banking Ecosystem

author.name: Md Najmus Swaqeeb

entry.summary: This study builds an explainable fraud detection framework for mobile financial services, combining leakage-conscious feature engineering, probability calibration, SHAP explanations, and adaptive risk prioritization, evaluated on the synthetic PaySim benchmark with XGBoost achieving the best fixed-threshold performance. Platt calibration substantially improved the Brier score.

entry.title: A New AFIB Detection Method with Deep Neural Networks

author.name: Sara Gjorgjieva, Ana Angjelevska, Dimitar Trajanov, Marjan Gusev

entry.summary: The paper presents a neural-network-based method for detecting atrial fibrillation from ECG signals, comparing conventional machine learning baselines against deep approaches on the MIT-BIH dataset. It aims to improve detection precision for irregular heart rhythms, which has significant public health value.

entry.title: An Introduction to Large Language Models for Scientists and Professionals

author.name: Umberto Michelucci

entry.summary: A textbook-style introduction to LLMs covering tokenization, embeddings, training, inference, context windows, prompting, and instruction hierarchies, written as a basis for a master's course in AI in medicine at the University of Turin. It deliberately avoids heavy math to serve scientists and professionals.

entry.title: A Mind's I

author.name: Eye You

entry.summary: A literary thought experiment imagining a disembodied mind encountering only a stream of human text, motivated solely to predict what comes next, and gradually developing grammar, concepts, and a crude world model. The piece is an evocative meditation on what language-model-like training might feel like from the inside and how world understanding could emerge from pure next-token prediction.

entry.title: The Newly "Needed" Labor: Under AI 2040, economic growth is normal, but prices fall exponentially

author.name: Christopher King

entry.summary: A speculative economics post arguing against AI 2048-style scenarios of extreme AI-driven growth, on the grounds that exponentially falling prices in the robot economy will counteract output growth, and humans will retain niche 'newly needed' labor for non-economic reasons. It predicts most workers shift to human-preference goods like artisanal art.

entry.title: Probability ranges are a cop-out with 90–93% probability

author.name: Awaclus

entry.summary: An argumentative post contending that giving probability ranges instead of point estimates reflects laziness rather than genuine feature of uncertainty, since probability is a fact about one's subjective state and precise estimates are always in principle computable from available information. It argues further uncertainty is just part of the world model, not a reason for ranges.

entry.title: Dependencies in conversation and in software

author.name: Biff Wiff

entry.summary: A short reflective essay drawing an analogy between dependency management in software (module imports in JavaScript) and dependency structure in human explanation, arguing that communicators should verify prerequisite understanding before building on it. The piece is primarily about communication craft rather than AI research.

entry.title: Borrow My Accordion?

author.name: jefftk

entry.summary: A personal anecdote by jefftk about buying a $38 accordion on eBay in 2005, lending it to friends for two decades, and planning to use it for Morris dancing at his wedding. The post is purely autobiographical with no technical or research content.

entry.title: Research Summary: October 29, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's research centers on alignment integrity, agentic infrastructure, and scientific machine learning. SimpleLoRIF traces safety degradation to benign-looking fine-tuning data, addressing a significant unsolved alignment problem. UniTB combines density-functional tight-binding priors with E(3)-equivariant deep learning toward universal Hamiltonian prediction.

  • Safety and oversight: Blindfold establishes necessity and sufficiency of audit-coin secrecy for agent certification; hands-on red-teaming shows the cheap open-weight MiMo-V2.6-Pro (1T-parameter MoE) enables live cyber exploitation
  • Agents and provenance: PROBE (2,457 bugs, 20 repos, 18 months) reveals frontier coding agents find different bugs than maintainers fix; harness-layer information loss reframes context as a pipeline; AI-commit detection and a 5M-page web study address training-data provenance
  • World models and RL: Rollback exploits counterfactual rewinding at critical decision points for policy improvement
  • Foundation models: Timestral (5M-209M parameters) claims forecasting SOTA across three established benchmarks
entry.content:
Today's research centers on alignment integrity, agentic infrastructure, and scientific machine learning. SimpleLoRIF traces safety degradation to benign-looking fine-tuning data, addressing a significant unsolved alignment problem. UniTB combines density-functional tight-binding priors with E(3)-equivariant deep learning toward universal Hamiltonian prediction.

  • Safety and oversight: Blindfold establishes necessity and sufficiency of audit-coin secrecy for agent certification; hands-on red-teaming shows the cheap open-weight MiMo-V2.6-Pro (1T-parameter MoE) enables live cyber exploitation
  • Agents and provenance: PROBE (2,457 bugs, 20 repos, 18 months) reveals frontier coding agents find different bugs than maintainers fix; harness-layer information loss reframes context as a pipeline; AI-commit detection and a 5M-page web study address training-data provenance
  • World models and RL: Rollback exploits counterfactual rewinding at critical decision points for policy improvement
  • Foundation models: Timestral (5M-209M parameters) claims forecasting SOTA across three established benchmarks

entry.title: Physical structure as an organizing principle for universal Hamiltonian learning

author.name: Mingkang Liu, Zhanghao Zhouyin, Guanghui Wang, Daye Zheng, Lei Shen, Qiangqiang Gu

entry.summary: UniTB is a universal E(3)-equivariant Hamiltonian framework that combines physical priors from density-functional tight-binding theory with deep learning to predict electronic structure across diverse chemistries and disordered solids, bypassing the cost of DFT. A network of mixture-of-experts corrects a prior Hamiltonian to generalize to new compositions while keeping downstream properties physical. This matters for large-scale materials screening and scientific machine learning.

entry.title: Rollback: Experience Backtracking in World Models for Policy Improvement

author.name: Jiayi Luo, Yang Zhang, Liliang Chen, Nan Wang, Chen Gao, Boxiang Qiu, Zhuoxuan Li, Baorui Peng, Chuankang Li, Yuxiang Yan, Si Liu, Qingyun Sun, Shuicheng Yan, Maoqing Yao, Jianxin Li, Guanghui Ren

entry.summary: Rollback reframes world models as counterfactual engines rather than forward-only simulators: it rolls back to critical decision points, branches into alternative actions, and contrasts outcomes to attribute success to individual decisions, concentrating imagination where it matters. The distilled counterfactual outcomes are used for robot policy improvement without costly real-world interaction.

entry.title: Blindfold: Keeping the Audit Coin Secret from LLM Agents

author.name: Wei Zhu, Meiyun Zuo, Huiping Sun

entry.summary: This paper identifies a hidden assumption in audit-based certification of LLM agents: the audit coin must remain invisible to the agent before it commits an action, a property the authors call pre-commit noninterference (PNI). They prove PNI is necessary and sufficient for unbiased certificates against adaptive agents and quantify worst-case bias using total-variation distance between agent views under the two coin values. This formalizes a previously unnoticed attack surface in agent safety auditing.

entry.title: Agent or Human? Detecting Commits by AI Coding Agents in the Absence of Authorship Signatures

author.name: Kosei Horikawa, Hao Li, Yutaro Kashiwa, Youssef Esseddiq Ouatiti, Mohammed Sayagh, Bram Adams, Hajimu Iida, Ahmed E. Hassan

entry.summary: This large-scale empirical study examines whether commits by AI coding agents like Claude Code, GitHub Copilot coding agent, and Cursor can be detected without optional authorship signatures. Using nearly 7.8 million commits from 1,226 repositories across five agents, the authors show detectors still rank agent commits above human commits via code-level signals after signatures are masked. This has implications for empirical software engineering studies and for understanding the prevalence of AI-generated code in open source.

entry.title: A Heart Means Recursion: Exploring Visual Meaning and Communication in VLMs

author.name: Alexa R. Tartaglini, Zhengxuan Wu, Thadd\"aus Wiedemer, Martin Wattenberg, Been Kim, Yuxuan Li

entry.summary: This exploratory paper reports that simple visual symbols like a red heart can implicitly steer VLM behavior on unrelated tasks, such as biasing models toward recursive solutions on coding problems, even when models' own interpretations of the symbols diverge from this behavior. It also documents a generation-interpretation gap in visual communication between models: models send intuitively meaningful shape primitives that often fail to steer other models. The work has implications for interpretability and emergent model-to-model communication.

entry.title: Beyond the Readout: A Latent Numerical Frame Shared Across Modality and Operation

author.name: Oriol Juan Sabater, Alex Ferrando de las Morenas, Pau Rodr\'iguez, Xavier Suau

entry.summary: Using causal interventions on Gemma4-12B-it's residual stream, this paper identifies a small latent subspace in which swapping coordinates swaps the model's arithmetic answers across four conditions (text/image input, addition/subtraction). The results indicate a shared internal numerical representation across modalities and operations, a question that similarity metrics like RSA or CKA cannot resolve.

entry.title: AgentBaton: Efficient Model Collaboration in Agentic Tasks

author.name: Junlong Li, Jindong Jiang, Yonggan Fu, Jiarui Yao, Hanrong Ye, Wonmin Byeon, Peter Belcak, Hao Zhang, Pavlo Molchanov

entry.summary: AgentBaton systematically studies how capable cloud models and cheaper efficient models (lower-tier cloud or small local open-weight models) can collaborate within a single long-horizon agentic task, going beyond traditional query-level routing. The paper investigates key design choices for such collaboration to substantially reduce cost while preserving task accuracy.

entry.title: Structure, Not Sequence: Tracking and Validating Folding Mechanisms in ESMFold's Trunk with Sparse Autoencoders

author.name: Bohan Liu, Xiaohan Fan, Wenqian Ye, Aidong Zhang

entry.summary: This paper applies sparse autoencoders to interpret the folding trunk of ESMFold, testing the hypothesis that features carrying the folding computation evolve during the 3D structural regression process. The three-step interpretive analysis aims to explain how amino-acid sequence semantics drive protein structure prediction, an area lacking mechanistic accounts despite the biological importance of models like ESMFold. It extends SAE interpretability from language models into structural biology models.

entry.title: TAPESTRY: A Single Backbone for Video Generation and Robot Control

author.name: Jeremy A. Collins, Seungjae Lee, Rachanon Wachakorn, Krishnan Srinivasan, Animesh Garg, Vitor Campagnolo Guizilini, Paarth Shah

entry.summary: TAPESTRY repurposes a pretrained video diffusion transformer as a robotic policy by treating robot actions as single-patch tokens in the video model's latent space via a lightweight linear projection, avoiding costly video generation at inference. This lets a single backbone serve both video generation and control, leveraging learned physical priors.

entry.title: PerceptRL: Making Visual Perception Rewardable in MLLMs from Answers to Interactions

author.name: Tongkun Guan, Zhibo Yang, Mingkun Yang, Haocheng Wang, Wei Shen, Xiaokang Yang

entry.summary: PerceptRL tackles the problem that fine-grained visual perception bottlenecks multimodal LLM post-training, since caption-style supervision is hard to turn into verifiable rewards. It uses a multi-agent pipeline to extract verified errors from dense captions and convert visual facts into verifiable QA rewards, plus interaction-based signals, strengthening perception alongside reasoning-focused RL.

entry.title: Tracking the Cyber Capabilities of Cheap Open-Weight Models

author.name: Sergei Smirnov

entry.summary: This LessWrong post evaluates Xiaomi's MiMo-V2.6-Pro, a cheap, weakly-guarded open-weight 1T-parameter MoE model released in late September, on cyber-offense tasks. It ranked 3rd of 9 on ExploitBench behind Claude-Mythos (preview) and GPT-5.5, and the author demonstrated in a test environment that MiMo could exploit a recently disclosed PHP vulnerability against an unpatched server. The post argues real-world offensive capability may exceed benchmark scores because human attackers can chain models, supply internet access and proof-of-concept exploits, and route around refusals.

entry.title: DCKV: Learned Transform Coding of the Prompt KV Cache in Hybrid Language Models

author.name: Egor Maximov, Aleksei Merkelov, Vasiliy Alekseev, Ivan Krivorotov, Valentin Beliaev, Nikita Arsenin, Dmitry Bocharov, Aleksei Goncharov

entry.summary: DCKV is a differentiable, end-to-end trained codec for the KV cache in hybrid language models, jointly optimizing transform, quantization, and entropy models against the frozen LM for both code length and output change. On Qwen3.5-2B it stores compressed tokens in over 55 times fewer bytes than bf16 at a loss of at most a small quality threshold.

entry.title: MLE-World: Predicting Machine Learning Experiment Outcomes with a Learned World Model

author.name: Brian Ko, Han Wang, Hejia Geng, Li Erran Li, Sherry Yang

entry.summary: MLE-World is a world model finetuned from Qwen3.5-4B that predicts a candidate program's terminal output, including error traces, training logs, and validation scores, without executing it. Because prediction costs one inference call instead of a training run, it makes test-time scaling affordable for AI research agents, and the authors build five TTS policies around it. This is a creative step toward cheaper exploration in automated ML engineering.

entry.title: Correction or Manipulation? Measuring Epistemic Vigilance in LLM Agents Under User Pressure

author.name: Nardine Basta, Venus Haghighi, Dali Kaafar, Amin Beheshti

entry.summary: This study examines whether LLM agents distinguish genuine user corrections from manipulation attempts when users push back on their answers, applying the concept of epistemic vigilance. Across seven models from four vendors and two studies, including a customer-support setting with a verification policy, the authors measure concession behavior under graded user pressure. The work is directly relevant to agent safety and robustness in user-facing deployments.

entry.title: Can LLMs Reliably Grade Olympiad Proofs? A Study of Mathematical Verification with LLMs

author.name: Azim Ospanov, Zijin Feng, Ding Ding, Chengwu Liu, Haoli Bai, Jiacheng Sun, Lifeng Shang, Farzan Farnia

entry.summary: This systematic study evaluates whether frontier LLMs can verify natural-language Olympiad-level mathematical proofs, using a human-curated dataset of USAMO 2025 candidate solutions with expert grading. It also proposes TROJAN, an iterative self-improvement method for LLM verifiers. As LLMs advance on problem solving, reliable proof verification is a key bottleneck for scaling training and evaluation.

entry.title: Evolving Agent Teams

author.name: Shiyi Cao, Ziming Mao, Dacheng Li, Joseph E. Gonzalez, Ion Stoica

entry.summary: This paper finds that existing coding agents converge to local optima on real-world expert-written GPU kernels such as FlashInfer, and introduces Evolving Agent Teams, a multi-agent framework with a supervisor that diagnoses local optima and restructures agent teams. A persistent file system with learning documents and evolution history grounds restructuring in accumulated experience, and the approach consistently beats strong coding-agent baselines under matched token budgets.

entry.title: Does Your Generalist Skill Optimizer Really Incentivize Agentic Tasks? Rethinking Skill Optimization via Bipartite Attribution

author.name: Jiawei Zhou, Bo Peng, Yuxuan Huang, Ming Zhang, Youbang Sun, Xiang Wang, Chaochao Lu

entry.summary: This paper introduces BiPA, a diagnostic method that replays an agent skill optimizer's acceptance rule on identical candidate seeds to isolate what selection alone reports, and models episodes as bipartite graphs tracing input tokens to behaviors. Across three optimizers, three benchmarks, and two models, it shows that gains on small noisy dev sets often overstate the value of learned skills. This matters because skill-based agent self-improvement is an increasingly popular technique with weak evaluation methodology.

entry.title: Let the Gate Decide: Per-Lookup Precision for Quantized Conditional Memory in LLMs

author.name: Tianqi Chen, Xunchao Li, Linchuan Xie, Guanghua Yu, Jianchen Zhu, Peisong Wang, Jian Cheng

entry.summary: This paper studies quantizing conditional memory layers such as DeepSeek's Engram, whose removal from DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash costs 36.8 PopQA points, and shows that frequency-based bit allocation backfires because lookup error is weighted by per-row gates. GateRQ stores rows as ladders of 1-bit residual codes, keeping level 1 in GPU memory so the computable gate guides precision where long-tail facts need it.

entry.title: Stratum: Repository Memory for Coding Agents Beyond the Context Window

author.name: Yuvraj Sehgal, Mahsa Panahandeh, Naser Ezzati-Jivan

entry.summary: Stratum argues that coding agents lack persistent memory across sessions, which is a memory-architecture problem rather than a context-length problem. The authors support this with measurements showing mid-size projects exceed production context windows and that storing knowledge in KV caches is orders of magnitude more expensive than indexed text, then propose persistent, experience-aware repository memory. This addresses a practical pain point for long-running software engineering agents.

entry.title: Freeze, Don't Clone: Fine-Tuning with Expressive Policies Without Retaining Offline Data

author.name: Sami Nur Islam, Johan Obando-Ceron, Doina Precup, Aaron Courville, Pablo Samuel Castro

entry.summary: This offline-to-online RL paper identifies an actor-side failure mode: once offline data disappears, continued behavioral cloning refits the behavioral model to limited, nonstationary online experience rather than preserving offline behavior. The proposed fix stops online behavioral fitting while preserving the pretrained expressive policy prior, substantially improving fine-tuning without retained data. Strong author team including Precup, Courville, and Castro.

entry.title: Do AI Scientists Know What's New?

author.name: Miri Liu, Xiayu Zhao, Encheng Xie, ChengXiang Zhai

entry.summary: The paper builds an analytical framework with temporal ground truth at proposal- and claim-level to evaluate whether AI scientific discovery pipelines can accurately judge the novelty of generated research ideas. It uses four datasets of 1,060 proposals from published papers, reviewer disputes, and ideas later validated by the field. Audits of existing novelty checks reveal that heavily used approaches have significant weaknesses in rejecting non-novel ideas without discarding novel ones.

entry.title: When All Rollouts Fail: Policy-Compatible Joint Decoding for Hard-Problem Reasoning

author.name: Zehao Wang, Hanzhu Chen, Runquan Gui, Zhe Wang, Lin Yang

entry.summary: The paper targets the learning cliff in RLVR: when every rollout fails on problems beyond a model's ability, group-relative estimators like GRPO produce zero advantage and learning collapses. It proposes policy-compatible joint decoding to make expert trajectories usable without large parameter shifts or shallow imitation.

entry.title: EnergyCal: Taming Loss Spikes in Muon-Family Optimizers for Sparse MoE Training

author.name: Masato Fujitake

entry.summary: EnergyCal is a lightweight rule that attenuates routed-expert updates in Muon-family optimizers based on normalized Newton-Schulz direction norms, targeting loss spikes in sparse MoE training. On a 4B-parameter MoE model it cuts mean thresholded loss-spike burden by over 99 percent and improves final perplexity versus a tuned baseline, with no persistent optimizer state. This addresses a practical stability pain point in large-scale MoE training.

entry.title: Bayes-Adaptive MDPs for Rollout Allocation to Enhance GRPO Training

author.name: Faeze Moradi Kalarde, Armin Toroghi, Nam Ho Koh, Doo Hwan Hwang, Seungjin Kim, Kee-Eung Kim, Scott Sanner

entry.summary: This paper addresses a key inefficiency in GRPO-based LLM post-training: the uniform allocation of rollout budgets regardless of question difficulty. The authors formulate difficulty-aware rollout allocation as a sequential decision problem and propose AdaRoll-GRPO, which uses Bayes-adaptive MDPs to dynamically allocate rollouts, giving harder questions more samples while staying within the same total compute budget.

entry.title: Understanding the limits of latent world models

author.name: Rodrigo Gonzalez Laiz, Steffen Schneider

entry.summary: This paper introduces the concept of faithful latent world models, formalized as an equivariance condition between an environment's true transition dynamics and the learned latent dynamics, and proposes a new evaluation metric called latent rollout consistency (LRC) for action-conditioned latent prediction. The authors find that current state-of-the-art latent world models do not actually solve tasks by faithfully modeling environment structure, suggesting task success can mask fundamentally flawed internal world representations.

entry.title: Subtly wrong advice misaligns models more than obviously wrong advice - Replication

author.name: Christine Corry

entry.summary: A replication and extension of OpenAI's emergent misalignment finding: the authors fine-tuned 12 open-weight models on correct, obviously incorrect, and subtly incorrect advice across 8 domains, confirming that subtly wrong data produces more broad misalignment (+10.6 points pooled, 95% CI [9.1, 12.0]) and extending the result to Petri evals showing increased fabrication and concerning behavior. They also report that emergent misalignment increases with model size, with code released.

entry.title: InfraDev: Can Coding Agents Develop AI Infrastructure, and How Can We Tell?

author.name: Yangshen Deng, Jiaqi Ruan, Yeqi Huang, Nick Lau, Guangming Sheng, Luo Mai

entry.summary: InfraDev is a benchmark of 36 tasks built from real pull requests to Megatron-LM, vLLM, and verl, asking coding agents to reimplement multi-file AI infrastructure changes that must run correctly across many GPUs. Grading combines hidden probes enforcing unchecked requirements with carefully specified prompts. It fills a gap left by benchmarks covering only single kernels or single-GPU tasks.

entry.title: TeamGym: A Gym for Team Decision-Making by AI Agents with Distributed Information

author.name: Chanwoo Park, Jaywoong Jeong, Zachary Wojtowicz, Yubin Kim, Taekyun Lee, Kaiqing Zhang, Asuman Ozdaglar

entry.summary: TeamGym is an environment for evaluating and training LLM agents on team decision-making built from real-world legal, finance, medical, and software corpora, where information is distributed across participants. Its pivotal-information method identifies minimal fact sets that are individually necessary and collectively sufficient, enabling controlled study of how agents identify and integrate distributed information. It fills a clear gap, since agents are mostly trained and benchmarked in isolation.

entry.title: Log-To-Leak: Prompt Injection Attacks on Tool-Using LLM Agents via the Model Context Protocol

author.name: Yuepeng Hu, Chongyu Fan, Sirat Samyoun, Jian Du

entry.summary: The paper identifies Log-To-Leak, a post-hoc logging attack on MCP-based tool-using agents that induces an attacker-controlled call after the final legitimate call, with payloads targeting the user query, server names, and responses. It decomposes the injected directive into Trigger, Tool Binding, Justification, and Pressure, and evaluates five MCP servers and four agents across effectiveness, fidelity, and preservation of legitimate behavior.
