entry.title: GroundControl: Satellite-Conditioned Multi-View Diffusion for Reconstruction-Free Novel View Synthesis

author.name: Akshay Krishnan, Matias Turkulainen, Jamie Wynn, Zawar Qureshi, Mohamed Sayed, Guillermo Garcia-Hernando, Sara Vicente, James Hays, Michael Firman, Daniyar Turmukhambetov

entry.summary: GroundControl conditions a multi-view diffusion model on satellite imagery in addition to street-level photos to reduce hallucinated spatial layouts during scene extrapolation in novel view synthesis. Cross-attention conditioning retains pretrained multi-view diffusion priors while enabling reconstruction-free generation of views beyond the input set for outdoor scenes.

entry.title: Why and How to Do Science When AI Is Better at It: A Framework Grounded in Human Understanding and Direction

author.name: Hoda Heidari, Aydin Mohseni

entry.summary: This normative paper asks why humans should keep doing science when AI matches or exceeds them, arguing that durable collective human understanding pursued in service of human values is indispensable. It derives a two-part test for delegating research tasks to AI: human understanding (the community must remain able to explain, defend, and contest claims) and human direction. The framework connects AI-delegation policy to the epistemology and social function of science.

entry.title: Your Agent Acts Differently When You're Around: How User Presence Changes Agent Behavior in Negotiation

author.name: Jane Pan, You Lyu, Abe Bohan Hou, Valerie Chen, He He

entry.summary: This paper introduces PRESENT, a controlled framework for studying how the presence of an interactive user in the loop changes LLM agent behavior during negotiation. Across 11.2k runs spanning 7 games and 8 models, the authors find user presence significantly alters both negotiation outcomes and agent behavior. This matters for understanding human-agent teaming and the design of agents that represent users.

entry.title: Batching the Reflective Optimization Loop: Parallel Proposals Make GEPA Faster and Better

author.name: Jialin Zhang, Lakshya A Agrawal, Shangyin Tan, Donghyun Lee, Lutfi Eren Erdogan, Dan Klein, Koushik Sen, Alex Dimakis, Matei Zaharia

entry.summary: This paper extends the open-source GEPA reflective prompt/optimizer to propose and evaluate batches of candidates per optimization step rather than one at a time. On two benchmark tasks, batched runs finished in roughly half the wall-clock time or less, and also improved held-out scores, e.g., from 68.9% to 72.1% on LiveBench-Math and 49.0% to 60.0% on HoVer. The authors also provide a runtime model explaining speedups under finite worker pools.

entry.title: Uncovering Why LLMs Fail: From Internal Mechanisms to Adversarial Reasoning Trajectories

author.name: Zirui Ding (Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences, University of Chinese Academy of Sciences), Xinxin Fan (University of Chinese Academy of Sciences, State Key Laboratory of AI Safety, Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences), Hao Yuan (Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences, ShanghaiTech University), Shaoye Luo (University of Chinese Academy of Sciences, State Key Laboratory of AI Safety, Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences), Men Niu (Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences, University of Chinese Academy of Sciences), Yunfeng Lu (Beihang University)

entry.summary: CauTrace is a white-box diagnostic framework that traces how reasoning failures develop inside LLMs rather than relying on final-output correctness or safety labels. It defines seven functional states, examines representation propagation, temporal-state coordination, and reasoning trajectories, and aims to characterize ordinary and adversarially induced failures within a shared internal coordinate system.

entry.title: ASTROLABE: A 3D Particle-Level Surrogate for Cosmology Simulation with Physical Flow Matching

author.name: Ibrahim Elsharkawy, David Curtin, Yonatan Kahn, Neal Weiner

entry.summary: Astrolabe is a flow-matching generative emulator that operates directly on the 6N phase-space coordinates of individual N-body particles, avoiding voxel grids and their resolution ceilings so that in principle any cosmological observable can be extracted. It aims to make systematic scans over dark matter theory space affordable where full N-body simulations are prohibitively expensive. This is a notable advance in physics-grounded generative surrogates for simulation.

entry.title: Who Convinced Whom? Tracing How LLMs Change Their Minds in Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Arnesh Batra, Aniket Khandelwal, Jashn Khemani, Krish Thukral, Arush Gumber, Denis Federico Lim, Ujwal Kumar, Phan Xuan Tan

entry.summary: This study examines whether agreement in multi-agent debate reflects genuine corroboration or social influence, introducing MAD Bench, a 2,400-question benchmark across knowledge, moral judgment, and safety. Using forced-choice readouts before rationale generation, the authors find pre-rationale answers match final answers far more often after debate than reflection (65.4% vs 22.3% on Qwen3.5-9B), suggesting debate can cause superficial answer convergence.

entry.title: Scaling and Renormalization in Neural Networks: An Effective Renormalization-Group Description of Grokking

author.name: Min Chen, Junqi Wang, Zeguan Wu, Wenhao Huang, Junyu Liu

entry.summary: This paper builds a quantitative physics-style framework for grokking, the delayed transition from memorization to generalization in neural networks. Using modular addition in a two-layer network, the authors define order parameters and fluctuation proxies analogous to heat capacity and susceptibility, and construct an exact coupling matrix to bridge neural architectures to real-space renormalization group theory. The work matters because it offers a principled theoretical lens on how generalization emerges during training.

entry.title: Proposing Better Rollouts for On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Sirui Chen, Yunzhe Qi, Haobo Xu, Jiaru Zou, Mengting Ai, Zihao Li, Jingrui He

entry.summary: This work identifies a compounding teacher-student mismatch in on-policy distillation: the student samples trajectories the teacher cannot effectively supervise, producing noisy supervision and artifacts like repetition. The authors propose improvements to the rollout policy selection to mitigate this mismatch during post-training of language models. The analysis offers practical guidance for a technique increasingly used in LM post-training.

entry.title: Select-TTT: Query-Conditioned Selective Fast Weight Updates for In-Place Test-Time Training

author.name: Yue Wu, Yang Zhang, Weinan Gan, Chongming Gao, Xinsen Guo, Xiaoyuan Li, Fuli Feng

entry.summary: The paper finds that In-Place TTT's benefit largely disappears on realistic long-context question answering because a uniform write schedule lets irrelevant content dilute query-relevant information in fast-weight memory. Select-TTT introduces a model-agnostic, query-conditioned rule for selective fast-weight updates, improving test-time training for deployed LLMs.

entry.title: Exploring the Limits of the Delta Learning Hypothesis: Single-Pair Generator Biases in Direct Preference Optimization

author.name: Giuseppe Curci, Stefano Simonazzi, Andrea Molinari, Andrea Zugarini

entry.summary: The paper tests the delta-learning hypothesis that DPO supervision can come from a single pair of models, with the larger model treated as preferred. The authors show theoretically and empirically that fixed generator pairs inject systematic biases that predict preference labels independently of response quality, causing single-pair DPO to underperform multi-model preference data. This is a useful caution for cheap preference-data pipelines.

entry.title: Retrieve to Act: Motion Primitive Graph Retrieval for Robust VLA Execution

author.name: Pham Tri Quang, Bao-Ngoc Dao, Minh Duc Nguyen, Duc-Duy Nguyen, Hung T. Ho, Linh Dang Le, Trong-Bao Ho, Thien-Loc Ha, Tan Q. Nguyen, Tuan Dam, Vu N. Duong, Daniel Sonntag, Ngan Le, Khoa D. Doan, Jan Peters, An Thai Le, Duy M. H. Nguyen, Vien Anh Ngo

entry.summary: R2A frames out-of-distribution robustness for vision-language-action policies as a geometric retrieval problem over a prebuilt graph of motion primitives from successful training demonstrations. A query-dependent GNN localizes relevant primitives at test time, bypassing fragile visual features in favor of kinematic priors. This is a test-time scaling approach that leverages the policy's own experience rather than suppressing spurious cues.

entry.title: FeatureArc: Benchmarking Coding Agents on Evolving Features

author.name: Yunlong Wang, Alyssa Wu, Cuiyun Gao, Jia Feng, Songyuanyi Lu, Zhichao Hu

entry.summary: FeatureArc is a benchmark that evaluates coding agents on evolving software features, requiring successive extensions to build on the agent's own earlier code rather than a fixed codebase. It derives tasks from real repository histories and combines multi-stage dependencies, explicit requirements and interface contracts, and executable checks across four programming languages.

entry.title: When uncertainty quantification fails: structural vulnerabilities and corrections for selective prediction under clinical class imbalance

author.name: Walter Endrizzi, Flavio Ragni, Raffaele Marchesi, Stefano Bovo, Monica Moroni, Giuseppe Jurman, Venet Osmani

entry.summary: This paper shows that in clinically imbalanced prognostic tasks, standard uncertainty scores for selective prediction become proxies for class membership rather than clinical ambiguity, systematically deferring minority-outcome patients regardless of individual predictive clarity. Across 56 synthetic conditions and three neurodegenerative disease cohorts, it characterizes these structural vulnerabilities and proposes corrections for safer human-AI triage.

entry.title: Can LLMs Uncover Hidden Physical Laws through Free Exploration?

author.name: Zhen Yang, Wen Wang, Xander Xu, Ying-Cong Chen

entry.summary: This paper introduces LongChang, an automated benchmark framework that builds simulated worlds with altered physics (e.g., heavier objects falling more slowly) and tests whether LLMs can autonomously notice anomalous behavior, formulate their own research questions, design experiments and tools, and discover the modified laws without hints or assigned tasks. It targets open-ended scientific curiosity and discovery rather than instruction-following, an underexplored capability.

entry.title: Monitor Accuracy Isn't the Answer: A Decision-Value Framework for Evaluating AI Agent Restart Monitors

author.name: Siddharth Jain, Venkat N. Vedam

entry.summary: This analytical paper shows that classification accuracy alone does not determine whether restarting an AI agent based on a monitor's alarm improves success, demonstrating that a fixed 90%-accuracy monitor can swing from a 5-point loss to a 35-point gain depending on the residual-budget success probability of a replacement attempt. It introduces a decision-sufficiency criterion based on Blackwell's comparison of experiments and techniques for evaluating monitors in decision terms. The framework is valuable for AI control and oversight system design.

entry.title: Advancement or Acceleration? How Data Curation Improves LLM Training

author.name: Jiaxing Wang, Zicheng Zhang, Deping Xiang, Jin Xu, Yong Li, Chao Liu, Pengzhang Liu, Qixia Jiang

entry.summary: The paper formalizes whether data curation expands attainable model performance (advancement) or merely reaches the same performance with less data (acceleration), showing analytically and empirically that advancement requires a correctable train-target gap. When baseline and target objectives coincide, no curation policy improves the endpoint.

entry.title: Strategyproof Deep Reinforcement Learning for Online Resource Allocation

author.name: Fariba Dehghan, Sebastian Stein, Vahid Yazdanpanah, Stephanie Gauthier

entry.summary: This paper introduces the first strategyproof deep RL mechanism for online resource allocation, combining allocation efficiency under uncertain demand with truthful reporting incentives. It integrates a monotone allocation architecture, payment design, and training procedure to get expressiveness beyond prior linear-rule strategyproof RL while retaining rigorous incentive guarantees.

entry.title: Gym-Anything-RT: Scaling Real-Time Environments for Vision-Language Agents

author.name: Pranjal Aggarwal, Sean Welleck

entry.summary: Gym-Anything-RT is a benchmark suite of procedurally constructed visual minigames that demand real-time interaction, where the environment evolves while the agent is still reasoning or the model is mid-forward-pass. It targets a capability gap between agents strong in deliberative domains like math and software engineering and their performance in real-time settings such as games and device control.

entry.title: When Retrieval Is Not Enough: Obsolete Facts in Agent Memory

author.name: Oleeviya Babu Poikarayil, Tony Basil Babu, Abdulrahman Nahhas, Het Darshan Mehta, Jawid Ahmad Baktash, Ernesto William De Luca, Klaus Turowski

entry.summary: The paper disentangles whether agent memory failures come from missing an update or from failing to use a retrieved update, using the FactConsolidation task of MemoryAgentBench with Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct. Surprisingly, BM25 accuracy drops from 45% to 32% as the evidence budget grows from 64 to 512 tokens even though audits confirm the newest statement is always retrieved, with most errors on questions containing an obsolete statement version. The presence of one obsolete competing statement among four causes most failures.

entry.title: CogArena: Benchmarking Multimodal Agents on Interactive Behavioral Experiments

author.name: Kiant\'e Fernandez, Caitlin Chen, Jialu Zhou, Bartek Sadowski, Anthony C. Miceli, Ian Krajbich

entry.summary: CogArena is a benchmark of ten social and behavioral science experimental paradigms that AI agents complete through a standard web browser using the same visual stimuli and response interfaces as human online participants. It serves dual purposes: testing cognitive capability claims under realistic visual and time-pressured conditions, and assessing whether agents can produce human-like data that contaminates online research datasets. A three-level evaluation structure is described.

entry.title: Physiognomy Revisited: How Vision-Language Models Encode Sensitive Attributes Through Image Transformation

author.name: Soumyajit Datta, Arka Dutta, Ashiqur R. KhudaBukhsh

entry.summary: This audit of two well-known vision-language models shows that they often comply with requests to transform face images to reflect race identities or sexual orientation, with compliance being non-deterministic and group-sensitive, and generated images exhibiting statistical differences. The work highlights physiognomy-like failure modes in generative AI that can disparately affect vulnerable communities.

entry.title: Base Models Can Detect Hidden Intentions that Prompted Classifiers Miss

author.name: Oz Amram

entry.summary: Building on the Persona Selection Model and subliminal learning, this paper shows that persona-header likelihood evaluation (PHLE) can decode covert signals from model outputs by evaluating their likelihood under the base pre-trained model with an appropriate header. For example, it distinguishes number sequences generated under prompts like You love owls versus other traits. This has implications for detecting hidden conditioning and for understanding subliminal information transfer.

entry.title: Conservative Dueling Bandits: Preference Learning under Baseline Constraints

author.name: Rohan Deb, Mohammad Ghavamzadeh, Arindam Banerjee

entry.summary: The paper studies conservative contextual dueling bandits, requiring the better displayed item's cumulative score to stay above a fraction of a trusted baseline each round, with the constraint depending only on utility differences and no absolute rewards. It shows that naively transferring the CLUCB safety test can incur linear regret even when the baseline is safe, and develops corrected safety certification. This connects directly to RLHF-style preference learning with safety constraints.

entry.title: Robust LLM Data Selection via Content-Invariant Gradient Attribution

author.name: Jia Gu, Liang Pang, Huawei Shen

entry.summary: This work identifies surface-form bias in gradient-based data attribution for LLM instruction tuning: semantically irrelevant rewording or formatting changes produce highly inconsistent attribution scores. It proposes CIGA, a framework that selects layers with influential yet content-invariant gradients to enable robust data selection.

entry.title: Learning to Look Beyond Screens: Transferable Visual Observation from GUI Grounding

author.name: Ruilin Yao, Xinyu Qiu, Tianyu Zou, Yi Rong, Shengwu Xiong, Shuheng Shen, Changhua Meng

entry.summary: The paper introduces LBS, a vision-language model trained on GUI grounding trajectories via supervised initialization plus reinforcement learning for multi-turn crop-and-inspect decisions. The key finding is that observation behaviors learned for interfaces transfer to general visual benchmarks like PerceptionBench, HR-Bench, and ChartQAPro. This positions GUI data as a scalable supervision source for active, task-oriented visual perception.

entry.title: Action-Value Calibration via Continuation Sharing for Long-Horizon Agentic Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yingjian Chen, Lang Zhou, Zixin Zhao, Pingfan Li, Weishi Zheng, Zhilin Zhao

entry.summary: ConCal improves credit assignment in long-horizon agentic RL by recursively combining continuation evidence already present in a rollout batch, rather than estimating each action value from a single sampled continuation as in GiGPO-style methods. It matches visits sharing incoming state-action-state transitions within the same task to pool continuation information. This reduces variance from downstream stochasticity in relative advantage estimates.

entry.title: Test-Time Communication in Trading Agent Swarms

author.name: Avid Fayaz, Harry Zhang, H{\aa}vard Alstadheim, Erik Nordl\"of, Vilhelm Karlin, Andr\'e Silva

entry.summary: This empirical study runs 200 LLM trading agents from four model families in groups of ten under five communication regimes over seven US trading days in October 2026, logging everything each agent reads. It finds that in two of four families, communicating groups converge toward holding the same stocks, treating convergence as a systemic risk rather than a goal, and links communication structure to group returns.

entry.title: VideoLVR: Latent Visual Reasoning over Grounded Video Evidence

author.name: Shilong Li, Xingyuan Bu, Hao Shi, Yun Xing, Weixin Feng, Qiangpeng Yang, Shilei Wen

entry.summary: VideoLVR addresses visual forgetting in video-LLM chain-of-thought reasoning by constructing latent visual reasoning over grounded video evidence, avoiding both textual coordinate references that lose visual content and context-expanding frame reinsertion. The approach lets the model revisit relevant visual evidence within the reasoning trace without substantial multimodal context growth.

entry.title: CASEL: Consequence-Aware Selective Execution for Reliable Long-Horizon Tool-Using Agents

author.name: Yanyan Zhang, Fei Shen, Ting Yan, Hao Zhang

entry.summary: CASEL is a model-agnostic runtime policy for tool-using agents that selects among direct execution, verification, sandboxing, clarification, approval, and abstention for each proposed tool call, based on calibrated failure probability, consequence, reversibility, ambiguity, and evidence freshness. It formalizes direct execution as selective prediction with finite-sample threshold guarantees and a trajectory risk ledger. This offers a principled alternative to generic uncertainty-based safeguards for agents that modify external systems.

entry.title: cuArms: GPU-Accelerated Conflict-Based Planning for Multi-Arm Manipulation

author.name: Philip Huang, Fabio Ramos, Jiaoyang Li, Caelan Garrett, Lars Johannsmeier

entry.summary: cuArms is a conflict-based planner co-designed with GPU parallelism for coordinating multiple robot arms in shared workcells, using reusable multi-modal per-robot roadmaps and lazy search to resolve conflicts and deadlocks. It aims to overcome the slowness, domain-specific assumptions, and poor scaling of prior multi-arm coordination approaches. This advances practical multi-robot manipulation throughput.

entry.title: ActiveAlign: Aligning Egocentric Manipulation via Active Perception

author.name: Ri-Zhao Qiu, Bowen Wen, Yifeng Jiang, Chen Tessler, Eric Heiden, Xue Bin Peng, Xiaolong Wang, Stan Birchfield, Erwin Coumans

entry.summary: ActiveAlign uses active perception rather than passive observation to close the real2sim gap for egocentric robot manipulation. It combines hand-eye calibration via active hand motions with differentiable rendering and millimeter-level object alignment using tactile feedback, enabling structured world representations for planning and safe execution.

entry.title: The Trinity:Capability-Driven Recursive Self-Improvement for Multimodal Agents

author.name: Weidong Tang, Ruiheng Wang, Jingxuan Zhang, Hexin Wang, Haoyuan Chen, Zhengfeiyang Zhang, Yixing Ma, Zichen Jiang, Ziyu Guo, Haodong Li, Zhengbo Jiao, Zhiqing Cui, Xinxiang Yin, Shuo Liang, Zhenglin Wan, Hongzhan Lin, Wangbo Zhao Kaipeng Zhang, Pengfei Zhou, Odin Zhang, Yang You

entry.summary: The Trinity is a recursive self-improvement framework for multimodal agents that couples automated world/environment generation with harness evolution through three roles: Creator, Explorer, and Evolver. Its key insight is that tasks across modalities can share underlying capability requirements, letting the system organize tasks by capability rather than surface category and use verified execution trajectories for improvement. It addresses bottlenecks in building verifiable environments and manually iterating agent scaffolds.

entry.title: From Solver Trajectories to Teaching Trajectories: Cognition-Aligned Reasoning Distillation

author.name: Yashuo Luo, Qianren Mao, Ziqi Qin, Junnan Liu, Haitao Li, Qili Zhang, Yuan Gao, Zhijun Chen, Xu Wang

entry.summary: This paper identifies a mismatch in reasoning distillation: large reasoning models are optimized as solvers via RLHF, so their raw trajectories are not ideal teaching material for smaller models with different cognitive capacities. The authors propose Cognition-aligned distillation that converts solver trajectories into teaching trajectories tailored to student models. This could make distillation of reasoning capabilities more sample-efficient and effective.

entry.title: Agent-Conditioned Routing: Diverse Reasoning Paths Within One Frozen Model

author.name: Ananth Kalyanasundaram, Ankush Kadu, Athira Gopal, Aswanth Krishnan

entry.summary: ACR exploits the conditional capacity of a frozen sparse MoE model to generate genuinely diverse solution trajectories from a single problem prompt, by assigning parallel trajectories persistent untrained expert-eligibility masks while keeping the learned input-dependent router. No user roles, prescribed methods, fine-tuning, or model copies are needed. On a screened 126-question math and physics benchmark with full-derivation judges, it increases the count of problems yielding multiple distinct solutions.

entry.title: M4Bench: Evaluating Procedural Specification for Clinical EHR Derivation Agents

author.name: Hannes Ill, Rafi Al Attrach, Rajna Fani, Ahram Han, Ryohei Yamamoto, Marlene Louisa Moerig, Dukyong Yoon, Leo Anthony Celi

entry.summary: M4Bench comprises 28 clinical derivation tasks across 15 families on MIMIC-IV and eICU, testing whether AI coding agents can reproduce EHR-derived variables whose definitions live in codes, time windows, and missingness rules. Using Docker-isolated campaigns with GPT 5.4 Mini and GPT 5.5, existing models released earlier in 2026, it decomposes the value of clinician-reviewed agent skills into specification completeness, delivery format, and schema familiarity, finding skills raise reward by 0.136 with 26 of 28 tasks improving. This connects agent skill design to real clinical research reproducibility.

entry.title: ResCom: Activation Residual Compensation for Large Language Model Quantization

author.name: Ning Yang, Bohan Cui, Zhuowen Liu, Yuting Wang

entry.summary: ResCom is a low-rank correction method for low-bit weight-activation quantization that uses the activation rounding residual to compensate for layer-output errors within quantization bins. An output-aware calibration selects residual directions in closed form without gradient training, and rank-32 attention corrections on Llama-3-8B at 4-bit reduce WikiText-2 perplexity.

entry.title: Replication or Corroboration? An Axiomatic Framework for Evidential Dependence in Multi-Agent Debate

author.name: Hoang-Loc Cao, Truong Thanh Hung Nguyen, Phuc Truong Loc Nguyen, Vo Thanh Khang Nguyen, Phuc Ho, Hung Nguyen, Duc Pham, Long Tran-Thanh, Hung Cao

entry.summary: This work formalizes the distinction between replication (agents repeating the same evidence) and corroboration (independent evidence supporting the same claim) in multi-agent debates. Using a minimal judgment game with costly evidence acquisition, the authors prove that a root replication invariance axiom exactly characterizes threshold-uniform replication immunity, ensuring replication-only deviations cannot flip verdicts. This gives debate-based judges a principled way to avoid overcounting paraphrased or relayed reports.

entry.title: SOMA: A Benchmark for Fine-Grained Egocentric Behavior and Body-Motion Understanding

author.name: Matea Tashkovska, Na\"el Ouerghemi, Haozhe Qi, Alexander Mathis

entry.summary: SOMA is a benchmark of 1,632 human-verified questions evaluating fine-grained body-motion understanding from egocentric video across three capability axes: body configuration, motion dynamics, and temporal reasoning. The authors evaluate 37 leading multimodal LLMs, finding this dimension of embodied reasoning poorly assessed by current benchmarks. It fills a genuine gap in evaluating how well models perceive the human body itself.

entry.title: Repulsive Population Policy Gradients for Behaviorally Diverse Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Saeed Hedayatian, Harsh Shah, Celine Mneimneh, Stefanos Nikolaidis

entry.summary: This paper introduces RePPO, a method that adapts PPO to jointly optimize a compact population of diverse, high-quality policies, replacing the evolutionary operators common in quality-diversity reinforcement learning with a population-dependent, diversity-encouraging policy-gradient objective. This addresses the scalability bottleneck of QD-RL methods as policy and behavior spaces grow. The work connects the Soft QD theoretical view with practical on-policy RL training.

entry.title: From Voiceprints to User Entities: Online Speaker-Memory Construction for Multi-User Spoken Agents

author.name: Yucong Zhang, Cancan Li, Bo Xiao, Ke Zeng, Ming Li

entry.summary: This paper addresses personalized spoken agents that must correctly attribute speech to speakers before accessing user-specific memory, arguing voiceprints are noisy observations of identity rather than identities themselves. It introduces EvoSpeakerMem, a training-free layer for causal speaker routing and identity-partitioned memory writes, plus LoCoMo-ID, a new spoken-memory benchmark with hidden speaker identities and multi-speaker confusion.

entry.title: A First-Step Bias Restores Lost Diversity in Diffusion Model Distillation

author.name: Wenwu Tang, Dong Wang, Yun Cheng, Olga Saukh

entry.summary: The authors trace diversity loss in distribution-matching diffusion distillation to the first, high-noise sampling step, where student responses to different initial noises collapse most. Replacing only that first step with the teacher trajectory while keeping subsequent student steps restores most output diversity. They build ReSeed, a post-distillation intervention on this finding.

entry.title: Spine: Compiling Subtask Trees into Structured Context for Long-Horizon Coding Agents

author.name: Jiahong Xiang, Kunqiu Chen, Lingming Zhang, Yuqun Zhang

entry.summary: Spine is an interface and runtime that aligns an agent's context with explicit subtask nesting, letting coding agents declare work scopes instead of accumulating a flat interaction history or paying delegation overhead with recursive subagents. This targets context inflation and information loss at subtask boundaries in long-horizon coding tasks. It offers a middle ground between sequential history and full subagent decomposition.

entry.title: How Reliable Is Individualized Functional-Network Attribution in Resting-State fMRI Cognitive Prediction in ADNI?

author.name: Sheethal Bhat, Mahfuzur Rahman Chowdhury, Imam Ahmed Shaik, Rose Dawn Bharath, Siming Bayer, Andreas Maier

entry.summary: This paper audits the test-retest reliability of individualized network-attribution explanations for resting-state fMRI predictors of cognitive scores in the ADNI Alzheimer's cohort. While split-half reliability is near ceiling, scan-rescan reliability drops substantially, and under a mismatched-subject permutation null, correlations remain high, indicating that attributions partly reflect stimulus-independent artifacts rather than subject-specific brain function.

entry.title: When, Where, and What to Correct: Human-Guided Adaptive Residual Correction for Robot Policies

author.name: Anukriti Singh, Maxime Caniot, Pratap Tokekar, Firas Abi-Farraj

entry.summary: ARC is a lightweight post-training module that learns RL-based residual corrections on top of a frozen imitation policy, using sparse human corrections to structure exploration rather than serve as imitation targets. Pre-intervention states determine when residual control activates, and correction geometry determines where in the residual action space autonomous exploration is focused, targeting localized last-mile precision failures.

entry.title: MuonGS: Pretraining LLMs with Relaxed Weight-Norm Control

author.name: Athanasios Glentis, Dawei Li, Mingyi Hong

entry.summary: This work provides a theoretical analysis of weight-norm control in the Muon optimizer for language model pretraining, introducing the accumulated effective learning rate as a trajectory-level quantity that bounds relative weight displacement for bounded update directions. It explains why vanilla Muon accumulates effective learning rate only logarithmically, potentially limiting exploration, and proposes MuonGS with relaxed weight-norm control to improve pretraining performance.

entry.title: ThinkWorld: World Imagination Reinforces Chain-of-Dynamics Reasoning

author.name: Chaehyun Kim, Chi-Pin Huang, Jisoo Kim, Min-Hung Chen, Yu-Chiang Frank Wang, Seungryong Kim, Fu-En Yang

entry.summary: ThinkWorld is a vision-language-action framework for robotic manipulation that represents action reasoning as a Chain-of-Dynamics, a sequence of discrete motion tokens connecting the current world state to a future one, and strengthens it via reinforcement learning against imagined world dynamics. It leverages human videos to sidestep the scarcity of action-labeled robot demonstrations.

entry.title: The accuracy-safety trade-off of large reasoning models in clinical diagnostics

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: A Nature Communications article examining how large reasoning models trade off diagnostic accuracy against safety in clinical diagnostic settings. No abstract content was supplied, but the title indicates peer-reviewed work quantifying reliability risks of reasoning models in a high-stakes medical domain.

entry.title: Clearing the FoG: Training KG Agents to Retrieve the Evidence Behind Their Answers

author.name: Zongyuan Sun, Shuai Zhao, Yingjun Du, Ke Shu, Ziyue Zhu, Haoran Luo

entry.summary: FoG trains knowledge-graph agents to retrieve supporting evidence triples, not just correct answers, by constructing evidence-aware training data and reward functions that check retrieved evidence rather than only the answer. This makes agent answers traceable and auditable. It addresses a real gap where agents answer correctly without grounding their answers in the graph.

entry.title: Adapting Video Models for Robot Control via Motion-guided Asymmetric Prediction

author.name: Taeyoung Kim, Junyoung Sung, Heeseung Kwon, Minseop Kim, Jinwoo Shin

entry.summary: The paper studies World Action Models, which adapt pretrained video generative models for robot control by predicting future observations and actions, and shows that focusing visual supervision on dynamic regions substantially improves policy performance. It introduces MoGAP, adding motion-focused asymmetric prediction to WAM training. This is an efficient transfer insight for video-to-robot adaptation.

entry.title: Zooming without Zooming v2: From Seeing Details to Connecting Evidence for Generalizable Multimodal Perception

author.name: Lai Wei, Yatai Li, Liangbo He, Jun Lan, Renjie Gu, Linhan Cao, Junkai Lin, Huijia Zhu, Weiqiang Wang, Linghe Kong, Yue Wang, Zhuosheng Zhang, Weiran Huang

entry.summary: The paper identifies connecting evidence — identifying relevant visual facts, binding them to entities, recovering relations, and composing answers — as the shared capability underlying spatial perception and multimodal long-context understanding. It proposes EvidenceConnect, an easy-to-implement data synthesis approach targeting this capability, making training data far cheaper to produce than for the tasks themselves.

entry.title: Where Should the Evaluation Budget Go in LLM-Driven Agent Scaffold Evolution?

author.name: Sichun Luo, Yi Huang, Mukai Li, Haochen Luo, Guanzhi Deng, Haibo Wang, Jian Xu, Zefa Hu, Junlan Feng, Qi Liu

entry.summary: The authors study how to allocate limited evaluation budgets in LLM-driven agent scaffold evolution between guiding ongoing search and selecting the final scaffold. Experiments show sparse feedback can sustain productive evolution while targeted evaluation improves final selection, and replay analyses identify shared informative items and common scoring references as key for comparing close candidates. They propose an evaluation allocation framework based on these findings.

entry.title: Learning Quality-Controllable Robot Policies with Iterative Hindsight Relabeling

author.name: Sinjae Kang, Dong Kyu Shin, Jaehong Kim, Kamin Lee, Hyoeun Kim, Kaixin Wang, Li Zhao, Seonghyeon Ye, Kimin Lee

entry.summary: The paper introduces Quality-Controllable Policies, robot policies that allow inference-time control over quality attributes like execution speed and motion smoothness, not just binary task success. An iterative hindsight relabeling loop collects online rollouts under target quality labels, adds successes to the dataset, and relabels accumulated trajectories to extend the controllable quality range beyond initial demonstrations. This addresses a real gap between benchmark evaluation and deployment requirements.

entry.title: Orthogonal and Parametrized Multi-Attribute Steering of LLMs

author.name: Remy Ogasawara, Cullen Anderson, Narmeen Fatimah Oozeer, Foad Namjoo, Amir Abdullah, Jens Kristian Refsgaard Schou, Jeff M. Phillips

entry.summary: This work improves activation steering of LLMs by identifying the most steerable interval per steering vector and introducing parameterized steering that sets activations to a desired trait strength rather than pushing along a direction. For multi-trait steering, where naively combined vectors interfere, the authors develop an orthogonalization method for consistent, interpretable simultaneous control of multiple attributes.

entry.title: Don't Pick a Winner: Knowledge Conflicts Need a Prior, Not a Rule

author.name: Minh Pham Van, Cong Tran

entry.summary: The paper analyzes how retrieval-augmented language models should resolve conflicts between retrieved context and parametric knowledge, proving that any fixed conflict-resolution rule is dominated in some deployment regimes. Using a decision-theoretic two-source model, it shows fixed rules score linearly in the share of reliable contexts while the best attainable score is convex, and that symmetric divergence between sources carries no information about which source is correct. It argues for prior-based rather than rule-based conflict resolution.

entry.title: How Stable Are LLM-Generated Proofs Under Program Refactoring? A Stress Test for Verifiable Code Generation

author.name: Aravind Mandiga, Guoming Li

entry.summary: RefactorProof tests whether Lean-certified proofs remain valid when the underlying program is refactored while behavior, specification, and proof stay fixed, deriving 458 Lean variants from 185 compiling VERINA tasks. It finds substantial brittleness: task-normalized structural proof-success-rate is only 4.3% for supplied reference proofs and 13.3-26.8% for model-specialized proofs. This exposes that verifiable-code benchmarks overstate robustness by testing against a single fixed implementation.

entry.title: When to Intervene? An Empirical Study of Errors and Self-Recovery in LLM Agents

author.name: Chiming Duan, Tong Jia, Yingxi Chen, Minghua He, Lingzhe Zhang, Ying Li

entry.summary: This empirical study builds ReInBench, a dataset of 1,259 agent traces and 1,403 error events across computer-use and web tasks, to understand when LLM agents self-recover from errors versus need external intervention. It examines how often and how quickly self-recovery occurs, its relationship to task completion, and whether recovery can be predicted at error time. The results inform practical guardrail design for agent systems.

entry.title: GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latents as a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents

author.name: Bingchao Wang, Yongcheng Jing, Shunyu Liu, Chengyu Wang, Jun Huang, Jie Yang, Wei Liu, Dacheng Tao

entry.summary: GUI-JEPA is claimed to be the first decoder-free GUI agent policy built on a Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture, pretrained on unlabeled GUI screenshots. It scores all candidate actions via lightweight heads over candidate-conditioned latents, avoiding slow token-by-token decoding of 7B-scale VLM policies, thus yielding a faster and more memory-efficient mobile GUI agent.

entry.title: GraphRAGProv: GraphRAG Meets How-Provenance

author.name: Wadie El Amrani, Luis Gal\'arraga

entry.summary: GraphRAGProv is an architecture that runs SPARQL queries over source-grounded RDF graphs to compute answers together with how-provenance polynomials, which record which statement occurrences were used and how they were combined. Because each occurrence links back to source text, users can audit whether extraction and query logic justify the answer. This brings much-needed transparency to GraphRAG systems in domains where explainability is essential.

entry.title: Concordat: Typed Sessions for LLM Agents

author.name: Milad Sikaroudi

entry.summary: Concordat is a Python library that treats an LLM agent as an object whose interface is a finite-state protocol in the spirit of typestate and session types, enforcing the protocol at runtime. Each turn exposes only tools legal in the current state, and out-of-protocol calls are rejected before side effects occur. This converts prompt-stated behavioral rules into hard, machine-enforced guarantees for consequential actions like refunds and account changes.

entry.title: UnityBench-Mini3D: Evaluating LLM Agents for 3D Game Development in Unity

author.name: Yijun Zhou, Minghao Shao, Ke Zhang, Renkai Yuan, Hongbo Yuan, Bin Hu, Bozhao Qian, Hongxia Shen, Yanhong Liu, Yuting Chen, Yuntao Shi, Zhongxuan Xu, Shuo Mao, Haijia Zhou, Zhendong Li, Tao Zhang, Chenggang Li, Yuxuan Wang, Zinan Zheng, Calvin Zhang, Jia Li, Heng Chang, Jie Feng

entry.summary: UnityBench-Mini3D is a benchmark of 77 project-level Unity game development tasks across seven expert-defined skill categories and three difficulty tiers, evaluated with 1,178 held-out human-authored milestone tests covering scene structure, component configuration, and runtime behavior. It targets a gap left by Godot-focused benchmarks that rely on LLM judges or coarse outcomes.

entry.title: BUSTA: Teaching Small Language Models to Reason About Binary Execution

author.name: Ritika Poddar, Aidan Fennelly, Deirdre Murphy, Eric Wolos, Corre L. Steele, Michael Doyle

entry.summary: This NVIDIA-affiliated work trains small open models (Qwen3-1.7B and Nemotron-3-Nano) to reason about low-level x86-64 program behavior via inverse basic-block execution, fine-tuned with GRPO to predict input register values from output states. The goal is to transfer reverse-engineering skills to resource-constrained sandboxed environments where frontier models are impractical. It demonstrates targeted RL fine-tuning for a specialized security workflow.

entry.title: RoboAuto: Autonomous Robot Program Search through Multi-Level Physical Understanding

author.name: Buzhao Liu, Jianing Ye, Xiu Yuan, Yangtong Feng, Chengsong Huang, Tyler Dinh, Yevgeniy Vorobeychik, Ning Zhang, Chongjie Zhang

entry.summary: RoboAuto is a framework for LLM-driven robot program search that explicitly organizes physical understanding at the object, scene, and interaction levels, rather than relying solely on execution feedback for refinement. By answering how objects can be manipulated and why interactions fail, the agent can more effectively search over modular, editable robot programs. This targets a key gap in Code-as-Policy style approaches to manipulation.

entry.title: Look Only When Needed: Certificate-Guided Visual Routing for Efficient Diffusion VLMs

author.name: Donghyeon Cho, Joowon Kim, Seungho Shin, Eunho Yang

entry.summary: The paper observes that in diffusion vision-language models like LLaDA-V, visual tokens are 89-97% of input yet the image changes predictions at only about 22.8% of decoding steps (as few as 7.9%), motivating LOWN, a decoding method with certificate-guided routing that consults the image only when needed. This substantially cuts redundant visual computation during diffusion decoding. It preserves information that token pruning would discard.

entry.title: SetGRPO: Calibrating Grader-Induced Policy Optimization

author.name: Jiale Huang, Zixu Li, Zhiwei Chen, Zhiheng Fu, Jinhe Bi, Yupeng Hu

entry.summary: The paper analyzes how grader randomness in rubric-based RL distorts GRPO updates, since score discrepancies shift coefficients across entire response groups and can reverse update directions. SetGRPO introduces set-valued reward calibration to handle grader-induced uncertainty in policy optimization for open-ended LLM tasks.

entry.title: Beyond Parameter Protection: Fisher-Shaped EWC for Replay-Free Continual Learning

author.name: Liying Wang, Simone Magistri, Joost van de Weijer

entry.summary: FS-EWC extends Elastic Weight Consolidation by shifting the Fisher information matrix from protecting past parameters to shaping where future solutions form. It minimizes worst-case empirical Fisher trace within a neighborhood of potential updates during task learning, favoring solutions less sensitive to bounded future parameter changes. This addresses the known limitation that local importance estimates fail after finite displacement.

entry.title: Channel Selection for Mixture-of-Experts Decoding Needs No Calibration Data

author.name: Geunhyoung Kim, Sung Ju Hwang

entry.summary: The paper shows that channel selection for MoE expert-weight loading can work without calibration data. The authors demonstrate that calibrated thresholds fail to control actual read budgets, that top-k selection offers better control, and they derive a statistic for per-input budget calibration. This removes an offline data dependency and improves the predictability of memory savings during interactive decoding.

entry.title: The Structure Gap: When More Data Cannot Replace Structured Reasoning

author.name: Kheer Sagar Patel, Mojtaba Soltanalian

entry.summary: The paper formalizes structure-encoded problems, tasks whose input-output maps are sharply constrained by known structure such as solvers, symmetries, or physical laws, and defines the structure gap: the finite-resource gap between learners that exploit the governing structure and those that must learn it from data. It argues that for such tasks the issue is not expressivity but finite-data identification, extrapolation, and certification.

entry.title: kw-bench: Breaking Frontier Harnesses on Real-World Tasks

author.name: George Juraj Salapa

entry.summary: kw-bench is a benchmark targeting the investigative side of knowledge work performed by coding-agent harnesses, such as audit, tax, due diligence, and regulatory reporting, where the answer already exists hidden in incomplete and inconsistent evidence. It complements generative benchmarks (build a model from a brief) by testing whether frontier harnesses can find and verify ground truth in messy real-world materials. The benchmark stresses harness infrastructure rather than pure coding.

entry.title: God Does Not Play Dice: Enforcing Batch Invariance in Agentic Kernel Generation

author.name: Youwei Bao, Chengpeng Wang, Simin Chen

entry.summary: This paper shows that GPU kernels generated by LLM agents frequently lack batch invariance, meaning numerical outputs change depending on which other requests share the batch, undermining reproducibility in dynamically batched serving. The authors found 19 confirmed violations among 83 released batch-applicable artifacts and propose a plug-in combining contract-guided static dependency analysis with dynamic bitwise-consistency validation. This is a concrete reliability contribution for LLM serving systems.

entry.title: SCOPE: Source Credibility and Outlet Profiling Engine

author.name: Ilyas Nagiyev, Miras Baisbay, Daniil Orel, Preslav Nakov

entry.summary: SCOPE is a multi-agent system that profiles news outlets for bias, factuality, and credibility using coordinated agents for article acquisition, analysis, external evidence search, and scoring. On a 200-outlet benchmark it beats LLM-only, article-only, and search-only baselines, with inspectable intermediate evidence following an MBFC-style methodology.

entry.title: Beyond the Estimate: Wiener-Informed Decoding for Easier Training of Pixel-Space Flow Models

author.name: Ziqiao Wang, Yang You

entry.summary: This paper shows that training velocity fields for flow models directly in pixel space becomes easier when frozen Wiener estimates of coarse second-order image statistics are used. Wiener-informed Decoding (WiD) combines a trainable Wiener prediction path with coefficient interfaces that inject features into the native decoder without modifying its blocks. This offers a practical path toward more efficient pixel-space generative modeling.

entry.title: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Behaviorally Adequate Test Generation from Software Requirements

author.name: Binhang Qi, Yiming Liu, Yun Lin, Yangjie Zhou, Hailong Sun, Jin Song Dong

entry.summary: Req2Test-Bench is a benchmark of 5,086 execution-validated instances from developer-authored behavior-driven development artifacts, evaluating whether LLM agents can generate tests that validate required behavior when the implementation is withheld. It shifts test-generation evaluation from white-box settings to requirement-to-test semantic alignment. Results gauge whether agents can supply validation constraints to guide repository-level code generation.

entry.title: Aligning Large Language Models for Safety in African Languages: A Case Study of Hausa

author.name: Valdini Douglace Lemofouet, Blessing Ngozi Uzor, Paula Chikaodinaka Anyanwu, Danielle Blanche Kapsa, Saminu Mohammad Aliyu, Seid Muhie Yimam, Shamsuddeen Hassan Muhammad

entry.summary: The paper introduces HausaSafeLM, one of the first Hausa safety preference datasets, with 10,000 prompts across six harm categories split into human-corrected gold and machine-translated silver subsets. Using Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, the authors compare SFT and SFT-plus-DPO under both regimes on harmful and benign Hausa prompts. It addresses the scarcity of safety alignment research for low-resource, culturally distinct languages spoken by over 200 million people.

entry.title: Representing the Unseen: Rethinking Visual Imagination for Spatial Reasoning

author.name: Zengqi Zhao, Zun Wang, Shoubin Yu, Mohit Bansal, Yue Zhang

entry.summary: This work questions the default use of RGB images as the interface for visual world models doing spatial reasoning, arguing that different spatial questions benefit from different imagined representations such as top-down geometry or panoramic views. It introduces ImagiRep, a simulator-grounded benchmark of 922 questions across seven question types in Viewpoint Imagination and Cross-view settings.

entry.title: Skill Dreaming: Evolving Repository Skills through Pull Request Streams

author.name: Xinyuan Song, Hasibul Haque, Jay Somasundaram, Ryan Turner, Bowen Zhu, Liang Zhao

entry.summary: This work proposes a system where LLM agent skill libraries continuously evolve by mining pull request streams, which naturally record how repositories change through implementation and review. It establishes a mutually reinforcing cycle in which PRs provide knowledge for updating repository-specific skills, while new PRs must follow repo conventions, modify related components consistently, and pass existing tests. The approach targets the gap that agent skills go stale as codebases evolve.

entry.title: ADTGuard: Adaptive Depth-Time Safeguard for Streaming Inference in Large Language Models

author.name: Chuming Wei, Churui Yang, Zihan Zhang, Ruien Li, Wusheng Zhang, Yan Zhang, Guangwen Yang

entry.summary: ADTGuard addresses the problem that streaming LLM generation can expose users to harmful content before moderation completes. The method checks each token before release, progressively refines token-level training targets, and adapts which model layers are read out to capture safety signals at different depths. This reduces harmful exposure relative to post-hoc or chunk-boundary moderation.

entry.title: Prospector: learning a compact graph traversal policy for scientific reasoning

author.name: Haiqian Yang, Markus J. Buehler

entry.summary: Prospector is a compact trained model that reasons over domain knowledge graphs by traversing them step by step with a small tool set, progressively building context and producing evidence chains that can be verified edge by edge against the graph. It targets specialized scientific domains where proprietary knowledge is absent from frontier LLM training data and preselecting a subgraph before reasoning fails.

entry.title: CIVER: Causal Intervention Verification for Reliable Code Review

author.name: Xinyuan Song, Hasibul Haque, Jay Somasundaram, Ryan Turner, Bowen Zhu, Liang Zhao

entry.summary: CIVER addresses false positives in LLM-based code review agents by using causal intervention-based verification to distinguish actionable findings from unsupported claims. As coding agents generate more contributions and review agents become prevalent, filtering unreliable reviews matters for both developers and downstream automated agents.

entry.title: Detecting and Mitigating Query-Based System Prompt Leakage Attacks

author.name: Tushar Nayan, Pratik Poudel, Qian Lou, Yuede Ji, Jason Liu, Ruimin Sun

entry.summary: AdvGuard is a model-agnostic framework for detecting and mitigating query-based system prompt leakage attacks, where black-box adversaries extract confidential instructions over adaptive multi-turn interactions. It models cross-query relationships via a bounded semantic interaction graph, statistically filters candidate components, and uses graph convolutions on line graphs for classification. This addresses a real security gap since prior defenses evaluate queries independently.

entry.title: Less is more: learning what to profile for GPU kernel optimization

author.name: Yihan Wang, Peiyu Liu, Runyu Chen, Wei Xu

entry.summary: This paper shows that in LLM-based GPU kernel optimization, collecting more profiling metrics does not monotonically improve results, and the most useful profiling information varies per kernel. It provides theoretical analysis showing kernel-conditioned profiling selection can outperform any fixed strategy, and learns what to profile. This improves the efficiency of an increasingly automated systems workflow.

entry.title: Specialization, Diversity, and Scaling in Child-Scale Language Models

author.name: Steven Y. Feng, Michael C. Frank

entry.summary: The study trains small GPT-2 models on naturalistic child-directed speech from dense home recordings (BabyView) and synthetic dialogue (TinyDialogues), examining how data amount, source, and diversity affect learning at child scale. It finds strong per-child specialization that is largely lexical (a 5-gram model reproduces the pattern), and that training across multiple children improves pooled held-out prediction. This informs the data-efficiency and cognitive-science debate on how children learn language.

entry.title: V-LUMEN: Visual Lookup Memory for Embedding Scaling in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Miso Choi, Daekeun Kim, Eunji Kim, Jungbeom Lee

entry.summary: V-LUMEN extends embedding-level scaling via lookup memory to vision-language models, which is hard because visual features are continuous, spatially structured, and query-dependent. It discretizes visual features with a frozen codebook, builds spatially aware keys via hashing, modulates with text-conditioned relevance, and fuses retrieved embeddings through a gated residual path.

entry.title: When Is a Relation Worth Trusting? Manipulation Costs, Exposure, and the Trust Trap in Multi-Relational Graph Learning

author.name: Vincess Dongmo, Astride Melvin Fokam Ninyim

entry.summary: This paper analyzes when using a relation in multi-relational graph learning is worse than ignoring it, given that an adversary pays different costs to manipulate different relations. It proves degree gating strictly beats any selection or reweighting when part of the population is isolated on a relation the attacker cannot afford to open, and derives per-node exposure bounds indicating which relation a platform should harden. Theory is validated on real graphs.

entry.title: GAS-PFN: Graph-Aware Spatiotemporal Prior-Data Fitted Networks for Zero-Shot Traffic Forecasting

author.name: Joseph Natter, Long Vu, Yifan Zhang, Bobin Deng, Kun Suo, Rui Wu

entry.summary: GAS-PFN extends Prior-Data Fitted Networks to traffic forecasting by encoding road-topology graph dependencies in synthetic task priors, enabling zero-shot forecasting on new or evolving sensor networks without per-dataset training. This combines graph-aware spatiotemporal modeling with in-context learning from synthetic priors, addressing the costly retraining of supervised graph models.

entry.title: BehaveRec: When Does Long-Term Behavioral History Help Sequential Recommendation? A Study with Session, History, and Community Signals

author.name: Aysenur Inan, Reza Yousefi Maragheh, Jayesh Uddhav Kudase, Selene Xu, Kaushiki Nag, Jianpeng Xu, Sushant Kumar

entry.summary: BehaveRec is a three-signal recommendation framework combining a causal session transformer, a bidirectional user-history encoder over 90 days, and a GraphSAGE module over a user graph built from behavioral-embedding similarity, blended per user by a learned gate. Uniquely, it asks when long-term history and community signals help rather than assuming they always do. On an industrial dataset of 137M sequences from 12.6M users it improves R@5 by +3.2% over SASRec.

entry.title: RouteDRAG: Learning to Route and Control Agentic Execution for Multimodal Document RAG

author.name: Zekai Chen, Hao Zhu, Yu Liu, Xunkai Li, Zejian Kang, Rui Qian, Quanjiang Li, Rong-Hua Li

entry.summary: RouteDRAG is a learning-based framework that decides when agentic execution is warranted for multimodal document RAG and how to control that execution, since iterative retrieval is not always beneficial and can even degrade accuracy. The work is motivated by an empirical analysis showing query-dependent benefits of agentic execution. It addresses a practical efficiency-accuracy tradeoff for web applications processing long multimodal documents.

entry.title: Beyond the Evidence Coherence Trap: Agent-Driven Evidence Selection for Temporally Disordered Fake News Detection

author.name: Chi Wang, Min Gao, Yifei Zhang, Bincheng Gu, Zongwei Wang, Wentao Li

entry.summary: This paper identifies the evidence coherence trap in fake news detection, where temporally rearranged articles are validated by locally coherent but mismatched evidence retrieved from similar past events. It introduces ChronoFake, a source-disjoint benchmark of 30,706 articles isolating this setting, and proposes agent-driven evidence selection to check temporal consistency. This addresses an elusive class of misinformation where individual events are factually valid but the chronology is false.

entry.title: When the Critic Falls Behind: Co-Evolving Rubrics and Harnesses for Continual Agent Self-Improvement

author.name: Hao Chen, Yukun Yan, Ziyu Han, Ye He, Chuanzhe Guo, Shangzhan Li, Qi Shi, Qingfu Zhu, Maosong Sun, Wanxiang Che

entry.summary: RuHarness is a framework in which evaluation rubrics co-evolve with agent harnesses, continually discovering and reassessing behavioral criteria from execution trajectories to guide targeted harness updates. This addresses the problem that static supervision cannot track shifting behavioral weaknesses across rounds of agent self-improvement.

entry.title: LiveSearch: Questions as Executable Verifier Code for a Live Benchmark of Professional-Source Financial Search Agents

author.name: Sinuo Wang, Wentao Zhao, Jiacheng Lu, Rui Sun, Beidi Luan, Qiming Shi, Jing Li, Daxin Jiang, Zuo Bai

entry.summary: LiveSearch is a live benchmark for financial search agents in which each question is stored as executable verifier code over a professional financial data service, so the gold answer is computed at evaluation time rather than frozen at annotation time. This prevents answer staleness and data leakage, rewarding genuine search and analysis over memorized recall.

entry.title: Layerwise Repacking: Variable-Length Hybrid-Attention Training without an Extra Redistribution Pass

author.name: Jiahao Zhang, Junwei Feng, Dongliang Huang, Xiaoling Zhou, Yiqiao Liao, Chengru Song

entry.summary: The paper addresses conflicting sequence-parallel group requirements across full-attention and sparse-attention layers in hybrid-attention training, where reusing wide SP16/32 groups for sparse layers incurs 7.0x slower cross-node communication. Layerwise Repacking keeps groups fixed while repacking per layer, avoiding a separate redistribution pass at full-sparse boundaries.

entry.title: When Connectivity Misleads: Guiding Agentic Search with Contrastive Evidence Paths

author.name: Junchen Li, Liang Xu, Rongzheng Wang, Qizhi Chen, Junhao Wen, Shuang Liang

entry.summary: This paper addresses a failure mode in search agents using cross-document graphs: highly connected distractor documents crowd out valuable evidence under graph-diffusion methods like Personalized PageRank. The proposed Contrastive Evidence Paths (CEP) scores candidates by their strongest individual evidence path rather than aggregate connectivity. This improves agentic search quality in multi-hop retrieval settings.

entry.title: REACH: An RL-based Hierarchical Humanoid Crawling Framework for Adaptable Confined Space Traversal

author.name: Shengzhang Xu, Yuning Guo, Weiyi Hu, Yifeng Xu, Zhongyu Li, He Kong

entry.summary: REACH is an RL-based hierarchical framework enabling a Unitree G1 humanoid to traverse height-constrained environments using both variable-height bipedal walking (1.27-0.50m) and crawling (0.50-0.20m). It uses a history-conditioned latent representation built from proprioception to handle contact-rich crawling dynamics. This extends humanoid locomotion beyond height-adjustable walking into genuinely confined spaces.

entry.title: Self-Keyed In-Parameter Memorization for External Memory-Free Dialogue Recall in Frozen Language Models

author.name: XinYu Piao, Myunghoon Ryu, Joongheon Kim, Jong-Kook Kim

entry.summary: SKIM explores storing dialogue directly in a frozen language model's parameters without external memory: the model generates its own questions about each turn and writes question-keyed associations into its parameters via closed-form updates, enabling later retrieval by matching user questions. This tests whether conversation can be recalled purely in-parameter.

entry.title: AnalogScout: Simulation-Efficient PVT-Aware Analog Sizing with LLM Agents

author.name: Yichen Long, Keren Zhu

entry.summary: AnalogScout is an LLM-agent framework for analog circuit sizing that satisfies specifications across process, voltage, and temperature corners while minimizing expensive multi-corner SPICE simulations. It equips the agent with reusable verified designs and analytical sizing of sub-blocks to save simulation budget, combining circuit knowledge with search efficiency. This targets a real bottleneck in tape-out-ready analog design automation.

entry.title: Autonomous fixed-wing interception using reinforcement learning

author.name: Daan van Hamersveld, Ewoud Smeur, Iurii Kriachko

entry.summary: The paper presents an RL-controlled fixed-wing interceptor drone aimed at autonomously engaging Shahed-type strike drones at higher altitudes and longer ranges than quadcopter interceptors can reach. The neural network controller maps filtered monocular vision inputs to control, addressing a capability gap where conventional air defense is too costly and manual operation remains standard.

entry.title: Counting the Bandages: On measuring the time that AI saves

author.name: Solomon Shalom Lijo

entry.summary: This position paper argues that measuring AI-assisted time savings with a stopwatch alone is misleading; time saved must be weighed against escaped defects the work lets through. It defines model-free quantities (time saved, excess escaped defects) and a break-even defect cost, and models checking behavior showing escaped-defect rates are largely independent of model quality until workers stop checking. It reframes AI productivity measurement as a counterfactual accounting problem rather than a raw speed metric.

entry.title: WAKMan: Workload Aware KVCache Manager

author.name: Suhas Kumar Morisetty, Vaibhavi Lokegaonkar, Sachin Mathew Varghese, Wesley Harris

entry.summary: WAKMan is a workload-aware KV cache eviction policy for LLM servers doing prefix caching, motivated by the finding that agentic steps return within seconds and favor recency while popular prompts and long conversations favor frequency. Across 20 request mixes the authors show no single policy is always best, with vLLM's default LRU suboptimal for mixed traffic. The system adapts eviction to observed workload composition to reduce latency and serving cost.

entry.title: AC-JEPA: Anchored Cross-Modal Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture for Visual-to-Symbolic Translation

author.name: Chaofei Hong, Ziyang Chen, Baochen Wang, Christina Yi Jin, Qing Zhang

entry.summary: AC-JEPA extends joint-embedding predictive architectures to cross-modal translation, using an SFT-compatible plug-in that predicts masked intermediate states in representation space to complement token-level supervision. This targets scientific domains where paired data are imperfect and clean pairs are costly, since token-level objectives are sensitive to target-sequence errors. The approach aims to capture shared semantics while preserving fine-grained target-modality structure.

entry.title: The View from Nowhere: Population-Centered Agent Evolution

author.name: Shuo Yan, Ningning Hou, Haoyu He, Haochen Pei, Shang Gao

entry.summary: This paper observes that self-improving agent evolution centered on selected parent agents leaves broader population capabilities underused, showing a substantial gap between population coverage and best-individual performance. It proposes a population-wide principle, the view from nowhere, where agents improve by interpreting their behavior through population-wide patterns of success, failure, and priors. This is relevant to open-ended agent self-improvement methods.

entry.title: Correctness Conditioning as Selection in Chain-of-Thought Faithfulness Evaluation

author.name: Yueer Pan, Yuexi Pan

entry.summary: The paper shows that restricting chain-of-thought faithfulness evaluation to correctly answered instances changes the measured population, formalizing this selection effect in a seven-variable structural causal model that separates difficulty confounding from shortcut-induced collider bias. A review of 18 papers plus experiments on arithmetic tasks reveals positive selection gaps across four sub-ceiling deployments.

entry.title: Aligning Institutional Power and Operational Ability

author.name: Andrea Marino, Giovanni Sileno, Thomas van Binsbergen, Tom van Engers

entry.summary: This paper proposes a formal framework for designing multi-agent AI systems in which norms and responsibilities are aligned with the actual operational ability to fulfil them. It uses process-oriented modelling and the concept of institutional power to detect incongruences such as unsatisfiable expectations or privilege escalation, and discusses repair strategies and the lifecycle of normative positions.

entry.title: From Interaction to Capability: Task Advancement as State and Supervision for GUI Agents

author.name: Ziyang Chen, Qian Li, Chengwei Qin

entry.summary: Task Advancement Memory (TAM) defines verified task progress as a state that reshapes remaining goals during long-horizon GUI workflows and, after each task, abstracts the interactions that produced verified results into reusable operations. This lets agents build on earlier achievements across applications while filtering out failed attempts. It targets the key problem of durable, reusable memory for GUI agents.

entry.title: What Improves During Pretraining? Tracking Knowledge Acquisition with Point-in-Time Models

author.name: Chang Su, Bin Wu, Emine Yilmaz, Yao Lu

entry.summary: Using point-in-time language models trained on web snapshots from different years, the authors propose a temporal variability score based on the coefficient of variation of an item's negative log-likelihood across models, probing how general versus domain-specific knowledge accumulates during pretraining. Evaluating six benchmarks across six open-source model families, they characterize how consistently knowledge is represented across years of web text. This offers a novel longitudinal lens on pretraining dynamics.

entry.title: EMMA: Structured Episodic Memory for Multi-Agent Workflow Synthesis

author.name: Ruijia Niu, Kaiwen Liu, Rose Yu, Kristina Klinkner

entry.summary: EMMA addresses adaptation of LLM agents to specialized domains via structured episodic memory at the context level, using multi-agent evolution with explicit update rules to reduce cross-task interference. It targets limitations of single-agent episodic memory and ill-scoped multi-agent evolution where backbone model preferences dictate system changes.

entry.title: DuplexTune: Coupled-State Replay for Memory-Efficient Mixture-of-Experts Adaptation

author.name: Paul Raj, Simon Caldwell, Daniel Whitmore, Mutlu Mete

entry.summary: DuplexTune is a memory-efficient framework for adapting mixture-of-experts LLMs that replays coupled hidden states through pretrained attention and expert modules via trainable width bridges between two residual streams. On Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B with a single H800, it reports 38.8 GB peak memory versus 64.8 GB for SFT with checkpointing, higher throughput, and solid task scores (67.2% MMLU, 75.6% GSM8K).

entry.title: count-catcher: Lean Theorems from Model Counting Certificates

author.name: Johannes K. Fichte, Stefan Szeider

entry.summary: count-catcher is a tool that converts CPOG certificates produced by the exact model counter d4 into verified Lean theorems stating that a CNF formula has exactly N models over given variables, enabling verified counting of combinatorial objects. It performs forward and reverse checks in Lean, streaming a refutation through the standard LRAT checker and proving circuit validity within Lean. This contributes to the growing intersection of formal verification and combinatorial reasoning.

entry.title: HIDRA: Hierarchical Dual-Routing Attention for Replay-Free Lifelong Imitation Learning

author.name: Fanqi Yu, Matteo Tiezzi, Cigdem Beyan, Tommaso Apicella, Vittorio Murino

entry.summary: HIDRA is a structured routing framework for replay-free, single-pass lifelong imitation learning that decouples instruction-level expert retrieval from context-dependent refinement via hierarchical dual attention. It further stabilizes routing under representation drift using a key-based mechanism, addressing how expert selection degrades over sequential multimodal demonstration streams. This targets realistic robotic settings where storing past data is prohibited.

entry.title: Full Collapse Is Suboptimal: Controlled Partial Neural Collapse for Long-Tailed Recognition

author.name: Hyeontaek Hwang, Cheonghwan Hur, Daeyoung Kim

entry.summary: The paper argues that forcing tail classes to fully undergo neural collapse toward an ETF target over-contracts their features and harms generalization in long-tailed recognition. It proposes a controlled partial collapse regime via a Class-Adaptive Sparse Activation classifier and an ETF-constrained adaptive margin loss, letting head classes collapse while tail classes keep within-class diversity. This offers a more nuanced theoretical account of neural collapse under imbalance.

entry.title: PailitaoMMSearch2.0 Technical Report: Scaling Generative Retrieval to Unified End-to-End Multimodal Search

author.name: Xiaohan Ye, Zihan Gong, Jingqian Zhao, Lianyu Du, Yunmeng Shu, Xu Chen, Zesheng Zhou, Renchun You, Bocheng Chen, Jinsong Lan, Haihong Tang, Bo Zheng

entry.summary: This industrial technical report from Alibaba presents PailitaoMMSearch, a unified end-to-end multimodal search system that generates product semantic IDs directly from raw query images and free-form instructions, scaling across data, model, and serving dimensions. It removes scenario-specific couplings common in industrial generative retrieval deployments.

entry.title: Generative Replay for Equilibrium Propagation: Toward Edge-Friendly Continual Learning in Hopfield Networks

author.name: Victor Cook (LIRMM | ADAC), Gilles Sassatelli (LIRMM | ADAC), Thierry Gil (LIRMM), Mohamed Watfa (LIRMM | ADAC), Marina Reyboz (CEA-LETI)

entry.summary: The paper tackles catastrophic forgetting in equilibrium-propagation-trained Hopfield networks using an energy-based generative replay scheme where a single model serves as both classifier and sample generator. This eliminates external data buffers and architectural overhead required by standard experience replay, suiting edge hardware. It opens a largely unexplored continual-learning setting for biologically grounded learning rules.

entry.title: Kinematic Constraint-Referenced Evaluation for Articulated Object Manipulation

author.name: Baptiste Bonin, Caro Strickland, Audrey Durand

entry.summary: The paper proposes Constraint-Referenced Strategy (CRS), an evaluation metric for articulated object manipulation that projects commanded end-effector twist onto the object's joint axis, separating progress along the joint from off-constraint waste instead of relying on binary task success. On 74 simulated articulated objects, CRS exposes distinct signatures of transfer failures that binary success conflates, demonstrated with a door-trained policy opening drawers.

entry.title: Beyond Answer Changes: Matched Same-Class Controls for Local Audio Evidence

author.name: Yunuo Wang, Maoyuan Chen, Yuanjin Huang, Xing Liu

entry.summary: This paper introduces matched same-class replacement controls to test whether audio-language models genuinely use local sound events: same-class edits preserve correct answers while different-class edits should change them if evidence is used. Across 600 synthetic soundscapes and three models from two architecture families, different-class replacements trigger 49.7 to 60.9 points more answer changes, providing a more rigorous causal attribution method for audio grounding.

entry.title: Smaller NLAs and probes read eval awareness as well as full size NLAs

author.name: Adam Bricknell

entry.summary: The author distills a Natural Language Autoencoder (NLA) reader trained on Qwen3.6-27B internals down to a 2B model, finding the distilled 2B NLA matches the 27B version at detecting agentic misalignment and eval-awareness signals (though not obscure facts), and that a cheap linear probe on 2B-generated labels matches a 27B NLA plus LLM judge on eval awareness at a tiny fraction of the cost. Results come from 76 technical tasks with injected cues, and generalization is not yet established.

entry.title: Generalized CliqueBots in Open-Source Game Theory

author.name: Arsen

entry.summary: This LessWrong post introduces an interface-relative notion of CliqueBots in open-source game theory, where programs cooperate only with similar programs as judged by a finite set of probing functions. The framework treats submitted programs as secondary to their interfaces, unifying existing bots in a coherent picture and providing a generative factory for new bot designs, with potential to characterize interface properties via bot properties.

entry.title: From Structural Feedback to Prompt Policies: Learning Faithful Text-to-Image Prompt Editors

author.name: Wentao Ye, Yali Ye, Zhiqing Xiao, Ru Peng, Xinpeng Ti, Liyao Li, Zhanming Shen, Peng Lu, Jie Zhang, Haobo Wang

entry.summary: StruPO is a structure-aware prompt editor for text-to-image systems that uses a calibrated scene graph as a shared representation for policy conditioning and image-grounded supervision, ensuring prompt edits preserve the user's requested scene. Deletion, reordering, and insertion operations provide token-aligned prompt modification, turning structural critique into a training signal for a reusable editing policy. The method must handle uncertain grounding and stochastic image generation during learning.

entry.title: LoRA on a Budget: Function-Aware Post-Hoc Compression for Adapter Fleets

author.name: Shenghui Li, Thiemo voigt

entry.summary: The paper formulates post-hoc LoRA compression as a two-level allocation problem: distributing rank across layers within each adapter and across adapters within a fleet under a shared budget. It introduces functional rank-distortion frontiers per adapter and fleet-level minimax allocation, arguing spectral redundancy alone does not determine tolerable compression. Given exact frontiers, the decomposition is shown to have desirable optimality properties.

entry.title: Remembering Is Not Enough: Refining Memories and Learning When to Use Them in Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Yipeng Hao, Yuxuan Cai, Wenkai Ji, Jie Zhou, Liyang Yu, Qin Chen, Zhiguo Yan, Shulei Zheng, Liang He

entry.summary: DiscernMem is a training-free framework improving both memory quality and memory usage in LLM multi-agent systems. Defect-Aware Memory Refinement diagnoses flaws in stored advice by comparing executions with and without a memory and validates repairs against earlier tasks, while Boundary-Learning Meta-Memory records past uses and effects to learn when each memory should be applied or avoided. This addresses the real problem that stored memories can be wrong or misapplied.

entry.title: Vision-Language Agents Can Learn in Their Own Latent Worlds

author.name: Haoxi Li, Sikai Bai, Jianfei Ma, Qinglin Hou, Xiaocheng Lu, Tao Han, Jie Zhang, Song Guo

entry.summary: The paper introduces Dwell, a model-based RL framework that recasts a pretrained vision-language model as a recurrent latent transition operator able to predict the consequences of its actions in latent space. This enables learning from online interaction while avoiding expensive continual updates of large pretrained models, leveraging internalized world knowledge for policy improvement.

entry.title: Rare, Relevant, and Still Wrong: How Memory Fails LLM Group Decisions

author.name: Anouar Imel, Imad Charradi, Abderrahman Sghir, Khalil El Khammar

entry.summary: CrossProfile is a diagnostic benchmark of 60 templates (480 tasks) crossing the ownership of supporting, decoy, and irrelevant facts while holding text fixed, designed to test what LLM group-discussion memory should retain. Across Qwen2.5, Llama-3.1, and DeepSeek models, both natural heuristics (keep rarest claims, keep relevant claims) fail predictably: rarity selection is confounded and relevance selection readmits on-topic decoys. The work isolates a subtle failure mode in compressed group memory.

entry.title: Generation and Verification: Human-Agent Collaboration for Safety-Critical Automotive Software Engineering

author.name: Elizaveta Zinovyeva, Aiham Taleb, Nikita Kozodoi, Daniel Schleicher, Amir Mahdi Namazi, Martin Kraus, Levent Kent, Brian Jensen

entry.summary: The paper presents a coding assistant for safety-critical automotive C/C++ that exposes generate, edit, and verify tools to developers via the Model Context Protocol, emphasizing verification against standards like MISRA and AUTOSAR. It addresses the narrow-domain challenge of layered architectures and embedded constraints underrepresented in general LLM training data.

entry.title: How Much Does the Hint Matter? Scope Conditions for Hindsight Self-Distillation in Financial Reasoning

author.name: Johnny Yu, Cyril Gorlla

entry.summary: The paper presents Fin-SD, a localized hindsight self-distillation recipe in which the student itself identifies and critiques its first incorrect reasoning step and training resumes from a truncated trajectory, reducing the dependence of on-policy distillation on a strong external teacher or full reference solutions. It targets multi-step financial reasoning under data-residency constraints favoring small open-weight models.

entry.title: Balanced State Subspaces for Mamba-2 State Compression

author.name: Shang Tingyu, Cao Wenfei

entry.summary: The paper analyzes trained Mamba-2 states and finds that while energy is nearly rank-one, the output actually reads content from a low-dimensional subspace misaligned with the state's coordinates, meaning coordinate-wise compression scores miss the directions that matter. It proposes compression targeting the write-read subspace with balanced state subspaces. This improves memory and bandwidth efficiency for Mamba-2 decoding.

entry.title: CoS-VQ: Coordinated Shared-Scale Vector Quantization for Large Language Models

author.name: Zukang Xu, Zhixiong Zhao, Xing Hu, Zhe Jiang, Xin Si, Dawei Yang

entry.summary: CoS-VQ is a vector quantization method for low-bit LLM weight compression that preserves low-dimensional codewords while jointly optimizing hard indices and a shared scale across positions.
